articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband Beam-Scanning Leakage Antenna Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To address the issues of low operating frequency and narrow beam scanning range in leakage antennas, this paper proposes a millimeter-wave fixed-frequency beam scanning leakage antenna based on liquid crystal metamaterial (LCM). This antenna uses a periodic arrangement of 48 Split Ring Resonators (SRRs) to couple TEM mode electromagnetic waves into free space. The LC layer is encapsulated in the transmission medium between the microstrip line and the metal ground plane. By applying a bias voltage to the microstrip line, a voltage difference is created between it and the metal ground plane, allowing control over the orientation of the LC molecules. Simulation results show that the antenna operates in the Q-band and achieves continuous beam scanning from -42° to 60° at 48.5 GHz, covering a total range of 102°. Given that the resonance of the antenna unit has a broadband characteristic., further experiments indicate that the antenna array has a wideband adaptability, enabling continuous beam scanning over a wide frequency range from 48.3 GHz to 49.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modal Inversion-Part II: Application in Determining Antenna Miniaturization Limit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Antenna miniaturization is an important research topic in antenna engineering, and there have been many related theoretical and technical studies. The reported theoretical studies mainly focused on establishing the relationship between the antenna miniaturization limit and the antenna bandwidth (or quality-factor). Different from the reported theoretical studies, this paper focuses on revealing the relationship between the antenna miniaturization limit and the antenna near/far field distribution, and proposes a method to determine the limit from the field distribution. The proposed method is based on a generalized electromagnetic modal inversion method.

articleTitle: A Novel Correntropy-Based Estimation Algorithm for Multi-Sensor Systems Under Hybrid Cyber-Attacks Using Multi-Dimension-Student's-t-Kemel
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: We consider the state estimation of the non-Gaussian systems observed by multi-sensors subject to hybrid cyber-attacks. The wireless communication network facilitates the information exchange while introducing the risk of cyber-attacks. The estimation performance of the conventional estimators no longer holds under the coupling effect of cyber-attacks and non-Gaussian noise. To solve the issue, we first introduce a new correntropy defined using the multi-dimension-student’ (MDSTK) inspired by the property of maximum correntropy criterion (MCC) in dealing with heavy-tailed noise. Derived according to the newly MDSTK-based cost function, we obtain a novel correntropy-based estimation for the fusion of multi-sensors with non-Gaussian noise under both denial of service and deception attacks. Simulations of a target tracking example are provided to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms as compared with related works.

articleTitle: Attack-Aware Capability Assessment Method Based on Specific Semantic Search
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an attack perception capability assessment method based on the specific semantic search for the problem of attack perception capability assessment of security protection equipment for power monitoring systems. The method aims to improve the recognition and localization accuracy of common attacks by accurately correlating the output products of security equipment with the execution of attack test cases. The research employs an attack-specific semantic generation technique that combines attack attribute values with timestamps to form specific semantics for subsequent matching. Pattern matching algorithm, specifically the BM (Boyer-Moore) algorithm, is further utilized to match the specific semantics with the output products of the security device Snort to achieve attack localization. Experimental results demonstrate that Snort exhibits high accuracy in perceiving the majority of attack types and exhibits an enhanced perception rate compared to certain baseline methods. In summary, the method proposed in this paper effectively improves the sensing ability of security equipment to attacks on the power monitoring system and provides a new idea for the performance evaluation of security protection equipment.

articleTitle: Construction and Optimization of Production Line Carbon Emission Management System Based on Digital Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In discrete manufacturing industries, carbon emissions on production lines are influenced by various factors, including equipment status and process variations. Accurate calculation of carbon emissions requires advanced carbon quantification algorithms. However, due to the presence of energy structure and process variations, single carbon emission prediction models have poor adaptability, leading to results that are not sufficiently accurate or reliable. Therefore, it is crucial to construct a set of electric-carbon coupling prediction models to achieve near real-time calculation of carbon emissions. This paper proposes an electric-carbon coupling prediction model based on the emission factor method, utilizing computer technology and data analysis methods to establish the coupling relationship between electricity consumption and carbon emissions. By collecting electricity consumption data and combining them with carbon emission factors from specific power sources, the total carbon emissions can be estimated. This model fully exploits the real-time value of electricity data, providing support for predicting enterprise energy consumption structures while also calculating carbon emission data at the same granularity as electricity data, meeting the fine-grained requirements of carbon emission management.

articleTitle: Research on Autonomous Inspection Path of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on Shuffled Frog Leaping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To address the issues of incomplete inspection scope and low efficiency in traditional electric power inspections, the fully autonomous inspection path of unmanned aerial vehicles based on the shuffled frog leaping algorithm (SFLA) is studied. Firstly, an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) leapfrog inspection strategy was proposed at the macro level, including UAV airport deployment, communication scheme design, and sche duling strategy research. On the basis, by establishing constraints for UAV autonomous inspection and using SFLA algorithm to search for the optimal solution for UA V autonomous inspection, a leapfrog fully autonomous inspection path was formed. The experimental results show that the proposed technology path has high efficiency and security in autonomous inspection.

articleTitle: RH-SQL: Refined Schema and Hardness Prompt for Text-to-SQL
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Text-to-SQL is a technology that converts natural language queries into the structured query language SQL. A novel research approach that has recently gained attention focuses on methods based on the complexity of SQL queries, achieving notable performance improvements. However, existing methods entail significant storage and training costs, which hampers their practical application. To address this issue, this paper introduces a method for Text-to-SQL based on Refined Schema and Hardness Prompt. By filtering out low-relevance schema information with a refined schema and identifying query hardness through a Language Model (LM) to form prompts, this method reduces storage and training costs while maintaining performance. It's worth mentioning that this method is applicable to any sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) LM. Our experiments on the Spider dataset, specifically with large-scale LMs, achieved an exceptional Execution accuracy (EX) of 82.6%, demonstrating the effectiveness and greater suitability of our method for real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Low Sidelobe Microstrip Antenna Array for 24 GHz UAV Obstacle Avoidance Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A low sidelobe microstrip antenna array for 24 GHz UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) obstacle avoidance radar system is designed according to the characteristics of direct flight UAV. In this paper, the theoretical model of the antenna is described, and the microstrip antenna unit and feeding network are designed by the electromagnetic simulation software and numerical calculation software. The simulation results show that the center frequency of the antenna array is 24.5 GHz, the gain is 25.05 dB, the beam width is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{8.46}^{\circ}$</tex>, and the sidelobe suppression is −16.62 dB. Impedance bandwidth and radiation bandwidth are greater than 1 GHz. The antenna was fabricated, and the actual measurement results show that the center frequency of the antenna array is 24.5 GHz, the beam width is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{7}^{\circ}$</tex>, the sidelobe suppression is −18.13 dB, and the radiation bandwidth is greater than 1 GHz. It is proved that the designed antenna has good bandwidth and direction characteristics, which can improve the detection range and detection accuracy of the UAV obstacle avoidance radar.

articleTitle: DTP-Based Payload Program Design for High-Throughput Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: CHINASAT-6E communication satellite is the first DTP-based Ku/Ka band high-throughput commercial satellite developed in China, which realizes flexible hinge communication between high-throughput user beams. The article outlines the design of the DTP-based Ku/Ka-band high-throughput payload scheme and summarizes the technical features of the payload's ground-to-satellite integration design, DTP control design, reliability design, etc. It also analyzes the effectiveness of in-orbit use as well as suggestions for the development of subsequent high-throughput flexible satellites. The successful launch and in-orbit application of the satellite have upgraded the technical level of China's high-throughput flexible satellites and laid the foundation for the development of subsequent high-throughput flexible satellites.

articleTitle: Variational Bayesian-Based PHD Filter with Adaptive Detection Probability
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The lack of prior information, such as noise model, clutter model and detection probability, may result in a deep decline of the filter tracking performance in the field of multi-target tracking. In this article, we conduct an in-depth research on the tracking scenarios with unknown measurement noise covariance and unknown detection probability, and propose a probability hypothesis density (PHD) filter with adaptive detection probability based on variational Bayesian, which models the measurement noise covariance (MNC) matrix and detection probability with the inverse gamma (IG) distribution and beta distribution, respectively, and expands the original state space to the extended space consisting of the target state, the MNC and the detection probability. Joint estimation of the three is performed. In the posterior PHD update steps, the detection probabilities of the detected and undetected parts are updated with the parameters of the beta distribution in different ways. Then the state and the MNC are decoupled by the variational Bayesian theory, and the variational iteration is used to approximate true posterior distribution. Simulation results show that the filter has good tracking performance when both the MNC and the detection probability are unknown, which is comparable to the prior information matched PHD filter.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Prediction Method Based on Optuna-Transformer Model in Power Fluctuation Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the scale of distribution systems, the proportion of highly intermittent photovoltaic power generation in distribution systems is increasing. To achieve high-precision prediction of photovoltaic power generation in power fluctuation scenarios, this paper proposes an Optuna-Transformer model for photovoltaic power prediction. First, the Transformer model is used to address photovoltaic power fluctuation characteristics with complex time series correlations. Second, Optuna is used to optimize the selection of the hyperparameters of the Transformer model. Finally, a real photovoltaic dataset is used to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of the model. The results show that the Transformer model optimized by Optuna has a stronger prediction ability than the traditional Transformer model.

articleTitle: Optimal Secure Control for Cyber Physical Systems Against Joint Sensor and Actuator Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the security control problem of CPSs subject to joint sensor and actuator attacks. Different from most existing results, a more realistic situation for the CPSs is proposed by considering joint sensor and actuator attacks, process noise, and measurement noise. To identify joint attacks on sensor and actuator, an effective detector is developed. Based on the detection results, the optimal secure control strategy is designed. Compared with the tradition control method, this paper designed control scheme can ensure that the CPSs achieve optimal performance when the sensor unit and actuator unit are attacked simultaneously. The efficacy of the developed optimal secure control strategy is testified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Using Deep ELM with Mixture Generalized Maximum Correntropy Criterion for SOH Estimation of Li-ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the increase of the number of charge and discharge cycles and the use time, the capacity of the lithium-ion battery will gradually decrease. Its performance will also gradually deteriorate due to aging and the influence of the operating environment. This will seriously affect the operation and driving of electric vehicles and the safety of human life and property. Therefore, it is particularly important to realize accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries. In this paper, on the one hand, we consider that the Battery Management System (BMS) often works in complex environmental conditions and is easily disturbed by non-Gaussian noise and random fluctuations. On the other hand, the large distributional differences between different datasets, the difficulty of obtaining lithium-ion battery data, and the small sample of data under study are considered. In this paper, a data-driven SOH estimation model based on lithium-ion battery is constructed using transfer learning and Mixture Generalized Maximum Correntropy Criterion (MGMCC). The effects of different noises on the estimation performance of the model are investigated. Finally, the effectiveness of the SOH estimation model proposed in this paper is verified under three noise environments.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Network-Based Gait Coordination Control for Bipedal Modular Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at bipedal modular robot (MR) system with strong coupling, a trajectory tracking method based on adaptive neural network (NN) is proposed to solve the gait coordination control issue, and the dynamic model of bipedal MR system is established by Newton-Euler iteration method. In different gait phases, the desired trajectory of the bipedal MR is generated based on the zero moment point (ZMP). On this basis, an adaptive NN control method is designed to track the desired trajectory, and the interconnected dynamic coupling (IDC) effect of bipedal MR is compensated. The algorithm improves the tracking performance of the robot system. In addition, the stability of the bipedal MR system is verified using the Lyapunov theory. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: Nodal Multicomponent Seismic Source Monitoring System Based on Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Today's field seismic signal acquisition is increasingly focusing on measuring translational and rotational components, while also considering the economic and convenient aspects of the instrumentation. The advancement of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) technology has enabled the development of nodal multicomponent seismic monitoring systems. This system utilizes MEMS-based sensors to measure multiple components, including acceleration, angular velocity, and magnetic field, among others. Additionally, this system can be integrated with wireless communication technology to facilitate remote data monitoring. This integration offers the benefits of low cost and small size, thereby making the MEMS-based nodal multicomponent seismic monitoring system a valuable tool for efficient seismic data acquisition and analysis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Optimal Tracking Control for a Class of Nonlinear Discrete-Time Systems with Dead-Zone and Sensor Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of adaptive fault-tolerant optimal tracking control for a specific class of nonlinear discrete-time strict-feedback systems. Unlike previous systems, The systems incorporate the dead-zone and sensor faults, making them more applicable and representative of real-world scenarios. To achieve optimal control, a backstepping with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm is employed. The system stability is demonstrated using the difference Lyapunov function method. Additionally, simulation figures are given to substantiate the efficacy of the designed control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Switching Nodes of Multi-layer Optical Networks Based on Quantum-classical Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a key technology widely used in quantum communication technology, which can achieve unconditionally secure information transmission. At present, the quantum-classical fusion is often used to construct QKD networks, thus enhancing the security level of the current communication network. In addition, the design of the switching node structure of the optical network is related to the planning and deployment of the entire communication network, which helps to build a flexible and scalable communication network. However, in the quantum-classical fusion network, due to the extremely weak quantum signal, it is susceptible to the crosstalk from the classical signal and the phase drift caused by the change of external environment in the transmission process. In this paper, a multi-layer optical network switching node based on the quantum-classical fusion is designed to enable QKD to be integrated into existing classical networks. The node uses conventional device to enable the isolation of quantum signals from classical and synchronization signals to reach more than 30 dB, and to increase the capacity of the switching node with flexibility and scalability.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control of an Integrated Energy System: Low Carbon Modeling and Intelligent Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: An integrated energy system is a complex system that requires intelligent control to optimize its operation. This paper proposes an intelligent control method for integrated energy systems based on a low carbon model. The model integrates a variety of low carbon technologies such as carbon capture systems, demand response, carbon emissions trading, and clean energy generation. The effect of the proposed intelligent control methods on reducing system costs and carbon emissions is verified through a case study. The results show that the combination of the intelligent control method and the low carbon model leads to a significant reduction in system operating costs and carbon emissions. This provides an important reference for intelligent control of the existing integrated energy system from a low-carbon approach.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Dynamic Event-Triggered Control for Discrete-Time Slow Sampling Singularly Perturbed Systems with External Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper deals with the observer-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{H} _{\infty}$</tex> control problem for a class of slow sampling singularly perturbed systems (S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>PSS). By introducing two internal dynamic variables (IDVs), a new observer-based dynamic event-triggered scheme (ETS) with more strict triggering conditions is designed to save more network resources under the unavailable system state. Next, a networked S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>PSs model is constructed, which describes the effects of observer-based dynamic ETS (DETS) and singular perturbation parameter (SPP) simultaneously. By constructing a new Lyapunov function dependent on two IDVs and SPP, the stability criteria of networked S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>PSs are ensured and the numerical stiffness problem can be avoided. Furthermore, this paper achieves the synthesis of the observer-based controller and the DETS. Finally, a fed-batch fermentation example is given to verify the validity of the main results.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Transmitter Front-end Module with Substrate Integrated Wave-guide filter for Ka-band Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, a Ka-band transmitter front-end module with SIW filter for high frequency wireless communication is proposed. The transmitter front-end module integrates multiple components such as mixer, substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW) filter, voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), low noise amplifier, multiplier and a power amplifier. The transmit gain of the RF Front-end link is more than 10dB, the transmission power is 11.823dBm at 27. 4GHz, and the intermodulation signal is suppressed below 63dBc. Full load thermal simulation result indicates that each chip junction temperature is below 64°C. Experimental measurement show that the insertion loss of the RF output signal transmission path is less than 0.34 dB and the return loss is less than -20dB at 28GHz. The third-order substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter insertion loss is less than 3dB, and bandwidth of 4% is obtained in 27GHz-band. The excellent overall performance of the novel integrated RF front-end system with SIW filter shows great potential to reach fully integrated passive front-end solution for a millimeter wave (MMW) wire-less communication system.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Optimal Control for Human in the Loop Multi-Agent Systems Under FDI Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates event-triggered optimal control for human-in-the-loop (HiTL) multi-agent systems (MASs) facing false data injection (FDI) attacks. An approach is introduced to enhance the security of sensor measurements against sparse attacks by employing a secure preselector, while also devising a state observer to estimate the system state, which is not directly measurable. Introducing an event-driven mechanism for solution transformation involves establishing a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, while employing a critic network along-side an experience replay technique to approximate it. Lyapunov stability theory is employed to derive an event-triggered condition ensuring the boundedness of consensus error and critic network weight error.

articleTitle: Composition and Application of Acoustic Detection System for Human Occupied Vehicle Research Vessel
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A human occupied vehicle (HOV) research vessel, as a modern specialized research vessel, should provide comprehensive support for the deep-diving operations of the HOV and perform ocean scientific research tasks. Its acoustic system includes a deep-water multi-beam sounding system, a medium and shallow water multi-beam sounding system, a deep-water single-beam sounding system, a deep-water shallow formation profile detection system, a deep-sea ultra short baseline positioning system, a shipborne acoustic doppler current profiler, an underwater acoustic communication system, and an auxiliary sensor system. This paper introduces the acoustic system of the HOV research vessel, discussing its basic functions and system composition. It also presents typical application methods and detection data during marine scientific investigations. Practical results show that the rational use of the HOV research vessel's acoustic detection system significantly improves the efficiency of underwater detection and facilitates the quick deployment and recovery of submersible instruments.

articleTitle: Research on Maintenance Testing Technology of Information Equipment Based on Cloud Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at the low degree of network, intelligence and universality in the maintenance and testing of information equipment in current weapons and equipment, this paper explores the key cloud testing technologies of “network sharing of test resources + open and autonomous of test management + intelligent adaptation of test objects” based on the cloud concept, and builds a remote network maintenance and testing platform suitable for a variety of objects. It realizes independent planning of test tasks, dynamic invocation of test resources, remote test of radio frequency signals, and effectively improves the testing and support efficiency of information equipment.

articleTitle: Wellington-YOLOv5I: An Aerial Insulator Defect Detection Based on YOLOv5 and Multi-scale Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Insulators are one of the important components of transmission lines. Due to being exposed to the natural environment, high-altitude insulators are subjected to long-term erosion such as wind, rain, and light, which inevitably leads to damage and serious pollution. Insulator defects can endanger the normal operation of transmission systems, therefore insulator defect detection plays an important role in the safety and stability of power supply systems. This paper proposed an improved insulator defect detection method Wellington-YOLOv5I, based on attention mechanism and multi-scale feature fusion, to address the issues of high environmental impact, low accuracy of small object detection, and loss of features during information extraction in traditional object detection algorithms; This article first added an output header to the network and introduced multi-scale fusion methods to better extract information. Finally, an attention mechanism was introduced to reduce natural interference and highlight the network's attention to the insulator part. Tests on the dataset had shown that compared to other algorithms, Wellington-YOLOv5I could significantly improve detection accuracy while maintaining a high detection speed. The average accuracy of this method was 4.2% higher than the YOLOv51 algorithm, and the FPS was only reduced by 2.6, providing a new approach for the detection of insulator defects in the air.

articleTitle: Adaptive Memory-Event-Triggered Encryption Control for Networked Control Systems Under Denial-of-Service Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Due to the essence of openness, networked control systems (NCSs) are susceptible to malicious attacks, network congestion and data leakage, which brings significant control challenges. This paper investigates NCSs under denial-of-service attacks (DoS) and proposes an adaptive memory-event-triggered encryption control method. An adaptive memory-event-triggered mechanism (AMETM) is designed to reduce the loss of critical data and save network resources. Based on the AMETM, an encryption-decryption scheme is designed to guarantee data privacy. Then an augmented switched system is constructed to characterize the impact of DoS attacks, AMETM and encryption-decryption scheme in a unified framework. The conditions for exponential stability of the system are obtained. Solutions to the observer gain, triggering parameters and controller gain are also given. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by a simulation. The results show that the scheme not only saves network resources and reduces the loss of critical data under DoS attacks, but also ensures data privacy and system stability.

articleTitle: Global Fractional Second-Order Sliding Mode Control for Underactuated Systems with Performance Constraint and Input Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With more degrees of freedom and intrinsic structural constraints, underactuated systems present significant challenges in control. For underactuated systems with performance constraint and input saturation, a global fractional second-order sliding mode controller (GFSOSMC) is proposed. By designing the performance function and error transformation function, the position error can be constrained within a prescribed range. The fractional order calculus operators which convert the integer order differential and integral quantities into fractional order ones are introduced to the sliding mode surface. To omit the convergent mode and remain robustness throughout, the global sliding factor is introduced. With the fractional second-order sliding mode surface and the global sliding factor, the GFSOSMC is designed. Then a hyperbolic tangent function is used to approach the input saturation. The proposed method not only addresses performance constraint and input saturation, but also effectively mitigates the chattering. Meanwhile, it enables the position and velocity to converge rapidly.

articleTitle: Optimized the Rebound Drive Control of the Needle Valve Seat of the Injector of the In-Cylinder Direct Injection Hydrogen Engine Injector
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this study, the motion law of the hydrogen engine injector and the influencing factors of the injector needle valve rebound problem were analyzed. The step-up and down-voltage chopper circuit is used in the injector drive control of the hydrogen engine, and the second-order driving circuit of another section of pull-up current is added when the needle valve is opened to reduce the electromagnetic force rising too fast when the needle valve is opened and a buffer current is added when the needle valve is seated, and the bounce problem of the hydrogen injector is optimized by the control mode of inhibiting the excessive acceleration of the needle valve by the small electromagnetic force. The drive control model is established by Simulink, and the two improved drive waveforms are simulated and analyzed. Through the control optimization of the hydrogen injector, it can be concluded that adding another stage of pulling voltage after the main pulling current can effectively reduce the collision problem caused by the turn-on by about 97.5%. Adding a buffer current after the end of the maintenance current can effectively reduce the collision problem when seated, which is reduced by about 81.6%.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction Model of PCB Etch Factor Based on DE-BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: As a core component of various electronic products, the production quality of printed circuit board (PCB) directly affects the performance and reliability of electronic devices. The etch factor serves as a key indicator for assessing the quality of PCB traces, and its rapid and precise detection is vital for enhancing the production efficiency and quality of PCB. In this paper, a differential evolution (DE) algorithm optimized backpropagation (BP) neural network (DE-BP) prediction model is proposed to achieve the prediction of the PCB etch factor. After employing feature selection to reduce the input features, the DE algorithm is utilized to optimize the initial parameters of the BP neural network. Subsequently, the trained model is applied to predict the etch factor of PCB. The results show that the DE-BP model constructed in this paper can effectively predict the etch factor of PCB. Compared with the traditional BP model, the DE-BP model exhibits enhanced prediction performance.

articleTitle: Motor Bearing Fault Diagnosis based on Improved MobilenetV2
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Addressing the challenges of insufficient characteristic information for motor bearings, complex fault diagnosis models, and low accuracy, this paper proposes a bearing fault diagnosis method based on an improved MobileNetV2 network. Initially, the method employs Continuous Wavelet Transform to convert bearing vibration signals into time-frequency images, resolving the issue of spatial information loss in one-dimensional signals and enhancing recognition precision and learning efficiency. Subsequently, a Parallel Convolutional Block Attention Module is utilized to adaptively optimize network focus on the signal, thereby improving feature extraction capabilities. Finally, the incorporation of the LeakyReLU activation function and Nadam optimizer enhances the accuracy and speed of fault detection. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves an accuracy of 99.59%, with significant improvements in recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, attaining an inference speed of 44.12 FPS and a parameter count of 2.80M. Compared to other methods, this approach offers superior stability, accuracy, robustness, and generalizability.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature and Thermal Stress of SiC MOSFETs based on Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: silicon carbide (SiC), as a new generation of semiconductors, has had a huge impact in the field of power electronics, and its superior electrical characteristics have become the key to the development of semiconductor devices today. However, the detection of health status of SiC MOSFETs is still not perfect. As the key parameters of health status of SiC MOSFETs, temperature and stress can be studied by finite element simulation. In this paper, the temperature distribution and thermal stress distribution of SiC MOSFETs are studied through the finite element simulation of SiC MOSFETs multi-physical field. It is found that the temperature distribution is positively correlated with the electric field excitation, and the stress distribution is exponentially increased with the electric field excitation. The multi-physical fields of SiC MOSFETs are coupled with each other. It provides a new way to detect the health status of SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Wood Surface Defect Detection Using Improved Deep Learning Algorithm:FRCE-YOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To address the challenges of large workload and slow speed in defect detection tasks in wood quality control, a lightweight multi-objective defect detection algorithm(FRCE-YOLO) is proposed. Firstly, the C2f-fast module based on the FAST module is introduced in the YOLOv8 backbone, and then RepGhostbottleneck module is incorporated in the neck to effectively reduce the number of network parameters. Simultaneously, CBAM is integrated into C2f module, which enhances the ability to capture various defect features and the loss function is replaced with EIOU. Finally, FRCE-YOLO is evaluated on the optimised dataset using YOLOV8 as a benchmark. Compared to YOLOv8, the mAP@0.5 has been improved by 6.9%, reaching 80.7%. The mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by 8.4% and reducing computational complexity by 1.2 GFLOPs. The results indicate that our algorithm performs faster, at a lower cost for wood defect detection.

articleTitle: Small Defect Detection Model of Oil Pipeline Based on Improved Swin Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of small magnetic leakage defect detection, insufficient detection data and low detection accuracy, a gate-controlled parallel expansion convolution shift window converter (GPST) is proposed. The gated parallel expansive convolution shifted window Converter (GPST) is an improvement on Swin- Transformer. The gated parallel expansive convolutional layer is introduced in the backbone network of GPST. The gated unit can reduce the unnecessary computation. The other part of convolution improves the ability of the network to extract global context information, which is conducive to improving the accuracy of model detection. The experimental results show that when IOU = 0.5, the accuracy of the algorithm is 95.6%, and the inference time is 8.2ms.

articleTitle: Deformable Multi-Sequence Guided Model for Cholangiocarcinoma Staging
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article explores using artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning, to improve the diagnosis and staging of Cholangiocarcinoma. Traditional imaging methods are limited by equipment resolution and subjective judgment, leading to variable outcomes. The paper proposes a deformable multi-sequence guided model using MRI data, addressing small sample issues with data augmentation and sequence equidistant sampling. It employs deformable ConvLSTM modules and a parallel co-attention mechanism to enhance multimodal data analysis. Experimental results show the model performs well in Cholangiocarcinoma staging, aiding clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Cooperative Opponent Intention Recognition Based on Trajectory Analysis by Distributed Fractional Bayesian Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Opponent intention recognition is a crucial component for multi-agent decision-making. This paper proposes a novel distributed fractional Bayesian inference algorithm for opponent intention recognition in the Multiagent Pursuit-Evasion (MPE) game for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) confrontation. The algorithm infers the opponent's intention between pursuit and evasion by analyzing the trajectories in dynamic interaction under a game-theoretical model. This process involves comparing the prediction trajectory with the observed noisy trajectory to update the intention beliefs using fractional Bayesian inference. Additionally, it obtains a consensual intention through distributed linear average. Our method can effectively distinguish the intention of opponents in MPE games. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed algorithm performance.

articleTitle: A Step-type Obstacle Detection Method based on 3D Point Cloud Map
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of precise detection of traversable obstacles resembling steps in 3D point cloud map generated by LiDAR, this paper proposes a detection algorithm based on Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and geometric constraints. The proposed method achieves accurate detection of step-type traversable obstacles in 3D point cloud map. Firstly, the 3D point cloud map is filtered to remove outliers and extract regions of interest. Then, the Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) plane fitting algorithm is employed to detect and remove ground points for eliminating clustering interference. Subsequently, the DBSCAN algorithm is applied for density clustering of the point cloud map without ground points. Finally, geometric constraints resembling step-type traversable obstacles are applied to the clustering results to select the optimal detection targets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed detection algorithm can accurately detect various step-type traversable obstacles in indoor 3D point cloud maps, achieving desirable outcomes.

articleTitle: Research on Robot Path Planning of Mountain Area Based on Stochastic Nonlinear Ant Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In an effort to improve the safety of robot application in mountain areas and overcome the defect that the conventional ant colony algorithm is prone to local optimum, this paper has carried on the corresponding research. Firstly, in the probability selection stage, considering that the maximum turning range of the robot to the left and right during the travel process is 180 °, a nonlinear weight factor proposed in this paper. By affecting the selection of feasible points by ant colony, the possibility of the robot to turn around greatly is reduced, which not only enhance the safety capability of the robot in the mountain environment, but also leads the robot to the destination. Besides that, this paper also introduces a random selection process in the path planning stage, thereby expanding the hunting range of the robot, so that the result of the improved algorithm can out of the local optimum, and the path length tends to the global optimal solution. The simulation results show that the stochastic nonlinear ant colony algorithm (SNIACO) can effectively enhance the safety of robot application in mountain environment, and the performance of path length, average rotation angle and path smoothness is also better than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Distributed Robust Privacy Preservation ICC-based Algorithm for Economic Dispatch in Smart Grids with Communication Delay via Using Chebyshev Polynomial
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper design the incremental cost consensus-based (ICC-based) algorithm to tackle the economic dispatch problem (EDP) in smart grids (SGs) with privacy preservation guaranteed via using Chebyshev polynomial. Robustness of the proposed ICC-based EDP algorithm is reflected in that communication delay between adjacent agents is considered, and the communication topology can be time-varying with row stochastic connection matrix. Moreover, the privacy of exchanged state information is preserved by using Chebyshev polynomial instead of adding random noise method. Comparing with the common adding random noise method, this kind of privacy-preserving method can achieve the accurate convergence of the algorithm. Subsequently, the convergence of the algorithm and the optimal solution of EDP are analyzed by detailed theoretical proof. It can be found that the convergence value of the proposed algorithm is the optimal solution of EDP, and the communication delay with the uniform upper bound can be allowed. Finally, the simulation experiment is given to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network for Information Diffusion Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Information diffusion is the process by which information spreads through a network of individuals or nodes, which is crucial for understanding and predicting social behavior. Research indicates that the diffusion of information is shaped by the network's structure, the personal characteristics of users, and the nature of the information itself. However, most models ignore the social network graph and treat the diffusion path of information as a sequence rather than a graph. This paper proposes a novel Spatiotemporal-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network (SAHGAT). The model constructs a heterogeneous graph that integrates user social attention and reposting behavior, using Graph Attention Network (GAT) to learn a comprehensive representation of users in terms of social relationships and information dissemination behavior. It combines users' social features, location, and time information to generate representations of the cascade sequence, aiming to predict the next user likely to participate in reposting. Experimental results on three datasets, including Twitter, show that this model outperforms models that ignore the social graph and treat the diffusion path only as a sequence.

articleTitle: A Strategy for Enhancing Modal Fusion Based on LLaVA towards Military Field
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The Large Language and Vision Assistant (LLaVA) has demonstrated the performance of state of art in visual question answering tasks, with accuracy constantly refreshing on various benchmarks. In the specific military field, the understanding and answering abilities of LLaVA towards military images urgently need to be strengthened, and there are problems with generated answers that are not related to the images or contain incorrect information. This paper makes two improvements based on LLaVA. Firstly, we construct a military dataset for model training, which includes images of weapons and equipment, battlefield environment and war situation. Secondly, in the multimodal fusion stage, a stacked attention network is used to capture the interrelationships between different modalities, focusing the question text on a strongly correlated part of the image, thereby improving the performance of the model on complex reasoning questions. The results in this paper show that the improved model performs better in military question answering than the previous general model.

articleTitle: Traffic Speed Forecasting using GCN and BiGRU
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Traffic forecasting is a component of the intelligent transportation system (ITS), which is of great significance to improve traffic operation efficiency and strengthen traffic safety. But, because of the complex and ever-changing temporal and spatial relationships between traffic flow, traffic forecasting is still challenging. To reduce prediction errors and effectively represent the spatiotemporal features of traffic data, a traffic speed forecasting model utilizing graph convolutional neural networks and bidirectional gated recurrent units (GCN-BiGRU) is proposed. On the one hand, graph convolutional neural network is used to extract the traffic data's spatial features, which allow them to capture the topology and semantic information between the traffic nodes. Additionally, a spatial embedding and an attention mechanism are introduced simultaneously to enhance spatial correlation between the nodes. On the other hand, in order to extract the temporal characteristics of the traffic information, bi-directional gated recurrent unit is utilized to obtain information from both forward and backward propagation, which improves the model's forecasting ability in the time dimension. The results of experiments on real datasets demonstrate that GCN-BiGRU has a good forecasting effect and performs well in terms of forecasting accuracy at time steps of 15min, 30min and 60min.

articleTitle: Sampled-Data Based Robust Multi-Objective Path-Following Control of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper proposes a sampled-data multi-objective path-following control method for autonomous vehicles based on the polytopic linear parameter varying (LPV) approach. Combining the active front-wheel steering (AFS) and the direct yaw moment control (DYC) strategies, an LPV path-following model is established subject to time-varying longitudinal velocity and uncertain cornering stiffness. Based on it, a sampled-data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}/GH_{2}$</tex> controller is obtained by solving linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), which guarantees the path-following performance and the lateral stability of the vehicle. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is verified in the simulation.

articleTitle: A WiFi Indoor Localization Method Based on Gaussian Mixture Distribution Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In response to the challenges of low positioning accuracy in indoor localization with the WKNN algorithm and the significant impact of k values on positioning results, a novel positioning algorithm is proposed that integrates the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with WKNN using Channel State Information (CSI). The algorithm utilizes CSI amplitudes collected from fingerprint points to create a Gaussian mixture probability distribution model, substituting probabilities for conventional amplitudes in Euclidean distance calculations. Additionally, probabilities are applied as weighting factors in calculations to effectively reduce errors between calculated distances and actual distances, thereby increasing positioning accuracy. To address the impact of k values on positioning outcomes, a k-value selection method based on a threshold is implemented, with final positioning results determined by the WKNN algorithm. Experimental results demonstrate a 22% improvement in positioning accuracy compared to traditional WKNN algorithms, with an 80% probability of achieving positioning accuracy superior to 1.82 meters.

articleTitle: Research on Java Performance and Energy Efficiency Optimization Technology for ARM Server
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Server is one of the most critical and commonly used infrastructure in information technology. Pursuing higher performance and lower energy consumption is an important goal that needs to be considered in server manufacturing and application, as it can bring better economic benefits to users. SPECpower is a benchmark developed by the global third-party non-profit organization SPEC (Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation) for evaluating Java server energy efficiency testing. This article focuses on ARM architecture Java servers and proposes and verifies key technologies for benchmark testing implementation and optimization through experiments. Conducting an ARM architecture Java server energy efficiency optimization evaluation, the optimized server energy efficiency has been significantly improved, providing reference for server deployment and optimization.

articleTitle: Implementation of Multiple Signal Classification Algorithm Based on Blade Server
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The MUSIC (Multiple Signal Classification) algorithm, as an important foundation of spatial spectrum estimation theory and methods, plays a crucial role in issues such as super-resolution angle measurement, multipath signal DOA estimation, and direction finding in high-density signal environments. However, the MUSIC algorithm involves a large number of matrix operations, and relying on traditional FPGA+DSP architecture design will have drawbacks such as low development efficiency, high resource consumption, and long processing time. CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture) is a parallel computing architecture proposed by NVIDIA, which combines the advantages of CPU and GPU and is mainly used to handle intensive and parallel computing. There are various matrix operation function libraries in CUDA, and relying on CUDA function libraries to implement the MUSIC algorithm has advantages such as short calculation time, flexible program design, strong universality, and portability. This article is based on the hardware platform of CPU+GPU, using the function library in CUDA to complete the program design and engineering implementation of the MUSIC algorithm.

articleTitle: Authenticated Encryption for the LOL Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the advent of the 5G era, in order to achieve ultra-fast software implementation for the ubiquitous virtual networks and high-security level for post-quantum cryptography to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authentication during data transmission, a methodology for integration of authentication and encryption processes for a general framework for designing blockwise stream ciphers is proposed, and automated analysis of the improved LOL framework are performed to prove its security. The key generation mechanism in the ZUC algorithm combined with the HMAC algorithm to generate tags is integrated into the LOL framework. The correctness and security of the encryption and authentication parts are verified using Cryptol and STP, tools for formal verification and automated analysis of cryptographic algorithms. Experiments have shown that the new scheme has high performance. The introduction of automated analysis tools provides a comprehensive assessment of security and ensures robustness under various attack modes, allowing data to be encrypted with simultaneous authentication, improving overall security and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Heap Security Mechanism Based on Block Randomization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: C/C++ languages often require dynamically man-aged temporary memory, i.e. heap memory, however securing heap memory is very challenging. Attacks like heap overflow, use-after-free, invalid-free, and double-free are very common, and these attacks can corrupt user data in heap memory, such as overwriting variable pointers, function pointers, and data to construct arbitrary memory reads and writes, as well as control flow hijacking. Despite the extensive research in the area of heap memory security, many modern software still suffers from such vulnerabilities. Therefore, the security of the heap region of a program is a growing concern, and the study of heap region security can help mitigate the negative impact of the increasing number of heap security vulnerabilities, which is of great practical significance. One of the major reasons that make the heap vulnerable is that the addresses of heap blocks are predictable in advance, because the allocation of heap space is too regular. In this paper, we propose a block randomization algorithm for the entire heap memory space. The algorithm proposes a random memory block allocation method that increases the unpredictability of the heap memory address and improves the security of the computer system, and at the end, the defense effect as well as the performance of the algorithm is tested through experiments to determine the optimal randomization parameters.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Fault-Tolerant Control for Robotic Systems with Output Constraint
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A predefined-time fault-tolerant control is proposed for robotic systems with output constraint. A predefined-time sliding mode observer (PTSMO) is designed to estimate the actuator faults. The position tracking error is constrained by a performance function and transformed by a transform function. With the transformed error and the fault information estimated by the PTSMO, a PTSM controller is designed. The system is proved to be stable and convergent within the predefined time while satisfying the output constraint performance. Simulation results indicate that when the robotic system encounters actuator faults, the proposed control can guarantee that the position tracking error is within the performance range and converges fast within a predefined time.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High-Speed Multi-Port Shared Cache Management System Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the rapid development of modern network technology and significant growth in internet traffic, the demand for network bandwidth has also increased, posing higher requirements for the data processing capabilities of switching systems. This paper designs and implements a high-speed multi- port shared cache management system aimed at avoiding the impact of data frame length and data bit width on memory resources. It dynamically adjusts space through memory recycling to save storage resources, enhance data storage efficiency, and improve data verification and error correction capabilities. The design supports line-rate forwarding for multiple gigabit ports using a dynamic shared caching strategy and integrates CRC checks and QoS scheduling functions. The RTL code for the high-speed multi-port shared cache management system was developed using Verilog language, and the design was comprehensively validated through a simulation platform and an FPGA verification platform. Both simulation and FPGA verification results have proven the design's correctness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Near-Field mmWave Imaging with Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar (CSAR) has achieved remarkable success in far-field imaging for aircraft and satellites. However, its application in near-field imaging has received limited attention. This paper proposes a near-field millimeter-wave FMCW CSAR imaging system based on time-domain Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW). Building upon the traditional Back Projection (BP) algorithm, this system integrates multiple receiving channels into a single antenna element, accurately fits complex circular trajectories, reduces the number of radar antenna elements, and lowers imaging costs, laying a solid foundation for subsequent applications of multi-channel CSAR imaging BP algorithms. This paper first introduces the imaging geometry of CSAR and then describes the relevant parameters and calculation formulas. Subsequently, it applies the BP algorithm to process multi-channel data to obtain the final imaging results. Finally, we present and compare imaging results from both simulated and measured data. The experimental results validate the correctness of the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system in practical applications.

articleTitle: RIS-Aided Full-Duplex Wireless Powered Communication Network: Dynamic Beamforming or Static Beamforming?
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enhanced full-duplex (FD) wireless-powered communication network (WPCN) with a hybrid access point (HAP) that concurrently transmits energy and receives signal. Iterative algorithms are proposed to discuss whether the RIS beamforming should be dynamic or static across the uplink and downlink time slots. Simulation results reveal that RIS brings significant gains to in maximizing the rate, and dynamic beamforming strategy is preferable in improving the system performance.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Multi-Frequency Band Transmission Scheme Based on Radio over Fiber Communication Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the increasing demand for communication, the future development of communication is moving towards high-frequency bands, large bandwidth, and fast transmission rates. Microwave photonics technology, due to its unique advantages in photonics, provides new solutions for future communication technologies. This article emphasizes the limitations of microwave technology, introduces radio over fiber communication technology, and designs a multi-band signal transmission scheme based on radio over fiber communication technology to enhance the signal transmission rate and flexibility of communication systems. Key parameters and performance indicators in multi-band radio over fiber links are discussed, and simulation analysis is conducted. The results of low BER and high isolation transmission are obtained. Through this research, feasibility is provided for RF links in high-frequency bands, large bandwidth, fast transmission rates, and flexible reconfigurability. Finally, this article outlines the potential development paths and key considerations for multi-band radio over fiber links.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Optimization for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting based on CNN-BiGRU
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Accurate and stable prediction of PV generation has the potential to significantly enhance the stability of power systems and mitigate the reliance on conventional environmental resources. Nevertheless, many prediction models lack data processing and do not consider the model's generalisation capacity, resulting in poor robustness of the model. To solve this gap, a hybrid deep learning framework based on multi-criteria optimization and successive variational modal decomposition is presented. Firstly, the Pearson correlation analysis thermodynamic diagram is utilised to determine the input characteristics of the model, then the PV data undergoes a process of consecutive variational modal decomposition to mitigate the presence of high-frequency noise. Furthermore, a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) network is employed to further investigate the temporal dependencies within each subsequence. Meantime, multi-criteria particle swarm optimization is utilized to optimize the important parameter of BiGRU model. The experimental findings demonstrate that the prediction model has superior prediction accuracy compared to alternative models.

articleTitle: Satellite Radar Group Target Tracking Algorithm Using TP-GLMB Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the group target detection scenario of low orbit satellite radar, the coexistence of distinguishable targets and indistinguishable targets in the group and the dynamic transformation lead to the degradation of tracking performance. To solve the problem, a GLMB filtering algorithm based on target type discrimination for partially distinguishable group targets was proposed. In the process of prediction and update, the target type parameter and DBSCAN clustering algorithm are introduced, and the centroid equivalent measurement is used to replace the indistinguishable target measurements. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better tracking performance when distinguishable and indistinguishable targets coexist and change dynamically compared with existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Low-Altitude Target Angle Estimation Based on Soft Threshold and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The traditional neural network-based angle-direction estimation methods are mainly for non-coherent signals, and it is difficult to effectively achieve the accurate estimation of direction of arrival in the low altitude multipath environment with low SNR. In this paper, we propose an innovative neural network algorithm that combines the soft threshold module and attention mechanism. The introduction of the soft threshold module aims to reduce signal noise and the attention mechanism is employed to further explore the connection between different channel features in order to enhance angle measurement performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves the accuracy of angle measurement and exhibits robustness under low SNR.

articleTitle: Impact of Crosstalk and Loss on the Training Process of Integrated Photonic Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Integrated photonic neural networks (IPNNs), with their ability to process large-scale data and parallelize multiple computational tasks, have shown impressive promise for applications in the field of artificial intelligence. However, due to some hard-to-ignore non-ideal characteristics of the underlying silicon photonic MZI devices constituting the IPNN, these non-ideal characteristics can cause the input signal to be affected by crosstalk noise and optical loss during transmission, thus affecting the training and inference accuracy of the IPNN. In order to solve these problems, this paper establishes an analytical model of IPNN affected by crosstalk noise and loss during the training process, covering component level, layer level and system level. Simulations using this model show that the inference accuracy of IPNN decreases by about 65% when the crosstalk noise in the training phase of IPNN reaches -20 dB, while the inference accuracy of IPNN decreases by about 55% when the optical loss reaches -0.5 dB.

articleTitle: Ship Fuel Consumption Prediction Model Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Recently, the European Commission and the International Maritime Organization (IMO) have implemented various operational measures and policies to reduce ship fuel consumption and related emissions. Considering that the accurate prediction of ship fuel consumption is crucial for controlling ship emissions, this paper proposes a ship fuel consumption prediction model based on long short-term memory (LSTM) technology. Firstly, the data preprocessing of the real ship data is performed by using the Chauvenet criterion. Secondly, the basic framework of the ship fuel consumption prediction model is established. Then, the LSTM algorithm is utilized to establish the prediction model. The accuracy of the proposed method is verified by the simulation of actual ship data.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Control of Excitation Structure Generator Based on Single Chip Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, the monitoring and control of generators have significantly improved. This system aims to achieve comprehensive and continuous monitoring of the operational status of excitation generators through advanced wireless communication technology. The core functions of the system include real-time acquisition of excitation current, temperature, and vibration signals, and the conversion of these physical parameters into digital signals. This paper utilizes a Radial Basis Function(RBF) neural network to process the collected vibration signals and determine the operational status of the generator based on the processing results. Compared with traditional generator fault monitoring, this system can more accurately monitor the operational status of the generator and control the generator based on the monitoring results. Hardware implementation has demonstrated that this system can more precisely monitor the operational status of the generator and achieve control over the generator.

articleTitle: Blind Area Optimization of Multiple Interference Incident Angles Based on Improved Harris Hawks Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The cancellation blind area is closely related to interference incident angle. The distribution and proportion of blind area vary with different interference incident angle. This paper proposes an improved Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) to optimize the blind area of sparse planar array with multiple interference incident angles. The simulation verifies that the method can control the blind area in main interference incident area below 8% and the blind area in non-main interference incident area no more than 18%. Compared with the uniform sparse planar array, the blind area is reduced by about 10% and 12%, respectively.

articleTitle: A Fast Acquisition Scheme of Pseudo-Noise (PN) Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Blind decoder is designed for the acquisition of m-sequences by the receiver. There may be many error chips in the m-sequence estimated by conventional detection methods., like eigenvalue decomposition. This decoder of the receiver can decode the m-sequence containing error chips and accurately restore the original m-sequence of the transmitter and provide an indication of whether to restore successfully. In order to achieve the above functions., firstly., several important conclusions is derived in the paper about the m-sequence that will be used in the design of the decoder; secondly., a voting model based on probability theory and mathematical statistics is proposed., which is used to decode error m-sequences blindly; finally., the theoretical boundaries of the blind decoder are derived for different m-sequences generated by line shift registers with different stages. Simulation results show that this blind decoder can perform accurate restores for m-sequences whose error chip rate is within the theoretical boundary.

articleTitle: Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation Based Parameter-efficient Tuning for Low-resource Visual Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The Visual Question Answering (VQA) task involves using pretrained Vision Language Models (VLMs) to provide accurate answers to natural language questions related to images. Among these, the Vision-and-Language BERT (ViLBERT) model employs two separate streams for visual and language inputs, fused through a co-attention mechanism, enhancing the accuracy and relevance of the answers. However, the parameter size of this model poses significant challenges in terms of computational resources and storage space when full fine-tuning it for VQA tasks. To address this, we introduce a parameter-efficient tuning strategy based on Quantized Low-Rank Optimization (QLoRA) into the VQA task, aimed at reducing the trainable parameter count and training time of VLMs. This approach minimizes the resource consumption of the ViLBERT model in VQA tasks. We applied the QLoRA fine-tuning strategy to the ViLBERT model and conducted extensive experiments on the VQA2.0, GQA, and Visual7W datasets. The results show that, compared to existing parameter-efficient tuning methods, our approach achieves higher model performance while improving parameter usage efficiency and reducing training time. This provides an effective strategy for similar challenges in VQA tasks.

articleTitle: Wide-Range Divider Chain Based on CML Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A wide range divider chain based on CML structure in 28-nm CMOS process is implemented including a main divider chain and a multiplexer selector in this paper. Each 2/3 dual mode divider can divide and divide the input signal, and the multiplex selector can screen the required frequency according to the control signal to output, which can achieve a large coverage and flexible and easy to adjust the frequency range of the divider output. In this work, the input frequency is between 20-30GHz and the output frequency is in a wide range between 0.83-15GHz. The frequency divider chain has a wider output frequency range and requires less hardware, which is more conducive to the on-chip integration of the digital PLL and greatly saves the entire chip area of the digital PLL.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Channel Amplitude and Phase Errors on EVM in Satellite Multi-Beam RF Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the multi-beam Radio Frequency (RF) system of satellites, the channel amplitude and phase errors are non-ideal factors that are difficult to eliminate, and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) is an effective indicator for evaluating such non-ideal factors. This paper establishes a multi-channel RF system model based on OFDM modulation, where the channel amplitude and phase errors can be set. Controlled experiments were conducted in multiple scenarios to analyze the EVM loss caused by channel amplitude and phase errors. Through analyzing the experimental results, two interesting conclusions were drawn. Firstly, channel estimation and equalization techniques can effectively mitigate the EVM loss caused by channel amplitude and phase errors, but the noise in the communication system can affect this mitigation effect. Secondly, channel amplitude errors can be effectively eliminated through amplitude normalization.

articleTitle: A 3-6GHz Fast Locking ADPLL Based on Charge-Steering-Sampling Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To meet the demand for high-performance clocks for 5G communications, this paper proposes a fast-locked 3–6 GHz ADPLL loop model based on the charge-steering-sampling (CSS) phase detection (PD) technique, which has an equivalent time-conversion resolution of 350 fs/bit and effectively reduces the quantization noise induced by the TDC. In addition, a two-stage Automatic Frequency Calibration (AFC) module is proposed to preset the frequency control words of the DCO coarse and medium tuning for fast locking. Further, a step-size controllable up/down counting filter is proposed to accelerate the locking speed and improve the frequency accuracy after locking. Based on TSMC 28nm technology, the overall ADPLL model is built using VerilogA/Verilog with a locking time of less than 1.8us, and the DCO part is implemented with a practical LC DCO structure, and achieves -122dBc/Hz@1MHz phase noise at an output frequency of 4GHz, which meets the requirement of fast locking under low phase noise.

articleTitle: An Improved SAR Image Recognition Method based on Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) rely on a large number of parameters and complex network structures, which require significant computational costs, making them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained platforms. In order to address the problems of lightweight deployment, we propose a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image recognition network based on graph neural networks. At first, we effectively reduce the computational cost of the network by designing the construction method of the graph structure and the aggregation formula of the graph network. Subsequently, a node-based attention mechanism is designed to extract structural features of the graph and enhance the network's recognition performance. Experimental results show that our proposed network achieves an accuracy improvement of 8.51 % compared to existing graph neural networks. Besides, compared to CNN and ViT, our network's training time is only 1/6, the number of parameters is 1/285, the FLOPs are 1/152, and the GPU memory usage is 1/5 with a decrease in accuracy of 0.84 %. Additionally, compared to lightweight networks, our network still has advantages in terms of computational cost.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Prescribed Performance Control for Nonlinear Systems with Actuator Failures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This work devises an adaptive fuzzy controller built on event-triggered control (ETC) and prescribed performance control (PPC) for a class of nonlinear systems that have actuator failures and external disturbances. Choice of prescribed performance function determines both the minimum convergence speed and convergence range of the tracking error. As well as The planed ETC can simplify analysis and calculations to conserve resources. The adaptive tracking algorithm is developed through employing the Lyapunov function and backstepping technique to assurance all signals within the closed-loop system are bounded and achieve rapid convergence of the tracking error to the required range. Ultimately, a mechanical example confirms the viability and excellence of the suggested control strategy.

articleTitle: A wideband horizontally polarized omnidirectional antenna conformed on a drone
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A conformal antenna in the 30-50MHz band for disaster relief cargo UAVs is proposed. The effect of lumped capacitance on the radiated current of large size antenna is discussed theoretically. The effect of zero-order resonance mode and first-order resonance mode on the expansion of antenna bandwidth is analyzed from the equivalent circuit.
