articleTitle: A Looped-Functional for Stability Analysis of Time-Delay Impulsive System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the stability of impulsive systems incorporating constant time delays through looped-functional analysis. A novel looped-functional is formulated, which relaxes the necessity for a positive Lyapunov function and utilizes information across the entire interval from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{k}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t_{k+}$</tex>. An improved stability criterion, formulated as a linear matrix inequality (LMI), based on the looped-functional approach. Finally, to validate the theoretical findings, two practical illustrations are presented to showcase the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed findings.

articleTitle: Adaptive Critic Learning for Optimized Tracking Control of an Unmanned Surface Vehicle with Guaranteed Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper develops a critic-based optimal control strategy for an unmanned surface vehicle (USV). To address the constraint requirement on tracking errors, universal barrier function is incorporated with the optimal control scheme, such that the tracking errors satisfy the transient and steady-state performance. Then, to obtain the optimal control law, a single-critic architecture is constructed to solve the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Meanwhile, the basis function in the critic network is selected as Gaussian function. With the improved critic weight updating law, the proposed optimal control algorithm not only relaxes the persistence of excitation (PE) condition but also guarantees the uniformly ultimately boundedness (UUB) of critic network weight. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness the presented optimized control scheme.

articleTitle: Performance Guaranteed Control for Multiagent Systems with Time-Varying State Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The consensus problem of a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems with time-varying state constraints is studied in this paper. Firstly, a prescribed performance function is established to restrain the states within safe allowable region. Secondly, a coordinate transformation function is introduced to transform the state constraint problem of the original variable into a boundedness problem of the new variable, which greatly relaxes the feasibility condition. Then, by resorting to backstepping technique, the consensus control scheme is developed for the considered systems. Finally, the feasibility of the designed method is verified through a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Control of Stochastic Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper addresses the tracking control problem for a specific class of stochastic nonlinear systems structured in strict-feedback form, utilizing output feedback signals. We introduce a fuzzy state observer employing fuzzy logic modeling to estimate system states. An adaptive fuzzy control algorithm is developed by merging dynamic surface control technique with backstepping recursive design.Following this, we establish a novel event-triggered mechanism designed to minimize unnecessary network resource transmission, which encompasses both the sensor-to-controller and controller-to-actuator channels. Through Lyapunov stability analysis, we prove that the controlled plant remains bounded in probability, with all signals globally bounded in probability. Additionally, it ensures that the tracking errors converge to a narrow vicinity around the origin. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is validated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Study on Hierarchical Equalization Topology Circuit of Lithium-ion Battery Pack Based on Buck-Boost*
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this study, an innovative two-layer equalization circuit design is proposed, which is based on a Buck-Boost circuit and a switched-capacitor circuit, and successfully realizes one-to-one and many-to-one equalization within a series-connected energy storage lithium-ion battery pack. The Buck-Boost converter is combined with a bus-based strategy to form a bus-based Buck-Boost equalization topology circuit, while a switched supercapacitor bank is combined with a switched-capacitor circuit to form a switched-supercapacitor bank equalization topology circuit, and the two improved equalization topology circuits form a doublelayer equalization topology circuit. On the MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation platform, eight series-connected lithium iron phosphate battery packs are used as the experimental model, and the static, charging and discharging experiments are carried out. The simulation experiments show that this scheme can effectively improve the balancing effectiveness of the equalization circuit, significantly reduce the inconsistency between single cells, and optimize the overall performance of the battery pack.

articleTitle: Controllability of dynamic-algebraic Boolean control networks based on the semi-tensor product
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper presents a study of the controllability problem of dynamic-algebraic Boolean control networks (DABCNs) based on the semi-tensor product of matrices. Firstly, the state transition matrix (STM) of DABCNs is constructed and based on the STM, the controllability matrix of DABCNs is provided. Secondly, a necessary and sufficient condition for the controllability of DABCNs is established. In comparison with the existing results, certain restrictions have been lifted. Finally, an illustrative example is provided to demonstrate the results obtained.

articleTitle: High Performance Vehicle Antenna for ISM Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article presents the design, simulation, and analysis of an innovative antenna unit tailored to operate within the 2.4 GHz Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) frequency band for smart vehicular applications. The antenna unit's compact architecture, comprising dielectric materials and slotted metal cavities, is thoroughly examined. Simulations demonstrate the antenna's exceptional performance, exhibiting a wide operational bandwidth from 2.38 GHz to 2.5 GHz, high gain exceeding 5 dB in the 2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz range, and effective impedance matching. The necessity of rooftop placement is elucidated, and simulations validate the antenna's robust performance when mounted on a vehicle. Furthermore, a decoupling array comprising two antenna units and negative magnetic permeability metamaterials is simulated, mitigating mutual coupling effects and ensuring high transmission efficiency within the 2.35 GHz to 2.55 GHz frequency range. The proposed antenna unit and decoupling array offer compelling solutions for enabling reliable wireless communications in smart vehicles, facilitating technologies such as vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication, in-vehicle networks, and telematics systems. The findings contribute to the development of intelligent transportation systems and the seamless integration of cutting-edge wireless technologies into the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis on Three Methods of Quartz Crystal Resonator Frequency Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The traditional methods for testing the frequency of quartz crystal resonators include the indirect calculation method, signal source oscillation method, and network analyzer method. Each of the three methods has major defects. According to the characteristics of the frequency of quartz crystal resonators, this paper proposes three new test methods: oscilloscope test method, frequency meter test method, and spectrum analyzer test method. These three methods differ in basic test principles, equipment configuration requirements, test accuracy, and applicable environment. This paper makes a detailed comparison of the advantages and disadvantages of these three methods, and puts forward selection suggestions for different application conditions: if you only want to measure the frequency of the quartz crystal resonator, use the spectrum analyzer test method, if you need to measure the frequency and also need to know the characteristics of the frequency, it is advisable to use the frequency meter test method. The oscilloscope test method can be used for qualitative and rough measurement of the frequency of the quartz crystal resonator. In addition, the possibility of instrument collaborative testing is also discussed based on their respective advantages.

articleTitle: Fault Set Pre-Screening Method Based on Greedy Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The pre-screening method is essential to the power grid reliability assessment. However, the traditional screening method has low efficiency and a high probability of missing severe faults with high frequency, adversely affecting the assessment accuracy. Therefore, based on the probabilistic graph and the improved greedy algorithm (IGA), this paper proposes a new pre-screening method to accelerate the first <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> faults that are most likely to occur. Firstly, the fault index is applied to describe the operation reliability of power grid components. Then, based on the load-shedding ratio (LSR) and the pre-ratio (PR), the greedy algorithm is improved to generate the fault set. The RTS 79 and RTS 96 test systems are applied to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved State Transition Simulated Annealing Algorithm was Used to Solve CVRP
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To overcome the shortcomings of the standard state transition simulated annealing gorithm (STASA) falling into local optimum easily and lack of searching ability in solving capacity-constrained vehicle path planning (CVRP), an improved state transition simulated annealing algorithm called state transition simulated annealing gorithm-2opt +(STASA-2opt+) is proposed. Firstly, an initial solution sequence is randomly generated, and then a redefined 2-opt+ operator is introduced on the basis of the exchange, symmetry and transformation operators of STASA to expand the search space of candidate solutions. At the same time, the newly defined external optimal solution set is introduced and the acceptance strategy of the solution is changed to prevent falling into local optimum. Finally, the experimental results of STASA-2opt+ and STASA in international benchmark examples are compared and analysed. The results indicate that STASA-2opt+ can effectively get out of local optimal solution and improve the quality of the solution, and has certain advantages in solving medium-sized CVRP. In the calculation example P-n55-k8, STASA-2opt+ gets a better solution compared with the official optimal solution, and has a decrease of 1.7% than the official optimal solution.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Stochastic Approximation Consensus Algorithms on Directed Matrix-Weighted Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper introduces one stochastic approximation consensus type algorithm for discrete-time multi-agent systems (MASs) under general matrix-weighted topologies. By analyzing the consensus error convergence, we establish one sufficient condition for achieving asymptotic unbiased mean-square consensus.

articleTitle: Robust Extended Kalman Filter for Graphical Nonlinear Systems with Hybrid Cyber-Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper studies the extended Kalman filtering for graphical nonlinear systems with hybrid cyber-attacks. The considered system states and measurement outputs are generated based on graph structures, and the measurement signals are subject to denial-of-service attacks and deception attacks. In order to improve the filtering performance of graphical nonlinear systems subjected to hybrid cyber-attacks, we design an extended Kalman filter with a diagonal gain matrix in the graph frequency domain by means of the graph Fourier transform. The diagonal form of the gain matrix allows the states of each node to be updated independently, thus reducing the iterative accumulation error. Further, we introduce higher-order terms in the first-order Taylor expansion of the nonlinear function to compensate for the linearization error. Finally, we obtain the diagonal Kalman gain matrix by solving two Riccati-like equations. A simulation example on a power system validates the superior performance of the proposed filter against hybrid cyber-attacks.

articleTitle: FOC Brushless Knob Interactive Farm TCP Remote Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The product is a low-cost innovative interactive environment parameter detection device, and equipped with the corresponding computer. Using TCP communication protocol, FOC brushless control, LVGL graphics library and other technologies, we finally produced a complete set of software and hardware systems that can collect the current farm environment parameters in real time, achieve hardware control interaction and remote data summary of computer computer through color screen and brushless motor display.

articleTitle: Real-time Detection and Recognition of Railway Traffic Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the freight railway system, the automatic detection and identification of traffic signals is of extreme importance. In this paper, we conduct an in-depth study on deep learning detection algorithm for railway signals, and propose an algorithm to detect the railway signals based on the improved YOLOv5. The Ghost convolution is used to replace the original convolution, and the bottleneck module in the GhostNet network is introduced into the C3 module of the original network. Besides, a heuristic method is used to identify the blinking state of traffic signals. The model is trained using the FRSign dataset. The trained network has a low computational burden and is capable of recognising traffic signals in real-time under a variety of conditions.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Delayed Neural Networks via Self-Triggered Impulsive Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of asymptotic synchronization in delayed neural networks (DNNs) by designing a rational self-triggered impulsive control (STIC) strategy. By applying a Razumikhin-like comparison lemma, the presence of time delays in the system is considered, and a self-triggered mechanism (STM) is formulated to determine the impulsive interval based on the previous impulsive moment. Utilizing the developed STIC strategy, a set of sufficient conditions for achieving asymptotic synchronization of DNNs is established, with a proof ensuring the exclusion of the Zeno phenomenon. Compared to the event-triggered impulsive control (ETIC) strategy, this STIC strategy offers an advantage by predicting the next impulse occurrence based on the previous impulsive instant and available information, eliminating the need for continuous system state monitoring to verify triggering conditions. This strategy reduces communication costs and enhances resource utilization.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Multidimensional Spacecraft Telemetry via an Integrated K-Means, VAE and SVDD Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by multidimensional, heavily imbalanced samples and the scarcity of labeled data in spacecraft telemetry anomaly detection, a data-driven anomaly detection approach that integrates clustering, Variational Autoencoder (VAE), and Support Vector Data Description (SVDD) is proposed. Initially, the data are clustered using the K-means algorithm based on the spacecraft's work mode. Then, VAE is employed to learn the latent distribution of each cluster's data, resulting in a latent space representation that encapsulates the inherent features of the original data. Subsequently, the reconstruction error of the VAE is calculated, and the SVDD algorithm is utilized to jointly detect anomalies in both the latent space feature learned by the VAE and the reconstruction errors. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can effectively detect anomalies in multidimensional telemetry data, achieving high accuracy of 97.12% and high recall rates of 99.29%. This provides robust support for the safe and reliable operation of spacecraft.

articleTitle: Design of Simulation and Evaluation System for Safety Operation in High Energy Radiation Scene Based on SysML
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the emergence and wide application of new energy sources and technologies, various high-energy radiation devices have become indispensable core facilities and play an important role. At present, there are not only a large number of high-energy radiation devices in service, but also many have been or will enter the decommissioning stage. Aiming at the uncertainty and fuzziness of the traditional safety evaluation methods in the maintenance and decommissioning of high-energy radiation equipment, this paper designs the algorithms of task allocation, path planning and safety ergonomics evaluation for high-energy radiation equipment. Based on the system modeling language, the rationality of the system control flow is verified, and a simulation evaluation system for high-energy radiation equipment is developed to realize the comprehensive evaluation of safety operation schemes.

articleTitle: A Study of Stochastic Radiation Sources Based on Metasurfaces and Vortex Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, a stochastic radiation source design method applicable to microwave staring correlated imaging (MSCI) is proposed. Utilizing the electromagnetic meta-surface's ability to modulate electromagnetic waves and the mode-orthogonal characteristics of vortex electromagnetic waves, a vortex radiation source based on the super-surface is designed, and its ability to generate stochastic radiation fields (SRFS) is verified by numerical simulation from the perspectives of both single vortex radiation modes and mixed vortex radiation modes. Finally, simulated imaging is carried out using the above two forms of radiation source respectively, which proves its feasibility for MSCI and the effectiveness of this design method.

articleTitle: E2F2: End-to-End Feature-Free Network for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the development of new energy technologies, such as solar and wind power, lithium-ion batteries are being widely used for energy storage and distribution. The State-of-Health (SOH) is very important for the safety and reliability of battery applications. However, existing SOH prediction methods usually require health feature extraction for model training, which limits the coherence and reliability of SOH prediction. To deal with this issue, we propose an End-to-End Feature-Free network (E2F2). The proposed model is an end-to-end neural network model that combines convolutional and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures to process raw battery data, effectively capturing both spatial and temporal dependencies without relying on pre-defined features, thus simplifying modeling and enhancing adaptability. Experimental results on a real dataset illustrate the high accuracy and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Real-Time Urban Rainfall-Runoff Prediction Using Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Accurate and real-time urban rainfall-runoff prediction (URRP) provides an effective approach which can be used for multiple subsequent tasks such as flood risk assessment, operational response, and resilience planning etc. In recent years, the emerging data-driven model has shown its potential to achieve promising performance on rainfall-runoff prediction. However, the conventional methods still cannot achieve the excellent performance. Thus, we are motivated to use recurrent neural network (RNN) for data-driven modeling to achieve excellent performance. In this paper, RNN is employed to achieve the real-time URRP task. We conduct the experiments on real-world data set, being collected from (Jan. 2018 to Dec. 2019) a complex terrain of 3.52 km2 in Chong Qing, China. The experimental results demonstrate that RNN-based model outperforms not only conventional machine learning, but also other basic deep learning ones.

articleTitle: Model-Based Cross-Scale Reinforcement Learning Optimal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A model-based cross-scale reinforcement learning optimal control method is proposed for a class of nonlinear singularly perturbed systems. Initially, according to the singular perturbation theory, the original singularly perturbed system is decomposed into fast and slow subsystems, thereby transforming the original optimal control problem into optimal control problems for the fast and slow subsystems. A cross-scale information interaction mechanism is proposed, where full-order system state data is sampled to update the initial values of the fast and slow subsystems. This approach helps overcome the limitations associated with the online solving of rigid equations and reduce the cumulative errors. To approximate the solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations for the fast and slow subsystems, neural networks (NNs) are employed to approximate the cost functions within iterative processes. Simulation resultst validated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Implementation and Application of Solvers for Simulation and Execution of Control Algorithms in NCSLab
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of high dependency and low flexibility caused by calling three-party services during simulation and experiments, this paper uses the NCSLab (Networked Control System Laboratory) as an application platform to implement the functions of multiple ordinary differential equation solvers, which are used for real-time simulation and experimentation of control algorithm. This paper mainly integrates the common ordinary differential equation solving methods and NCSLab platform, and verifies the support of NCSLab platform for different solving methods through the actual simulation process.

articleTitle: LQR Control of Two-Wheeled Self-Balancing Vehicle Based on ARX Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of inaccurate parameters of the mechanism model of the two-wheeled self-balancing car, the ARX model was selected to describe the dynamic characteristics of the object near the working point, the modeling method based on system identification technology was studied, and the one-step prediction error and long-term prediction error were used as performance indicators, and the modeling performance of the mechanism model was compared, and the LQR control strategy based on the ARX model was designed, and compared with the double closed-loop control strategy based on PID control. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed modeling and control scheme are verified in real-time control.

articleTitle: Repeater Jamming Delay Updating Method Under Error Influence
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: When multiple UAVs implement track deception jamming on networked radar, the actual track of UAVs will be affected by the natural environment to produce position errors. When the disturbance persists, it is difficult to compensate the errors quickly only by flight control system. In order to enable multiple UAVs to form enough false tracks which can pass the homologous detection by networked radar during the adjustment process, this paper analyzes the effect of VAV position error on track deception jamming from the theoretical level, then proposes the method of delay update based on particle swarm optimization algorithm, and constructs the homologous detection method of networked radar based on spatial resolution unit criteria, and last verifies the effect of the delay updating. The simulation results show that after updating the delay through the algorithm proposed in this paper, the false track distance difference generated by the UAVs during track adjustment due to environmental disturbance can meet the requirement of distance resolution, and then pass the homologous detection.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Attention Mechanism Hot Spot Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To solve the problems of scarcity of hot spot image data and insufficient feature extraction of photovoltaic modules, a multi-channel attention mechanism hot spot detection algorithm based on YOLOv5 is proposed. The hybrid data augmentation method of grid masking and image elastic deformation is used to effectively expand the data of a small number of existing hot spot datasets, while the multi-channel attention mechanism is used to interact with cross-latitude information to obtain the features of hot spot images. The average precision 50 (AP50) of the improved algorithm is improved by 1.17% compared to the baseline model YOLOv5, and its inference speed reaches 100.12 frames/s. It is demonstrated through attentional ablation experiments that capturing the interaction between channel attentions is important for improving the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: MRI Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation Based on 3D Global Attention Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Stroke is a prevalent cerebrovascular disease that causes motor impairments, cognitive deficits, and language problems, and is the second leading cause of death globally. Accurate measurement of affected brain regions post-stroke is crucial for effective rehabilitation treatment. Manual delineation and quantification of stroke lesions in MR images by radiologists are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, research into automatic stroke lesion segmentation is of great significance. Although deep learning-based segmentation techniques have made progress, model performance still needs improvement. This paper presents a stroke lesion segmentation approach based on a 3D Global Feature Attention Convolutional Neural Network (3D GFA-UNet). The 3D Global Feature Attention module enhances segmentation performance by capturing long-term dependencies and global contextual information. Tested on the ATLAS v2.0 dataset and compared with three advanced deep learning networks, the 3D GFA-UNet has achieved average Dice and IoU scores of 0.6125 and 0.4898, respectively.

articleTitle: An $8\times 1$ GS/s Time-Interleaved ADC Model and Background Calibration for Mismatch
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article presents a TIADC model based on Verilog-AMS with the sub-ADC adopting pipeline ADC. The TIADC has 8 channels with a single-channel sampling rate of 1GS/s and a total sampling rate of 8GS/s with 12-bit resolution. It also completed the calibration of the offset mismatch, gain mismatch and timing skew. The paper uses iterative averaging algorithm for offset and gain calibration. With 2us calibration SNDR and SFDR can be improved by more than 20dB.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Suppression in Circular MIMO Array Imaging Based on the Partial Equivalence Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel approach for circular multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array imaging, termed the Partial Equivalence-based Method (PEM), specifically aimed at sidelobe reduction. The circular MIMO array can be decomposed into bistatic single-input single-output (SISO) arrays with varying angles separation between the transmitter and receiver, denoted as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{TR}$</tex>. In traditional MIMO equivalence approaches, each pair of transmitting and receiving elements is treated as an equivalent channel. However, the wavenumber spectra of equivalent channels with larger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{TR}$</tex>, are concentrated near zero frequency, leading to increased sidelobe levels when integrated into the MIMO imaging output. Consequently, this paper implements the Partial Equivalence Method (PEM) to restrict the scope of equivalent channels. This approach selectively preserves only the equivalent channels where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{TR}$</tex> falls within a predetermined threshold, effectively alleviating the detrimental impacts associated with large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{TR}$</tex> components. Through point target simulations and electromagnetic simulations, this paper demonstrated the PEM can effectively reduce sidelobes and enhance image quality in circular MIMO arrays imaging. The findings have significant implications for enhancing the application of circular MIMO arrays in security screening, medical imaging, and beyond.

articleTitle: Research on Maneuvering Target Tracking Algorithm with Adaptive Turning Rate Based on Dynamics Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Stable tracking of maneuvering targets is widely applied in the aerospace field. In this paper, an adaptive single-model maneuvering target tracking algorithm based on aircraft dynamics model is proposed. Firstly, the algorithm evaluates the real-time maneuvering overload characteristics of the target according to the historical state of the target and obtains the real-time spatial motion plane and turning rate of the target. Then, the complex maneuvers of the target in the ground coordinate system are transformed into turning maneuvers in the moving plane, and the extended Kalman filter is carried out in the moving plane coordinate system. Finally, the state estimation of the target in the ground coordinate system is obtained by coordinate transformation. In this paper, the tracking performance of the proposed algorithm is tested through the typical S-maneuver of the target. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has strong adaptability and high tracking accuracy with simple model, and can output the real-time maneuvering characteristics of the target, which can guide the subsequent target behavior prediction and intention recognition and has important engineering application value.

articleTitle: A Wide-Range Delay Lock Loops for Pipelined ADCs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Traditional clock units, predicated on inverter delay lines, are constrained and often inadequate for the demands of high-precision analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This paper introduces a novel wide-range, low-power Delay-Locked Loop (DLL) tailored for pipelined ADCs, designed using a 152 nm CMOS process. The proposed DLL features a dual-path delay unit that modulates the output signal's delay time through the dynamic control of a charging and discharging mechanism. This innovation significantly expands the operational frequency range of the delay line and ensures precise control over the delay period. Simulation results indicate that the DLL operates efficiently within a broad spectrum of 170 MHz to 630 MHz under a 1.8V supply voltage. Notably, with an input reference clock signal at 500 MHz, the DLL achieves an impressive peak-to-peak jitter of 1.16 ps and a low power consumption of 1.54 mW. This advanced DLL is capable of generating the requisite five-phase clock for pipelined ADCs, adeptly fulfilling their stringent operational requirements.

articleTitle: Analysis and Validation of Medium-Long Wave Remote Transmission Channels using Vertical Electric Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Medium-long wave exhibit distinct advantages over shortwave communication, including a stable signal channel, robust resistance to nuclear explosions, extended transmission range, and the ability to penetrate seawater and geological layers. The efficiency of traditional medium-long wave transmission is hampered by the use of horizontal or buried antennas as transmitters, significantly impacting the signal's transmission range. In this paper, base on the high power characteristics radiated by the vertical antenna, the attenuation properties of medium-long wave signals generated by ground-based vertical antennas within the transmission channel are analyzed using wave-hop theory, and the long-distance transmission capacity of this mode based on the ambient electromagnetic noise levels is evaluated. Concurrently, experimental validation is conducted to verify the accuracy of the channel model. This new antenna transmitting method can greatly improve the transmission distance of medium-long wave signal.

articleTitle: Distributed resilient Nash equilibrium seeking for second-order MAS subject to intermittent DoS attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper considers the problem of distributed Nash equilibrium (NE) seeking for second-order multi-agent systems under intermittent denial of service (DoS) attacks. Based on the local state information of neighboring agents and the gradient play, a Nash equilibrium seeking algorithm is designed for second-order multi-agent systems (MAS). It is proved that the distributed NE seeking of switching topologies under intermittent communication constraints can be realized when the average dwell time of the topology satisfies a certain switching condition. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation example.

articleTitle: Multi-Period Day-Ahead Storage Scheduling with Uncertain Inflow
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the widespread integration of renewable energy into the power grid, the inherent variability and intermittency of renewable sources can compromise grid reliability and security. Traditional deterministic approaches fall short in addressing this challenge, while uncertainty optimization methods offer a more effective solution. This paper addresses the water inflow uncertainty in the day-ahead storage scheduling. By leveraging the multiplicative autoregressive method, a multi-period stochastic programming model is established to minimize the expected daily operating cost. Then, a stochastic dual dynamic programming algorithm is devised to find the optimal generation dispatching strategy. Finally, case studies on the IEEE 30-bus systems are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: An Orthogonal X- Junction Detector Based on Local Periodicity
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: An adaptive method to detect the location of the orthogonal X- junction is presented in the paper. The correlation between the candidate point and the junction center can be measured quantitatively based on the periodical pixel distribution around the junction, and the junction detection is translated into searching local maximum or centroid. The proposed method is feasible and insensitive to the junction orientation, the arm thickness and the noise. The chessboard corner detection can also be implemented by the proposed method. Example images are provided in the paper to show the validity and reliability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Online Evaluation of Communication Interference Effectiveness Based on CRITIC-AHP
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of online evaluation of the communication interference effect, an online evaluation method of the multi-attribute communication interference effect based on subjective and objective weights is proposed. In this paper, various communication behavior parameters are selected as interference effect evaluation indicators from the perspective of transmitter anti-jamming. The Criteria Importance Through Inter-criteria Correlation, CRITIC) and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) determine the objective and subjective weights and combine the two to determine the final weights. The interference effect is judged according to the degree of change of each indicator parameter before and after the interference. At the same time, to objectively reflect the degree of parameter variation, the anti-jamming ability of the modulation style is numerically calculated. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively reflect the interference effect and still has stable performance in the case of small samples.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Method of Rotating Machinery Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Precise diagnosis of faults is the key to maintaining rotating machinery. Traditional fault diagnosis methods face several challenges, such as the need for manual feature extraction, difficulty in fully exploring nonlinear features, and low accuracy in noisy environments. To address these issues, this paper introduces a multi-scale fault diagnosis model called GA-Res-LSTM, which integrates the Ghost Module and attention mechanism, and incorporates residual connections in the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. This model leverages an enhanced ghost module to automatically and adaptively extract multiscale features from the original signal. The attention mechanism assigns weights to these features, focusing the model on the most critical ones. Subsequently, feature learning and enhancement are performed using residual connected LSTM networks. The Global Average Pooling (GAP) method is employed to mitigate overfitting, leading to effective fault classification of rotating machinery through the fully connected (Fc) layer. The results from our experiments indicate that the proposed method can attain high diagnostic performances in low Signal-To-Noise Ratio (SNR) environments with small operating costs. The recognition accuracy of the network under resource-constrained conditions is guaranteed.

articleTitle: Unaligned Multispectral UAV Object Detection Algorithm Research
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: UAV targets, due to their concealment and flexibility, have important applications in fields such as military reconnaissance and border surveillance, and also pose potential threats to air safety and public security. This paper addresses the detection problem of such targets by proposing an algorithm based on unaligned multispectral imagery. Firstly, an in-depth analysis of existing detection technologies was conducted to identify the technical difficulties and challenges in target detection. Then, combining the characteristics of multispectral imagery, a feature-level fusion strategy was proposed. By using a deep learning model, the information from visible light and infrared was effectively integrated, enhancing the performance of target detection.

articleTitle: Adaptive Containment Control for Nonlinear P-Normal Multiagent Systems with Sensor Failures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper considers the adaptive containment control problem for a class of nonlinear p-normal multiagent systems (MASs) with sensor failures and unknown time-varying parameters. Unlike the structural features of existing results, the dynamic of each agent is a power exponential function. By using an approach called adding a power integrator technique, the problem of power exponential terms being positive odd in p-normal MASs has been solved. Then, a novel control scheme is proposed to resolve sensor failures by using Nussbaum gain technology. Additionally, the fuzzy logic system is utilized to handle the impact of unknown time-varying parameters. In view of the backstepping technique, all signals of the system are demonstrated to be bounded. A simulation example is obtained to evidence the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Spike Neural Network with Delayed Propagation Characteristics and Hardware Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Spike neural networks, as mathematical models for simulating biological neurons, have received high attention in the fields of life sciences and artificial intelligence due to their biological rationality and hardware friendliness in working mechanisms. However, the discrete signal form of pulse neurons makes them non differentiable and unable to propagate backwards. This paper proposes a delayed propagation pulse neuron model to solve this issue. This model operates on the long-term characteristics of pulse neurons, by treating the effect of pulse signals on neurons as a continuous charging current to achieve signal continuity and thus obtain differentiable characteristics, achieving backpropagation. At the same time, the use of capacitance charging models to construct low-cost neuron hardware circuits provides a new development direction for brain-like computing hardware.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Nonlinear Multiagent Formation Obstacle Avoidance Controller Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, the formation problem of double-integral multiagent systems with unknown nonlinear dynamics is studied. Considering that there may be obstacles in the operating environment of the agent, a formation obstacle avoidance controller is designed with the help of artificial potential field. The good approximation performance of radial basis function neural network is used to eliminate the influence of unknown nonlinear dynamics on the controller design. Based on Lyapunov stability theory, it is proved that the proposed formation control method can make all signals in the closed loop system uniformly bounded. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy and the feasibility of formation obstacle avoidance are verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Radar Pulse Stream Deinterleaving Based on Interpretable Spiking Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Radar pulse stream deinterleaving is an important part of electronic support measurement (ESM). However, most of the existing pulse stream deinterleaving methods can only run offline and have poor adaptability to data noise. In this paper, I have developed an interpretable spiking neural network to solve the problem of online deinterleaving of radar pulse streams under severe data noise conditions. Firstly, the PRI pattern information of the target radar is obtained from the database, and then the PRI pattern is loaded into the synaptic connection delay of the interpretable spiking neural network. In the process of continuous input of pulse stream, the pulse substream conforming to the correct pattern makes the voltage of the spiking neuron accumulate continuously. When the voltage of the goal spiking neuron exceeds the threshold, the corresponding radar pulse is successfully deinterleaving. For data noise such as the spurious pulse, the voltage caused by it gradually decays because it does not conform to the delay pattern of the proposed SNN. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prescribed Performance Optimal Control for Flexible-Joint Robots with Random Noises
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, an optimal control algorithm is designed for flexible joint (FJ) robot system with random noise. The reinforcement learning strategy based on identifier structure is designed by using neural network approximation. The identifier aims to compensate the unknown dynamic. The prescribed performance function is introduced simultaneously in the control design of the system. The error is confined to the set area. To reduce the amount of computation, the adaptive backstepping design takes use of dynamic surface control. It is very effective in reducing the amount of computation. Besides, the suggest ed approach can guarantee that the tracking error converges to a small neighborhood of the origin. Finally, the effectiveness of the designed control method proved by F J robot example.

articleTitle: A 380 GHz Waveguide-to-suspended Microstrip Line Transition Structure Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Waveguide-planar transmission line transition structure is widely utilized in millimeter-wave and terahertz bands, which is one of the most important signal transmission paths. This paper presents the design of a 380 GHz waveguide-suspended microstrip line transition structure. Additionally, the air cavity of the suspended microstrip line is improved to meet the terahertz band package support problem, making it more conducive to the protection of the core circuit substrate. A height- reduced waveguide combined with a segment of high and low impedance matching line yields the optimal impedance matching effect. The whole structure is assembled on a 30-micron-thick quartz substrate. According to the simulation results, the return loss reaches below -31dB at the center frequency point of 380 GHz and is better than -20dB in 358–403 GHz, enabling broadband transmission at 45 GHz. The length of the whole structure is only 0.96 mm, with compact size and high simulation performance, which could be widely used in terahertz communication systems and provide a useful reference for future frequency band research.

articleTitle: Improved PRF Design Method for High-Speed Maneuvering-Platform SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: When the high-speed maneuvering-platform synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is used for long-range imaging, the antenna elevation beam covers a large range of ground echoes, leading to a small PRF upper limit, while the large azimuth signal Doppler bandwidth caused by the high-speed motion of the platform results in a large PRF lower limit. This situation may cause the lower limit of the PRF to exceed the upper limit, making PRF design impossible. To tackle this problem, an improved design method of the PRF lower limit is proposed. Simulation results show that the proposed method for high-speed maneuvering SAR imaging can effectively extend the range of PRF selection and better meet the need of practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Research on Abnormal Detection for Wireless Communication Network based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Communication anomaly identification is a key research area in communication network security. In wireless communication networks, node behavior analysis based on listening technology and statistical detection technology has the shortcomings of high energy consumption, sensitivity to network topology and environmental changes, insufficient data and malicious attacks. In this work, we start by generating data sequences of network behavior under normal and abnormal conditions. We then input the data series into the recurrent neural network (RNN) model for training. During training, the RNN model learns patterns of normal network behavior in order to identify anomalous behaviors subsequently. Once the model is trained, we can use it to predict whether a new data series is normal or an anomaly. When the model's predictions for a new data series are inconsistent with the actual situation, we can flag it as an anomaly. We divide the dataset into a training set and a test set, and usually use cross-validation or retention methods to ensure the reliability of the experiment. Then, we input the training set into the RNN model for training, and use the test set for model evaluation.

articleTitle: Offline Handwritten Signature Verification using Siamese Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Offline handwritten signatures constitute one of the most prevalent and universally recognized identifiers within the domains of biometrics and document forensics. They are routinely employed for daily attendance tracking, credit card authorization, and the authentication of business agreements to confirm individual identities. The task of offline signature verification remains formidable due to the intricacies involved in distinguishing subtle yet critical variations between authentic and expertly forged signatures. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces a two-stage Siamese network framework for offline handwritten signature verification. It incorporates an advanced spatial transformation module that autonomously emphasizes the features indicative of handwriting style for more accurately capturing the unique handwriting characteristics of target signature. Furthermore, the Focal loss function is adopted to address the significant imbalance between positive and negative signature samples prevalent in most contemporary datasets. Experimental results on four real-world handwritten signature datasets in various languages demonstrate that our proposed model surpasses state-of-the-art approaches in verification accuracy.

articleTitle: Estimation of RoA for Nonlinear Systems Based on Gaussian Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper employs Gaussian Processes (GPs) to estimate uncertainty dynamics inherent in nonlinear systems. A control policy ensuring the system satisfies initial stability constraints is derived using linear quadratic regulator (LQR). By modeling the Lyapunov function based on uncertain dynamics as GPs, the stability of the system dynamics in the Lyapunov sense is ensured. To discretize the Lyapunov function with Lipschitz continuity, a finite number of discrete points are chosen to represent the properties of the function. The region of attraction (RoA) based on Lyapunov function is widely utilized as a safe constraint in the field of control. Additionally, the maximum uncertainty dynamics are chosen as the boundary for exploration to expand the evaluation of the RoA. Finally, a simulation example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Analytical Solar Radiation Pressure Model for a GEO Large Antenna Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Large space antenna satellites, as representative large space structures, exhibit complex dynamic characteristics under space environmental perturbations due to their unique configurations, affecting operational stability. To investigate the impact of solar radiation pressure perturbations, this study employs an advanced orbital prediction algorithm. Addressing the unique configurations and variable area-to-mass ratios of these satellites, an high-precision analytical solar radiation pressure model was proposed. This model optimizes the calculation of perturbation forces and accurately derives the relationship between area-to-mass ratio and solar incidence angle. Comparative simulations with a macro-model method verified the method's accuracy and effectiveness. The model also precisely calculates perturbation torque for complex antenna structures. This high-precision model enhances the understanding of large space antenna satellites' dynamics and provides critical support for orbit and attitude control.

articleTitle: Motor PCB Defect Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7-tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to accurately and efficiently detect various defects that may occur in the production process of motor PCB (Printed Circuit Board), a motor PCB defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv7-tiny is proposed. MobileNetV3-Small is used as the backbone and combined with the structural re-parameterization method to achieve a model that significantly improves the inference speed and reduces the consumption of computing resources while maintaining high detection accuracy. By introducing the α-SIoU loss function and adaptively adjusting the weight factor to optimize the model's detection performance for defects of different sizes and complexity, the model's robustness and accuracy are effectively improved under complex backgrounds and changing defect shapes. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv7-tiny model has a mAP of 91.33% on the motor PCB defect detection task, while greatly reducing the FLOPs and parameter amount of the model. Compared with existing lightweight detection algorithms such as YOLOv3- tiny, YOLOv5n, etc., show superior detection accuracy and operating efficiency.

articleTitle: A Tunable Frequency Relaxation Oscillator for DC-DC Switching Power Supply Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: DC-DC switching power supply driver chips applied to the power supply systems of various electronic products require high-performance oscillators. Based on this requirement, this paper designs a tension oscillator with wide frequency modulation range and high accuracy. The oscillator is based on the 0.18μmBCD process library, using Cadence software in the chip system under the typical application environment simulation, the typical oscillation frequency of 991kHz, through the setting of peripheral resistors can be adjusted to the frequency range of 300kHz ∼ 2.5MHz; in the temperature range of -5O °C to 120 °C, the rate of change of frequency is 1.7%; in the 3.5V to 6V The frequency variation rate is 0.8% in the supply voltage range of 3.5V to 6V. Simulation results show that the oscillator performs well and is suitable for DC-DC switching power supplies.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Dense U-Shaped Network for Efficient Infrared Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Infrared small target detection is a fundamental task in object detection and is crucial for infrared search and tracking systems. Currently, most infrared small target recognition technologies employ deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to construct models, incorporating attention mechanisms to enhance multi-scale feature fusion and improve detection accuracy. As network structures become more complex, the large number of model parameters demands higher computational power. However, the application scenarios for infrared small target recognition are often in vehicle-mounted, airborne, or even satellite-borne environments, which have significant limitations on computational resources. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lightweight improved dense U-shaped network based on the Dense Nested Attention Network (DNA-Net). The Group Multi-axis Hadamard Product Attention (GHPA) module is introduced to optimize the backbone network structure. This simplification of the dense network model maintains detection accuracy while reducing the number of parameters and the complexity of the model, improving the time cost of model training and inferencing. Through comparative experiments, the proposed lightweight improved dense U-shaped network has been validated on open-source datasets, demonstrating that it maintains recognition accuracy while reducing computational and time costs.

articleTitle: STYOLOv8: Research on Traffic Signal Light Detection Method Based on SwinTransformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Traffic light detection is widely used in the field of automatic driving. This paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 object detection method based on SwinTransformer, which combines Transformer to realize global feature extraction and reconstruction of images, enhances feature extraction through self-attention mechanism, and combines YOLOv8‘s efficient detection framework. An object detection system with high performance and high computational efficiency is realized. Through testing on traffic signal data set, the experimental results show that the proposed method achieves remarkable results in both accuracy and precision.

articleTitle: Finite-Iteration Learning Control for Nonlinear Systems with Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: For most of the existing iterative learning control (ILC) results, the tracking of the target trajectory is achieved asymptotically as the iteration number tends to infinity. In this study, a finite-iteration learning control (FILC) strategy is proposed to achieve the accurate tracking of trajectory in a finite iteration number. As the first study of FILC, a linear parameterized system with parameter uncertainties is considered in this article. To eliminate the influence of unknown parameters, we first design a parameter update law. The true value of the unknown parameter is estimated in a finite iteration number by using the proposed parameter update law. Then, with the help of the true value of unknown parameter, a novel fractional-power structure control law with a iteration-varying control gain is designed. Under the proposed FILC scheme, the tracking of target trajectory is achieved in a finite-iteration number. The computation method of the iteration number is given. Illustrative examples are provided to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Communication IP Core Based on CAN Bus Encryption and Authentication
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The emergence of intelligent connected vehicles has brought great convenience to people's travel, but the safety risks that come with it cannot be ignored. This article proposes a hardware based solution to address potential risks. This scheme designs an IP core with initialization and updating of encryption keys, plaintext encryption, and authentication functions. This IP core encrypts transmitted messages using the national security SM4 algorithm in CFB (Cipher Feedback) mode and adds integrity verification codes to endow the onboard CAN bus with the ability to resist replay attacks without changing the existing communication protocol.

articleTitle: Key Technologies Research of Hubless Rim-driven Thurster for Deep-sea Vehicles based on Mutidisciplinary Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Achieving high motion performance is crucial for ensuring the successful operation of both manned and unmanned submersibles in the underwater environment. The submersible's design is a critical factor for optimizing its motion, reducing resistance, and enhancing the efficiency of its thruster. In comparison to traditional thrusters, rim-hubless thrusters employ a multi-paddle ring-drive structure that reduces wingtip vortex in the flow field, thereby minimizing cavitation vibration noise and preventing underwater cable entanglement. As a result, this design significantly enhances the operational safety of the submersible. Moreover, the rim-hubless thruster offers advantages such as high efficiency, reliability, low noise, and minimal vibration. This paper focuses on the design of a hubless deep-sea thruster, utilizing finite element analysis, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and electromagnetic design methods. The hubless propeller blades are meticulously calculated and determined, and the propeller's performance under various rotation conditions is simulated. Additionally, the optimization of motor parameters that match the hubless propeller is carried out. Furthermore, a magnetically coupled dynamic static sealing compensation structure is designed to meet the specific requirements of deep-sea applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Control of Satellite Formation Configuration Maintenance Under the Influence of Space Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article proposes a strategy for maintaining satellite formation configuration under the influence of space perturbations, which incorporates a non-singular terminal sliding mode controller on the basis of natural formation configuration designed for control. Firstly, considering the formation configuration drift caused by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>term perturbation and atmospheric drag perturbation, a satellite relative motion dynamics model coupled with perturbation forces is established to ensure its accuracy and reliability. Secondly, based on the design method of natural formation configuration, a non-singular terminal sliding mode controller is combined to achieve more accurate maintenance of satellite formation configuration. Finally, sufficient simulation analysis was provided to compare and verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Design of Small Omnidirectional Unmanned Surface Vehicle and Motion Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, an experimental platform for omnidirectional unmanned surface vessel (OUSV) with overdrive characteristics is introduced. When the four motors are operating, the normally unmanned ship can move horizontally in any direction in the horizontal plane. In the event of a motor failure or when required, it can be switched to a two-motor driven differential control mode to sail in the same way as a traditional underdriven vessel. In this paper, the motion control characteristics of the omnidirectional motion mode and differential control mode are studied from the aspects of motion modeling, platform design based on 3D printing, and control simulation. Finally, the corresponding heading angle control experiment and the path following experiment based on the improved LOS are designed, and the experimental results show that the control effect is in line with expectations.

articleTitle: Exponential Stability Conditions for Load Frequency Control With Multiple Delays Under Aperiodic Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In practical power system, load frequency control (LFC) system generally operate under sampling manner and transmission delays has a negative impact on LFC system. This paper investigates exponentially stable conditions for LFC system involving multiple delays under the sampling manner applying integral quadratic constraint analysis. Firstly, according to the derived discrete-time model of LFC system, a feedback inter-connection model of the linear system and uncertain operator is built. And then, considering exponential decay rate, inter-connection model of transformation is obtained. Next, applying integral quadratic constraint analysis, exponential stability with exponential decay rate is developed. Finally, numerical simulation is conducted to certify the advantage for the proposed conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Apriori Algorithm with BitSet Encoding and Hash Prefixes on Spark
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: As data volumes rapidly expand, traditional frequent itemset mining algorithms often face dual challenges of efficiency and scalability when processing large-scale datasets. This study introduces an improved Spark-Apriori algorithm implemented on the Apache Spark platform, which integrates adaptive bit length BitSet item encoding and hash prefix technology, aimed at enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of frequent itemset mining in big data environments. By introducing adaptive bit length BitSets, this algorithm dynamically adjusts encoding lengths based on the frequency of itemsets within the dataset, not only reducing memory consumption but also accelerating the data processing procedure. Simultaneously, the utilization of hash prefix technology optimizes the generation and filtering of candidate itemsets, significantly enhancing the data's parallel processing capabilities. Experimental results show that compared to the traditional Apriori algorithm, this algorithm demonstrates substantial performance improvements, particularly in scenarios with high data density and large numbers of itemsets. This research not only validates the potential of adaptive bit length BitSets and hash prefix technology in optimizing frequent itemset mining but also provides new perspectives and practical technological approaches for future research in big data mining.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Detection by Second Harmonic of Heartbeat Signal Based on UWB Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Ultra wideband (UWB) radar detects respiration rate (RR) and heart rate (HR) through chest movements caused by respiration and heartbeat. However, the heartbeat signal is easily interfered with because the heartbeat signal and the harmonics of respiratory signal are usually in similar frequency bands and the heartbeat signal strength is relatively weak. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a new HR detection method, in which multiple range bin signals are firstly selected to process them, and then analysed in combination with the variational modal decomposition (VMD) algorithm. The method indirectly achieves HR detection by detecting the second harmonic of the heartbeat signal, which solves the problem that the harmonics of the respiratory signal overlap with the frequency band of the heartbeat signal and are difficult to separate.

articleTitle: Radar-Based Human Activity Recognition Using Residual Network Model with Multi-Domain Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the field of radar-based human activity recognition, a large amount of research is conducted based on single-domain information, with insufficient utilization of multi-domain information. Based on this, this paper proposes a multi-domain information fusion network, integrating information from Range-time maps (RTM) and Doppler-time maps (DTM). Firstly, residual networks are used to extract features from the two domains separately, followed by feature-level fusion and convolutional processing. The classification results are obtained through two fully connected layers. Using this model can achieve richer feature representations through feature fusion, effectively improving the accuracy. The results demonstrate the improved accuracy of this model compared to other models, with an accuracy of 95.031% on the publicly available dataset from the University of Glasgow.

articleTitle: A Double Loop Based Low Dropout Linear Regulator Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper presents a double loop based LDO which has the ability to drive heavy load with large current and capacitance. A double-loop circuit has been implemented for the frequency compensation of the whole loop. Additionally, a carefully designed buffer circuit has been introduced to improve the loading capacity and to achieve high stability. The proposed LDO is implemented in a 0.35μm BCD process, achieving a phase margin of more than 35°to drive a large load capacitance range from 0 to 100μF and a large current load range from 1m to 3A under various PVT conditions.

articleTitle: An Epigraph Approach for Distributed Economic Dispatch in General Dynamic Directed Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The intricate complexities of modern energy systems highlight the cruciality of nimble and trustworthy methodologies for the smooth functioning of intelligent grids. This article delves into the economic dispatch problem (EDP) within smart grids, with the objective of maximizing generator scheduling efficiency to meet total demand while minimizing expenditure. We present a comprehensively decentralized algorithm, tailored specifically for addressing the EDP in directed networks, while accounting for the dynamics of communication environments. This algorithm integrates the epigraphic methodology and relies solely on row-stochastic weighting matrices for its execution. We provide theoretical justifications to ensure the convergence of our proposed algorithm, thereby exhibiting its ability to efficiently dispatch the optimal economic solution. To substantiate the efficacy of our algorithm, we conduct simulations, furnishing empirical proof of its performance.

articleTitle: Research on Activity Diagram Testing method based on UML Testing Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The correctness of the UML activity diagram itself is an important research content in the field of model-based testing. This article focuses on model-based testing of the model itself, elements of the UML activity diagram such as nodes, edges, and groups are formally defined. The activity diagram is used as the system under test (SUT) to build a UML model, and then the model is tested based on the UML Testing Profile (UTP). Similar to software testing, the testing process is divided into unit-level testing, integration-level testing, and system-level testing. The ATM example is used to demonstrate the activity diagram testing methodology based on UTP proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Enabling Digital Twin Using MEMS and Sensor Technology with Historic Data: From Data Fusion to Knowledge Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Microelectromechanical systems and Sensor Technology (MEMS-ST) can be used together with historical data to enable digital twins. This paper presents a novel framework that transitions from the data fusion of MEMS-ST to the knowledge fusion necessary for estimating the strength capacity of highway bridges. This innovative approach provides critical information for bridge design, transportation planning, and the assessment of existing pavement and infrastructure. The unique framework integrates real-time data from MEMS-ST systems installed on a bridge with historical records and engineering standards, addressing a significant gap in current methodologies. Through a comprehensive literature review, this study evaluates the existing reports and articles on developing bridge digital twins to measure live loads on highways. Utilizing datasets from sensors and the National Bridge Inventory, the proposed framework processes data based on the Load and Resistance Factor Design method and continuous multivariate probability distributions. The innovative application of the Dempster-Shafer Theory within the knowledge fusion framework distinguishes this work, enabling the combination of different sources (86, 126% increase) of evidence into a cohesive global belief. The results demonstrate that this framework can automate the analysis of vast amounts of data, improve efficiency (615,000 bridges in NBI and 93.1M truck data), and provide more reliable insights compared to traditional methods. Specifically, it enhances the safety and stability of bridge structures (Credibility 1.088; Plausibility 1.089) while offering new ways to design and maintain bridges more effectively. This paper sheds light on bridge digital twin systems.

articleTitle: GNSS Signal Acquisition Based on Compressive Sensing and Improved Measurement Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The main task of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver is to obtain satellite signals, but the signal acquisition operations performed in this process consume a large amount of hardware resources. Compressed sensing is a new signal sampling theory that can reduce the calculation amount of the acquisition process, but it will also bring a certain signal-to-noise ratio loss. In order to improve the acquisition performance on the basis of reducing the amount of signal acquisition calculations, this paper proposes an improved measurement matrix compressed sensing signal partial matched filter-fast Fourier transform (PMF -FFT) acquisition method, which improves the Gaussian random matrix through singular value decomposition and improves the incoherence of the measurement matrix. Simulation results show that this method significantly reduces the amount of acquisition calculations without greatly reducing the acquisition performance.

articleTitle: A Method for Malicious Encrypted Traffic Classification Based on Contrastive Pre-Training
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Malicious Encrypted Traffic Classification (METC) is a critical task in mobile internet management, aimed at detecting and identifying malicious activities to safeguard network security. With the large-scale and rapid proliferation of mobile applications (apps), the diversity and complexity of malicious traffic are continually increasing, posing significant challenges to traditional traffic classification methods. Researchers are increasingly focusing on learning-based approaches to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of METC. However, despite promising results, these methods still face two significant challenges in real-world network environments: the pervasive class imbalance problem and the reliance on a large amount of labeled data. We propose PMTC, a pre-training-based METC framework designed to effectively address these challenges. Our key insight is to reconstruct the initial traffic training set and subsequently conduct contrastive pre-training by increasing the proximity of positive traffic pairs together while creating distance between negative pairs, thereby avoiding the direct use of individual traffic sample labels. This approach not only improves classification accuracy but also maintains high performance in scenarios where data labeling is challenging. Extensive thorough experiments on multiple public datasets with imbalanced class distributions demonstrate that PMETC significantly achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. These results indicate PMETC has substantial potential and practical value in coping with the complex and dynamic network environments and in detecting malicious traffic.

articleTitle: 3D Weighths: Leveraging LKA-Embedded SimAM for Enhanced Mobile ViT in Rice Diseases Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the present research, we enhance the Mobile ViT model by integrating Large Kernel Attention (LKA) Convolution and SimAM Attention Mechanism, improving its global feature capture and attention to critical details. Our refined model outperforms the standard MobileViT by 2% in classifying rice leaf diseases, the size is 3.78MB, only 8KB larger than Mobile ViT. especially in handling diverse disease images, it surpasses the original model in seven out of 10 disease categories and matches its performance in the remaining 2, highlighting its robustness and versatility. This advancement significantly boosts the accuracy and effectiveness in identifying various rice leaf diseases.

articleTitle: Medical Ultrasound Image Denoising Based on Greedy Two-Dimensional Variational Mode Adaptive Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In medicine, dynamic frequency scanning adjusts operating frequencies based on target depth, yet ultrasound images often suffer from significant speckle noise, compromising imaging quality.
