Therefore, a novel denoising method for ultrasound images is proposed, which combines greedy two-dimensional Variational Mode Decomposition (2D-VMD) with the three-dimensional Block Matching and 3D Filtering algorithm (BM3D). Firstly, the parameters K of 2D-VMD are adaptively optimized using sample entropy and uncertainty, decomposing the image into sub-modes with different central frequencies. Subsequently, the high-frequency and low-frequency modes obtained after decomposition are subjected to denoising using the BM3D algorithm. Finally, the denoised sub-mode images are reconstructed after denoising. Extensive comparative experimental results indicate that this method significantly improves the denoising effectiveness of medical ultrasound images.

articleTitle: Online Test-Time Adaptation for Electronic Nose Drift Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Sensor drift is a common problem in E-nose systems. In recent years, research on this problem has made significant progress, and various drift compensation methods have emerged. Although these methods have achieved notable performance in recognition accuracy, they seldom deal with the drift problem in the online scenarios. Therefore, this paper proposes an E-nose drift compensation method based on online test-time adaptation. The method first removes abnormal data using data preprocessing methods to ensure the training quality of the model. Then uses a mutually learning teacher-student distillation model with continuous updates to adapt the model to drift data. The online recognition of unlabeled drift data is finally realized. The ability of the test-time adaptation (TTA) to adaptively adjust to the unlabeled drift data also makes the model highly robust and adaptable. Experimental results on public datasets show that the proposed method is effective enough to deal with the drift problem in the online case, and it also exhibits a high recognition rate compared to other state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Microwave Schottky Diode Electro-Thermal Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, an improved SPICE model for Schottky barrier diodes is developed by analyzing the characteristics of the diodes at different temperatures. The parameters reverse saturation current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_0)$</tex>, ideality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n)$</tex>, and series resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Rs)$</tex> are correlated with temperature to establish an electro-thermal model for Schottky diodes. The proposed model is applied to a simple shunt diode pre-distortion linearizer to verify the model's performance. Under an input power range of −25 dBm to 5 dBm, measurements show that the developed model exhibits higher accuracy in the S21 amplitude curve of the linearizer across different temperatures compared to the model provided by the manufacturer.

articleTitle: Spoofing Attack Detection in ADS-B Data Through Frequency Enhanced Patch Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the face of growing air traffic complexity and the escalating sophistication of cybersecurity threats, the centrality of Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) in air traffic control systems is undeniable, necessitating rigorous defense measures for its data due to the elevated security risks that can compromise the safety and efficiency of the airspace. To address these challenges, this paper proposed the Frequency Enhanced Patch Attention Network (FEPAN)-an advanced method built on the Transformer architecture and enriched with a novel frequency-based contextual enhancement specifically designed to expose anomalous patterns and activities within ADS-B data that conventional analyses might miss. Thoroughly tested against expansive ADS-B datasets featuring simulated deceptive maneuvers across diverse flight phases, our FEPAN methodology exhibits superior ability to pinpoint such intricacies with high accuracy, offering an indispensable tool for reinforcing the safeguarding of airspace operations.

articleTitle: Research on Legal Judgment Prediction with Multi-Task Learning and Causal Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the increasing attention to legal artificial intelligence, Legal Judgment Prediction has become a hot topic. The core objective is to automatically predict the final judgment outcome, which consists of three parts: relevant legal provisions, charges, and penalties, by analyzing the related information of the case. Most existing studies treat the prediction of the three parts as separate tasks, and few consider the logical relationships between the subtasks. Additionally, some studies only establish multi-task learning models from the perspective of shared features, which fails to fully leverage the consistency constraints among subtasks. Therefore, this paper proposes a method based on multi-task learning, considering the logical relationships between subtasks, aiming to deeply explore the relevance between subtasks and guide the model to perform interpretable reasoning. The experimental results have proven the effectiveness of the proposed method, and its comprehensive performance is superior to existing models.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fuzzy Fault-Tolerant Control for Robotic Arm with Sensor faults
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, the fault-tolerant control (FTC) problem of a single-link robotic arm (SLRA) with sensor faults is investigated. Fuzzy logic systems (FLSs) are exploited for approximating unknown nonlinearities. According to the introduce the specific auxiliary functions, the unknown coupling terms with uncertain parameters generated by sensor faults are solved effectually. Under the backstepping control framework, a fault-tolerant controller is constructed. Then, the stability of the closed loop system is proved via Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, a numerical simulation example is provided to further show the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Wide-Beam Radar Liquid Level Measurement Technology Based on MIMO Millimeter Wave Linear Array
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the effects of clutter interference points and level fluctuations in the industrial liquid storage tank environment on a non-contact wide-beam radar level measurement device. The proposed algorithm combines a MIMO uniform linear array and DOA estimation, aiming to eliminate the influence of interference points in the tank and to obtain accurate level information in real-time using an angle-amplitude-distance fusion processing system. The algorithm's effectiveness and theoretical analysis are evaluated using actual measurements from milk tanks. Designed level measurement devices with centimeter-level accuracy in tank environments. The data results show that the algorithm eliminates the limitation of the beam width on the radar level meter, which is essential for the application and promotion of low-cost and miniaturized radar level meter products.

articleTitle: Research on Safety Filling Control Device for Industrial Gas Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: According to the actual needs of safety management for industrial gas cylinder filling, a low-cost safety filling control scheme for industrial gas cylinders based on MQTT protocol was proposed. The embedded hardware and software of the safety filling control device for industrial gas cylinders was designed and developed. The solution and device had been piloted and applied in multiple industrial gas cylinder filling enterprises in Shandong Province. The practices indicate that this device can help industrial gas cylinder filling enterprises to achieve automation and digital safety management.

articleTitle: Development of Growth Control System for Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Plants Utilizing the Vector Fractal of Bezier Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The fractal dimension serves as a crucial metric for characterizing the complexity of fractal structures. Therefore, employing process control methodologies to analyze the intricate morphology of mycorrhizal fungi holds immense significance in comprehending the fungal-mediated plant growth processes. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of utilizing fractal dimension, Beziel curves, and artificial intelligence techniques in investigating mycorrhizal systems while proposing and designing a growth control platform to explore the fractal characteristics of arbuscular mycorrhizal structures and their correlation with plant growth status. The assessment of mycorrhizal system's fractal dimension enables us to comprehend its structural intricacy and unravel the underlying mechanisms within the mycorrhizal ecosystem

articleTitle: Efficient Low-light Image Enhancement combining Dense Residual Blocks with Mix Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: An efficient low-light image enhancement method is proposed by us. Specifically, we combine the strengths of dense and residual networks to create a dense residual block, enhanced by a mix attention mechanism and skip connections. This configuration facilitates efficient learning of image features. Additionally, we add an iterative brightness enhancement function to improve the brightness of image features. More importantly, the network's optimization can be achieved by integrating various loss functions. Quantitative and qualitative assessments performed on established public datasets attest to the superior performance of our technique in enhancing low-light images compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Synchronization for Neural Networks Under Asynchronous Deception Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper studies the problem of event-triggered synchronization in neural networks. We consider the case of sensor-to-controller and controller-to-actuator deception attacks and model these attacks as two independent Markov processes. In order to cope with data transmission congestion, we introduce two event triggered mechanisms to improve transmission efficiency. To meet the synchronization requirements, we propose a corresponding controller design. by using the analytical method of linear matrix inequalities, the feasibility of the proposed theory is verified, and the superiority of the method is demonstrated through experimental results.

articleTitle: A Float Motion Classification Method of Freshwater Fishing Using Mobile Phone Video
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Float is the underwater eye of the anglers. The long wait in freshwater fishing is a test of the patience of the anglers. It is very easy for the anglers to stare at the float for a long time with the naked eye, and it is not conducive to the health of the anglers to sit for a long time. However, it is not accurate to get up and walk around and watch the float. This paper proposes a video monitoring of float motion on the water surface using a mobile phone to reduce the irritability of waiting for a long time. After detecting and segmenting the float tail, the float motion is classified into black float, top float and drift float by This drift is judged as black drift, top drift and moving drift using vertical and horizontal velocities. Experiments show that the classification accuracy is 92%. It has good application value.

articleTitle: Toward Understanding How the Saturation Effect Impacts the Spread of Computer Viruses
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: It is well known that people who know the presence of network viruses will defend against them, and the more computer viruses are detected and the more measures are taken. However, most previous computer virus propagation models have completely ignored the saturation effect. This paper investigates how the saturation effect impacts the transmission of electronic virus. For this purpose, a new transmission model of network virus is proposed, in which the virus is not very prevalent. Under certain conditions, there is a global asymptotical stable equilibrium point with no virus in this model. Finally, we give several numerical examples to exhibit that sufficient saturation effect is greatly conducive to containing network viruses.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Containment Control for Multiagent Systems under Denial-of-Service Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the fully distributed predefined-time containment control problem for nonlinear multiagent systems (MASs) with denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. The containment error convergence time can be flexibly adjusted by employing the designed time-varying function (TVF). The containment controller signal is updated by applying a fully distributed hybrid event-triggered mechanism (ETM), which provides the condition for information transfer in the case of DoS attacks without using the global information of Laplacian matrix, and the controller does not need continuously update so that communication resources can be saved. The MASs are proved to be stable by using the Lyapunov stability theory. Finally, the simulation results show that the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Analysis of Congestion Propagation Characteristics on Wireless Networks with Internet Virus Propagation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Network congestion causes great harm to wireless networks, and for this reason, a variety of congestion control strategies have emerged, the main idea of these strategies is to alleviate network congestion by timely diversion and discarding the excess load on the congested nodes (links). Among them, the discarding strategy will reduce the network transmission reliability, and the diversion strategy of load volume with different efficiency will cause the congestion phenomenon to propagate on different nodes (links), even leading to cascading failures of the network and expanding the harm of congestion. In this paper, we investigate the propagation characteristics of congestion in wireless networks based on the Internet virus propagation model and research several diversion strategies, which are of positive significance for the further study of the network congestion problem generation mechanism and control strategies.

articleTitle: Adaptive neural network tracking control for n-order SISO nonlinear system with input saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive neural network control problem is studied for a n-order SISO nonlinear system with input saturation. Firstly, neural network (NN) is adopted to approximate the unknown and nonlinear function in the control system. Secondly, by introducing a saturation function, the controller signal can be limited within the pre-defined range effectively. Finally, the stability of the closed loop system is proved by using the Lyapunov theory and all signals are uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB).

articleTitle: Vital Sign Detection for Relaxed State of Human Body Based on 4D Point Cloud Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Non-stationary vital sign detection has always been a challenge in the field of remote detection. In this paper, we propose a new method to solve the problem of vital sign detection under relaxed states, which contains the human body in different sitting directions or random limb movements states. We first perform 3D imaging of the human body based on a 2D virtual array which is formed by MIMO technology, then analysis the signal feature to classify the abdominal, neck, and limb parts of the human body, and form a 4D point cloud, finally, multiple signals from the abdomen are used to extract respiratory rate, and multiple signals from the neck are used to extract heart rate. By this method under different relaxed states, the experimental results show that the average RMSE of respiratory rate is 1.18 BPM, with an average accuracy of 95.38%. The average RMSE of heart rate is 3.82 BPM, with an average accuracy of 95.18%.

articleTitle: A Method for Evaluating the Directionality of the HPM Helical Array Antenna at Varying Input Power Levels with Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the target positioning of high-power microwave (HPM) systems, the measurement of the pointing angle of the high-power microwave antenna plays a key role. In this paper, we propose a novel multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based method for determining the pointing angle of the high-power microwave helical antenna. This method can predict the pointing angle even when there are errors in the input. To validate our idea, we constructed a dataset that includes the real and imaginary parts of the voltage signals received by the dipole antenna, along with the corresponding output angles. We used this dataset to train our MLP and demonstrated its effectiveness, showing that the MLP can produce accurate results even for input data not present in the training set, in contrast to traditional methods. Moreover, the MLP exhibits enhanced representation and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on OCR Detection Technology for Beer Bottle Cap Inkjet Coding in Industrial Scenes Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The inspection of inkjet coding on the filling line in the beer industry plays a crucial role in ensuring the quality control of products before shipment. Currently, the primary method in industry relies on manual inspection, which suffers from defects such as waste of manufacturing resources, low efficiency, and a high error rate. Against this backdrop, this article proposes an OCR (Optical Character Recognition) model based on deep learning, including image processing, improved DBNet for text detection, a direction classifier for text box correction, and an improved CRNN for text recognition. This method achieves over 90% accuracy, significantly improving inkjet coding inspection efficiency on beer bottle caps in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Pig Behavior Detection Model Based on Improved RT-DETR
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The commercial and large-scale nature of modern pig farming necessitates innovative solutions, with computer vision emerging as a potent tool for group pig rearing. Despite the complexity of farming environments, which can result in significant occlusions and overlaps, impeding effective pig behavior detection, this paper presents the Slim PBi-DETR model. An enhancement of the RT-DETR model, it integrates a Bi-Level Routing Attention mechanism to augment recognition rates under challenging conditions and incorporates lightweight modifications to accelerate inference. The experimental outcomes indicate that our model attains an mAP of 87.5%, surpassing the RT-DETR model's mAP by 1.4% and reducing the model's GFLOPs by 30%. The Slim PBi-DETR model excels in accuracy and inference speed in scenarios with occlusions and overlaps, offering robust technical support for the intelligent surveillance of group-raised pigs.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Path Planning for Multi-Region Coverage by Multi-Objective Genetic Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is important in performing water search and rescue (SAR) tasks for drowning personnel. During the search process, a group of UAVs need to cover all task areas completely while considering energy limitations. In this paper, we propose a coverage path planning (CPP) algorithm based on improved multi-objective genetic algorithm for multiple UAVs to cover multiple discrete small areas. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Clinical Intelligent Diagnosis and Treatment of Hemorrhagic Stroke
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Among hemorrhagic stroke cases, acute cerebral hemorrhage conditions account for 10-15% of stroke cases. Its complex etiology is usually triggered by ruptured cerebral aneurysms, abnormalities of cerebral arteries, and other factors that cause blood to enter the brain tissue, resulting in mechanical damage and physiopathological reactions. This disease has an acute onset and rapid progression, the prognosis is usually poor, the mortality rate is high, and patients often suffer from neurological deficits that place a heavy burden on the patient and his/her socio-economy. Extension of the hematoma is one of the risk factors for poor prognosis and can be acutely life threatening. Therefore, early identification and prediction of hematoma expansion and edema development are crucial for improving prognosis. Medical imaging and artificial intelligence provide powerful tools for monitoring brain injury [1]. Intelligent diagnostic models can predict poor prognostic risk factors and support personalized treatment.

articleTitle: Optimization Design Study of Thermal Management System for Lithiumion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The study focuses on enhancing the thermal efficiency, economy, and safety of lithium-ion battery thermal management systems using an advanced optimization approach. This approach includes improving thermal management material conductivity, refining heat dissipation designs, and integrating modular structures with intelligent controls. Several strategies were tested through simulations and experiments, involving phase change materials, heat pipes, and liquid cooling systems. Results indicate that these technologies substantially boost temperature management and uniformity, prevent thermal runaway, and increase system safety. This suggests that such innovations significantly benefit the longevity and safety of batteries in electric vehicles and portable devices.

articleTitle: Multiple Augmented Graph Contrastive Learning for Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Graph Contrastive Learning (GCL) is widely used in the recommendation domain because it does not require extensive manual annotation. Most existing graph contrastive learning methods perform random data augment of the user-item bipartite graph, such as randomly removing edges with a specific probability or performing node discarding. We believe that in the process of performing the above random augment, there is a possibility that certain important nodes or edges may be deleted, so that its performance is deteriorated, which in turn affects the downstream recommendation. In this paper, we propose a method: Multiple Augmented Graph Contrastive Learning for Recommendation (MAGCLR). Our approach involves assigning importance values to edges and discarding them based on their respective importance levels, with less important edges being more likely to be discarded. We also conduct removal of influential nodes. Finally, we jointly train the edge discarding view and the node perturbation view. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that our proposed method achieves better performance compared to randomly aug-mented recommendation algorithms.

articleTitle: Prescribed-Time Clusters Flocking for Multi-Agent Systems of UAVs and USVs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of clusters flocking for a heterogeneous multi-agent system of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs). The dynamics models of the UAVs and USVs are established separately. Due to the different state dimensions and dynamics models of the UAVs and USVs, the two types of agents are formulated with two clusters. Then, the functions of formation errors of the two clusters are constructed. For the two clusters, a new type of prescribed-time formation control laws is designed respectively. Moreover, compared with the conventional formation control that can only ensure that the multi-agent system completes ideal formations without strict time constraints theoretically, the present prescribed-time control laws can enable the multi-agent system to complete ideal formation strictly at a prescribed time independent of initial formation errors. Finally, the effectiveness of the prescribed-time formation control is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: A Ship Vibration Monitoring System Based on Optical Fiber Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of ship vibration and noise monitoring, a vibration monitoring system based on a fiber Bragg grating sensor is designed in this paper. The monitoring objects include the ship hull and main electromechanical equipment. The fiber Bragg grating sensor is used to establish A quasi-distributed sensor network, the signal demodulation and A/D conversion are carried out by the specially designed FBG demodulation instrument, and the signal processing, data management, and centralized monitoring and alarm functions are realized by the software program of the upper computer system. The on-site monitoring and alarm functions are realized by each monitoring and alarm sub-station. Due to the use of the latest optical fiber sensing technology and distributed control mode, this system has the advantages of strong anti-electromagnetic interference ability, wide vibration monitoring range, high modularization degree, and strong expansibility, and has a high popularization and application value.

articleTitle: An ISAR Image Generation Method with New Azimuth Based on Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Due to ISAR images' strong pose sensitivity, they have significant differences under different azimuth conditions. However, obtaining ISAR images of the target's full pose in practical applications is difficult, which can adversely affect downstream tasks such as deception jamming. Therefore, it is necessary to use limited azimuth ISAR images to generate ISAR images with missing azimuth angles and supplement the missing data. This paper is inspired by the Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) structure and designs a novel network for the multi-azimuth rotation task of ISAR images to meet the needs of multi-angle sample expansion. We use azimuth information as conditional input to train the network and establish a mapping between azimuth information and the generated target pose. In addition, to solve the problem of pattern collapse, we use ISAR images and their feature maps as inputs to make the generated images more in line with the physical features of the target. Meanwhile, a comprehensive loss function was designed that combines adversarial loss, reconstruction loss, and angle loss to ensure that the generated image is visually and structurally closer to the actual ISAR image. The experimental results show that the difference between the generated ISAR image and the real label image is slight when our network's rotation angle is small. Especially when the rotation angle is controlled within 10°, the network can generate high-quality images that are highly similar to real ISAR images, and the network's strong generalization ability provides strong support for achieving effective deception jamming.

articleTitle: Performance Realization for Gas Turbine System: Adaptive Constraint Regulation Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the excessive consumption of fossil energy and the growing environmental pollution caused by its combustion, the gas turbine system (GTS) plays a key role in distributed renewable energy fields due to its versatility, efficiency and controllability. This paper focuses on the adaptive constraint regulation problem for the GTS with time-varying load disturbance, thereby facilitating exact speed tracking to regulate the fuel flow for the turbine under variable load conditions. Therein, a residual transformation dynamics based on the performance function are established for triggering the preset-time residual convergence and output performance constraints. Then, an adaptive constraint controller is developed to ensure the desired regulation level of the GTS. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed strategy can mitigate the load disturbance effect and guarantee the GTS performance constraints.

articleTitle: Detection of Winding Deformation based on the Vibration Phase Difference between Multiple Sensors of Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach based on the vibration phase difference between different measurement points to detect winding deformation in a transformer. The previous experiment investigated the relationship between the stability of the transformer system and the phase difference between the vibration signal of the transformer and the electrical input. However, obtaining the electrical input in field tests is difficult. Therefore, the vibration phase difference between measurement points is studied. Subsequently, a faulty-state indicator is proposed, which represents the variation in phase difference. To validate the proposed method, laboratory experiments are conducted on a 110 kV power transformer under short-circuit and unloaded conditions. In the experiments, winding deformation was introduced to the target transformer. The findings indicate that winding deformation can cause an increase in the variation of phase difference under different operating conditions. In summary, the proposed indicator can effectively evaluate mechanical condition of a winding.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus of Leader-Following Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems: A Dynamic Event-Triggered Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the bipartite consensus of nonlinear multi-agent systems that exhibit cooperation-competition behaviour using a dynamic event-triggering control method. The setting of error functions based on agent states in much literature has been expanded in this article. We have additionally introduced combined measurement functions to solve the consensus problem with antagonistic behaviour and Lipschitz nonlinear dynamics. In addition, sufficient criteria for achieving leader-follower bipartite consensus are derived by applying the Lyapunov stability theory. By incorporating dynamic event- triggering parameters, the controller update is no longer restricted to a constant condition but adapts dynamically based on the error. Moreover, our communication strategy enhances communication efficiency and eliminates Zeno behaviour. A numerical simulation has conducted to evaluate the superiority of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: FTN Detection Algorithm Based on Iterative Residual ISI Estimation and Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To address the severe Inter-Symbol Interference (lSI) problem introduced in faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) communication systems, a soft-information sequence detection algorithm based on iterative residual lSI estimation and correction is proposed. The algorithm first performs matched filtering and downsampling on the received signal, then obtains bit soft-information using soft demodulation, and utilizes channel decoding to acquire the initial decoding result. On this basis, the algorithm estimates the residual lSI component by re-mapping the initial decoded symbols and subtracting them from the received signal. The estimated lSI is then superimposed onto the mapped symbols as the input for the next iteration, achieving gradual lSI elimination and sequence detection performance improvement through multiple iterations. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve bit error rate performance close to Nyquist orthogonal transmission under different signal-to-noise ratios and compression factors, and can effectively converge after 3–4 iterations. Compared with existing FTN sequence detection algorithms, this algorithm greatly reduces computational complexity while ensuring detection performance.

articleTitle: An Acupoint Location Method Based on Lightweight Efficient Channel Attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), acupuncture localization plays a crucial role in the adjunctive prevention and treatment of various diseases. Traditional localization methods rely on anatomical knowledge and experience, but they are limited in accuracy and labor-intensive. Recently, deep learning techniques have emerged in the medical field due to advancements in computer networks, offering new avenues for acupoint localization. Inspired by the success of deep learning in medical imaging, we propose a Lightweight Efficient Channel Attention (LECA) network for acupoint localization. Specifically, MobileNetV2, a representative lightweight network, is adopted as the backbone of the LECA network to construct an efficient acupoint localization network with high accuracy. Additionally, Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) is integrated to enhance feature extraction capabilities. LECA network effectively improves the accuracy rate and reduces the number of parameters, and the average accuracy on the test image dataset reaches 87.7%, which is better than other existing deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Nonlinear Multiagent Systems Tracking Control with Dynamic Connectivity Preservation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper delves into a specific category of multiagent systems marked by nonlinear uncertainties. It tackles the distributed adaptive consensus tracking issue while emphasizing dynamic connectivity preservation. Considering the presence of uncertain nonlinear terms in the system, neural networks are utilized approximate these nonlinear terms. Taking into account the dynamic transformation range of communication among agents, an adaptive neural network controller is designed using an error transformation method to ensure the initial dynamic connectivity preservation patterns. Furthermore, the proposed control method is demonstrated to maintain boundedness for all signals through Lyapunov theory. Numerical simulations provide evidence of the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: GCIM based Improved Proportionate APA for Cluster-Sparse Identifications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In cluster-sparse system identification, a series of algorithms have been proposed by solving the cost function with a cluster-sparse penalty. Inserting the mixed the cluster-sparse improved proportionate affine projection algorithm (CS-IPAPA) has been derived for cluster-sparse system. However, for CS-IPAPA, the mixed may not be the best choice compared to the mixed Therefore, injecting the and generalized correntropy induced metric (GCIM) into the mixed problems of CS-IPAPA, we propose a family of GCIM-based CS-IPAPA from a basis pursuit perspective. In addition, considering the computational cost of exponential operations and the historical information of the proportional matrix, we derive a simplified version of CS-GCIM-IPAPA with the Taylor expansion method and time-shift property. Finally, compared to some competing sparse algorithms, we conduct a series of simulations to verify the superior filtering performance of our proposed algorithms with different input signals and various parameters.

articleTitle: Range-Doppler Image Interference Detection Based on Fourier-Polar Coordinate Transform for Over-the-Horizon Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper studies the detection of interference in over-the-horizon (OTH) radar systems, particularly transient interference (TSI) and radio frequency interference (RFI). We introduce a novel interference detection approach that utilizes range-Doppler (RD) image. Traditional techniques of feature extraction is unable to detect some interference. Hence, we develop the Fourier-polar coordinate transform (FPCT) for feature extraction of RD images. Then, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm is employed to classify the features. Based on FPCT and KNN, our classifier is designed, to classify the RD images into three categories: TSI, RFI, and no interference. In experiments, we simulate our design and traditional feature operators. The results show that our proposed FPCT and classifier achieves higher accuracy than traditional classifiers.

articleTitle: Research on Photovoltaic Power Prediction Method based on LSTM-KAN
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The effective integration of photovoltaic power stations in power grids necessitates accurate prediction of solar photovoltaic power generation. However, current prediction methodologies that depend on manual feature extraction, conventional modeling techniques, and isolated deep learning (DL) models fall short of satisfying the performance requirements for intricate and highly variable scenarios. Therefore, a novel approach is proposed in this study that leverages environmental climate information for hourly photovoltaic power generation prediction. The prediction task is characterized as a structured output prediction problem wherein multiple inputs are concurrently employed. To account for correlations between consecutive hours, the proposed predictive model utilizes KAN network modified Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks during training. Experimental results using environmental datasets from Shanghai, China demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms LSTM.

articleTitle: A Practical Approach to Television-Assisted Control Utilizing Eye-Tracking Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the establishment of TV as a home entertainment center, its control mode has undergone changes from physical knobs to infrared remote control, and then to modern intelligent control based on digital technology and the Internet. However, despite the rich functions of the current smart TV remote control, the complexity of operation has also increased, and emerging interaction means such as mobile phone APP remote control, gesture recognition and voice recognition are still facing limitations and inconvenience. Therefore, this paper proposes a practical TV-assisted control method based on eye tracking, which aims to solve the existing problems of smart TV control, such as operation complexity, hand occupation and the limitations of emerging interactive means, and provide a more convenient and comfortable viewing experience. The system uses the gaze confirmation mechanism, the user only needs to complete the operation through the natural gaze behavior, widely applicable to all kinds of consumers, and is expected to completely liberate the hands of users, to meet the majority of users' expectations for smart TV control. This study not only shows the innovative direction of smart TV control technology, but also provides a new idea for the future smart home interaction design.

articleTitle: Extended Observer-Based Fault-Tolerant Attitude Control of Hypersonic Reentry Vehicle Considering Actuator and Sensor Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A backstepping fault-tolerant control (FTC) scheme is presented for hypersonic reentry vehicles (HRV). The scheme is based on an extended state observer (ESO) and is capable of handling simultaneous faults in both the actuator and sensor. The ESO is reconfigured to approximate actuator and sensor faults and state variables. The estimated state variables are incorporated to design the adaptive backstepping fault-tolerant controller. The designed observer is proven to be uniformly ulti-mately bounded through Lyapunov analysis. Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Simulation of Vibration Characteristics of Saturated Reactor Under Fault Conditions of Converter Station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Saturated reactor of high voltage DC converter valve is the key primary equipment of converter valve. The vibration during normal operation belongs to high frequency vibration, and its vibration signal contains a lot of information. Its state evaluation is of great significance for the safe operation of converter valve and saturable reactor. In this paper, the actual ±800kV DC converter valve saturated reactor is taken as the research object, and a ±800kV UHVDC transmission simulation model is established. The simulation model takes into account the electromagnetic transient characteristics of the converter valve, which can well reflect the operation state of each device of the converter valve. The current flowing through the saturated reactor under different states of the converter valve is simulated and calculated. Then, a three-dimensional simulation model of saturated reactor is established. The magnetic field distribution, stress and vibration acceleration of saturated reactor are simulated and calculated by using the current data of simulation one as excitation. The experimental results show that the vibration signals of the saturated reactor are quite different under different states of the converter valve. The magnetic field will be greatly distorted in the state, and the maximum magnetic field intensity is 2.17T; the stress of the saturated reactor is 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>;the conclusions obtained in this paper can provide reference for the design of saturated reactor for DC converter valve.

articleTitle: Verification of Frequency and Time Offset Estimation Method for Chirp Signals in Mobile Satellite Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to address the synchronization issues caused by Doppler shift and delay in geostationary orbit satellite communication, a synchronization method based on Chirp signals is introduced. This method designs the structure of Chirp signals based on the frequency offset and delay of geostationary orbit satellites, and performs carrier synchronization and timing synchronization simultaneously using the up-Chirp and down-Chirp algorithms. The principle of this method is elucidated in this paper, and simulation analysis is conducted. System testing and validation are carried out using the GNU Radio platform and USRP transceiver components. The Chirp signal has a sampling point of 128. When the SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) is 5 dB, the simulated error of frequency offset estimation is approximately 5 Hz, and the simulated error of delay estimation is approximately 1.65×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–6</sup> s. The measured error of frequency offset estimation is approximately 7.2 Hz. Through the comparison of simulations and measurements, it is demonstrated that this method effectively solves the synchronization issues in geostationary orbit satellite communication.

articleTitle: Parametric Dynamic Distributed Tracking Control of Continuous-Time Linear Multi-Agent Systems with Specified Convergence Speed
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, the consensusability of continuous-time linear multi-agent systems (MASs) with one leader over undirected topology is considered. We introduce a novel distributed control protocol with parametric dynamic compensation to facilitate the achievement of tracking consensus. The necessary and sufficient consensusability conditions are derived theoretically. Based on this, the modified linear quadratic regulator (MLQR) optimal control scheme and Geršgorin's circle criterion are employed to ensure the tracking consensus with specified convergence speed. Finally, a numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of theoretical results.

articleTitle: A Secure Authentication Mechanism for WSN Nodes Based on Hybrid License Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: WSN is an important part of IoT, which is usually deployed in unattended areas and faces many security threats, and authentication mechanisms are crucial. Current authentication mechanisms rely on trusted third parties, which can easily lead to a single point of failure, thus affecting the stability of system security. In this paper, a secure authentication mechanism for WSN nodes based on a hybrid license blockchain is proposed. Firstly, the WSN cluster network model is constructed, and the WSN nodes are classified according to the different types of tasks, and the nodes are divided into base station, cluster head nodes, and ordinary nodes. Then, a blockchain network is constructed between different types of nodes to form a hybrid network model to promote collaboration among nodes. Finally, based on the hybrid permission blockchain model, a secure authentication mechanism is designed by combining cryptography and certificate-less signature strategies to ensure node security and maintain system stability. Security analyses and performance comparisons show that the mechanism can effectively defend against common network security threats and attacks while offering significant advantages in terms of computation and storage overhead.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Cooperative Exploration Route Planning Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The route planning problem for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) involves finding a path that allows the UAV to search a designated airspace extensively while avoiding dangerous areas. Ensuring effective cooperative detection among multi-UAV is a significant research challenge. To address this, this paper establishes a discrete multi-UAV cooperative exploration route planning model using a grid-based airspace map. A multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm based on Value-Decomposition Networks is proposed. This algorithm decomposes the overall value function among individual agents, enabling each agent to make independent decisions and resolving the “false reward” problem in multi-agent systems. The proposed approach demonstrates favorable results in the route planning of multi-UAV.

articleTitle: A Three-Stage Impulsive Delay Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In most research on impulsive control, the phenomenon of delay is often overlooked. However, in safetycritical applications involving the synchronization of two systems, transmission delays and information interference inevitably occur during the information transfer process. In this paper, we address the issue of delay synchronization between two systems. We derive stability criteria based on Lyapunov stability, impulsive control theory, and linear matrix inequalities. Subsequently, we design a three-stage impulsive switching controller with time windows. This controller achieves delay synchronization between two chaotic systems. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this method in stabilizing the systems.

articleTitle: Grey Wolf Optimizer for UAV Path Planning Based on Differential Evolution Mutation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: As the application environments for drones become increasingly complex, there is a need for an efficient algorithm to handle drone path planning problems. However, the results of many algorithms may be infeasible or inefficient, especially when facing three-dimensional complex flight environments. This paper proposes a combination of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Differential Evolution (DE) algorithms in the mutation phase, which maintains exploratory capabilities while promoting exploitation, to address UAV path planning problems. In GWO-DE algorithms, the GWO and DE algorithms are well-coordinated, adding a balance between exploitation and exploration. Additionally, chaotic initialization is employed to alleviate the issue of overly concentrated initial populations. The parameters are handled nonlinearly, and different alpha wolves are employed at different stages to improve the efficiency of early-stage development and later-stage exploration. In the three-dimensional simulation of UAVs, the proposed GWO-DE outperforms GWO and DE. The UAV path lengths generated by GWO-DE are shorter than its competitors.

articleTitle: Collision-Free Formation Finite-Time Prescribed Performance Control for Under-Actuated Unmanned Surface Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper studies the distributed path-following time-varying formation control problem for a fleet of under-actuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) with collision avoidance and connectivity preservation. A finite-time-prescribed performance-based (FTPP) formation control scheme is proposed based on the error transformation. To provide transient and steady-state performance specifications on velocity errors, including convergence time and range, a finite-time performance function (FTPF) is introduced in the control design. Radial basis function neural network (RBF) is utilized to compensate the effects of uncertain dynamics in USVs. Finally, by Lyapunov stability analysis, it is shown that all error signals of the closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed formation control scheme.

articleTitle: Non-Overshooting Output Regulation of Linear Systems via Positive Systems Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the non-overshooting output regulation problem by using the analysis and synthesis approaches of positive systems. Combining linear programming with gain matrix decomposition technique, a state feedback control law with two different kinds of design parameters is designed to ensure the stability and positivity of the corresponding closed-loop systems, which leads to the solvability of the non-overshooting output regulation problem of linear systems. Finally, an example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: A Novel Representing Method of Radar Emitter PDWs Based on Non-Uniform Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In modern radar system, the common parameters become more and more complicated. Interval-value parameters caused by the intentional or unintentional deviations have been the research hotspot in radar emitter type recognition work. However, the effect of representing accuracy on the interval-value parameters of pulse description words (PDWs) have not been sufficiently considered. In this paper, a novel parameter representing method based on non-uniform encoding (NUE) is proposed. The NUE transforms the interval-value PDWs into vectors, which reaches higher accuracy and larger range in the new features. To get better recognition performances, the new sequence is input to different networks. Simulation results indicate that our proposed PDW NUE has better representing accuracy and good recognition performance.

articleTitle: A Non-associative Learning Emotional Progressive Circuit Based on Forgetting Memristor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Brain-like hardware is a key step in realizing artificial intelligent machines, and forgetting memristor is a new type of memristor whose dynamics are very suitable for simulating neurons and synapses in the human brain nervous system, however, there is a lack of relevant research on forgetting memristors in recent years. In this paper, a voltage-controlled forgetting memristor with threshold characteristics is proposed, and the basic characteristics of the memristor are encapsulated and verified in LTSPICE circuit simulation software. A threshold-variable neuron model based on the memristor is proposed, and a circuit is used to implement the changed model. Based on the threshold-variable neuron circuit, a neuron circuit with biological non-associative learning properties is designed, which is capable of exhibiting the habituation and sensitization processes in the non-associative learning properties. Finally, an affective progressive circuit was constructed by combining multiple neurons and memristive forgetting synapses. The circuit has human non-associative learning emotion progression characteristics and can simulate emotion decay for familiar things, emotion enhancement for special things, as well as emotion forgetting characteristics.

articleTitle: Demand Response-oriented Optimization of Energy Consumption for Multi-type Central Air Conditioners
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The increasing demand for air conditioning due to global warming poses challenges to the power grid during peak load periods in summer. Air conditioning systems, which account for a significant portion of building energy consumption, can be utilized in demand response programs to alleviate peak demand and optimize grid operations. In this study, operational models for both traditional central air conditioning systems and ice storage systems are developed, including components such as pumps, cooling towers, and refrigeration units. The ice storage system stores and releases energy during peak periods to reduce peak demand and maintain grid stability. The study employs the raccoon optimization algorithm (COA), inspired by raccoon behavior, to optimize the operation of complex central air conditioning systems. The algorithm aims to reduce energy consumption while meeting the cooling needs of users. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the COA algorithm in optimizing energy consumption of central air conditioning systems and enabling their participation in demand response programs, ultimately contributing to intelligent grid operation and peak load management for grid stability.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Delayed Neural Networks via Intermittent Control Involving Tow Switching Periods of Different Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of synchronization of delayed neural networks by employing dual-periodic intermittent control with two different ratios. Some easily-validated sufficient criteria, are obtained by using Lyapunov stability theory, technique of linear matrix inequalities(LMIs), and the mathematical induction. To illustrate the efficacy of intermittent control with two distinct switching periods, a numerical demonstration is provided.

articleTitle: Time Domain Broadband Electromagnetic Modeling of Dynamic Group Targets based on Shooting-and-Bouncing Ray Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Electromagnetic characteristic analysis is widely used in detection and recognition, but commonly used commercial electromagnetic simulation software has many problems: firstly, the core algorithms of many software are numerical algorithms. Although these algorithms have high calculation accuracy, their computational memory requirements are too large and the calculation time is too long. Secondly, the acceleration effect is not good in some applications. Thirdly, the simulation ability for dynamic scenes is insufficient. Based on the time-domain Shooting-and-Bouncing Ray method, this paper studies the time-domain broadband electromagnetic modeling technology of dynamic group targets, which has the ability to simulate and analyze broadband electromagnetic of dynamic group targets and electrically large complex materials. To solve the efficient modeling problem of dynamic group targets, this paper adopts pre-processing techniques such as mesh generation dynamic acceleration and fast hidden elimination. An optimization scheme was proposed for the boundary volume hierarchy (BVH) acceleration algorithm in the bouncing ray method, which achieved non recursive stack free BVH traversal on the GPU and reduced memory required for computation. Based on the above algorithm, electromagnetic simulation software has been developed, which can achieve functions such as dynamic scene construction, electromagnetic simulation, and data post-processing. It can efficiently and accurately simulate and analyze the dynamic broadband electromagnetic characteristics of complex group targets. The simulation results verified the effectiveness of the algorithm and software.

articleTitle: Preassigned-Time Partial Component Synchronization of Multi-Weighted Complex Networks with Different Dimensional Nodes and Quantized Couplings
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The research studies the preassigned-time (PDT) synchronization of multi-weighted complex networks (MWCNs) with different dimensional nodes and quantized couplings. Subsequently, mapping the systems to the identical node dimensions via a mapping function. Additionally, a feedback control strategy is proposed to realize PDT partial component synchronization for different dimensional systems. Eventually, through theoretical derivation, the sufficient conditions for PDT partial component synchronization of the MWCNs is established.

articleTitle: Electricity Load Forecasting Based on Patch Channel-Mixing Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Recent research has demonstrated the strong potential of Transformer models in electricity load forecasting, due to their ability to effectively address the long-term memory modeling issues in the load forecasting process. However, there are several issues with Transformer models for load forecasting, including quadratic time complexity, difficulty in screening factors with electricity load, and false similarity points due to the modeling methods on point level. To address those issues, we propose an efficient design of Transformer-based model for electricity load forecasting. It is based on two components: (i) divide the load sequence and multi-factor sequence into subsequence level segments with multiple resolutions, and then use them as input markers for the Transformer model. (ii) channel mixing, where the load channel interacts with multiple factors channels to achieve explicit modeling of the relationship between load and multiple factors. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that our model significantly outperforms existing methods on two large-scale datasets, and provide a new solution to the load forecasting problem.

articleTitle: Automatic Coal Feeding Control System Based on STM32
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The automated control of coal addition is a crucial process in modern industrial coal-fired power plants. This paper presents a system for automated coal addition control to ensure unmanned and regulated coal addition, thus preventing the coal bunker from being underfilled or overfilled. The system utilizes an STM32 microcontroller as the main control chip and a novel millimeter-wave radar to monitor the coal level in the bunker in real time, activating or deactivating the coal conveyor belt accordingly. Additionally, it incorporates alarm devices to alert operators in situations of underfilling or overfilling. A USART serial port screen is integrated into the system for human-machine interaction. In terms of coal level monitoring, a Digital Signal algorithm is used to calculate the coal level inside the bunker, displaying it as a percentage on the serial port screen. Through testing, the system has demonstrated the expected performance in terms of measurement accuracy, control effectiveness, and human-machine interaction.

articleTitle: Design of A Wide-band Compact Phase-locked Baseband Source
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, a wide-band compact phase-locked baseband source is designed with an output frequency range of 300MHz~6GHz.Firstly, DC-DC and LDO cascade are used to realize the design of a highly stable voltage regulator source, and an external sampling resistor is used to realize the DC-DC voltage regulation function. Then, the baseband source circuit is designed and tested based on phase-locking technique, and the C8051 control program is developed to realize the wideband output. Finally, after testing, the power is ±1dB flat at OdBm, and the phase noise is better than 95dBc/Hz 1kHz with good stability. At the same time, this paper through the device selection compact design to achieve the baseband source surface-mounted, the circuit area will be reduced by more than 50%; at the same time, the signal pins will be pinned out to improve the compatibility of application scenarios. This design also has the advantages of stable broadband signal output, strong compatibility, small size, and embedded in the device without the need for collocation, convenient intermodulation, very flexible use, and broad application prospects.

articleTitle: A Target Region Based Non-Uniform Remote Sensing Image Process Method Using Data Hiding
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, by taking advantage of various image data hiding scheme, we proposed a non-uniform optical remote sensing image scheme of which informative target region remains lossless via the compression-reconstruction process. Two different strategies are proposed in case of different input image's characteristic itself. Experimental results show that over 30% of test image set fit the proposed scheme in which their target region can be lossless transmitted through digital image compression of compression ratio (CR) equals 4 or 16. Meanwhile, the vision quality of constructed background area is fairly acceptable.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Stability of Dissipative Hamiltonian Differential Algebraic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The paper focuses on the fixed-time stability issue of dissipative Hamiltonian differential algebraic systems (DH-DAS). Due to the singularity, classical analysis methods of fixed time stability for ordinary differential equation are invalid. In order to overcome this difficulty, a decomposition method is proposed to derive differential part and the algebraic part from DH-DAS. By utilizing the structural properties of the dissipative Hamiltonian systems, several fixed-time stability criteria are derived.

articleTitle: Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Smart contracts are among the most important applications of blockchain technology and are vulnerable to network attacks, leading to significant financial losses. Thus, smart contract vulnerability detection has become an important research field. Currently, there are problems with limited detection types and low detection efficiency in smart contract vulnerabilities. It is particularly crucial to achieve high detection efficiency and cover a wide range of vulnerability types in smart contract vulnerabilities. This paper builds a dataset named SC-4, which consists of over 3000 data of four common vulnerabilities in smart contracts: Reentrancy, Transaction Order Dependence, Unchecked-Send, and Unhandled-Exceptions. We propose a smart contract vulnerability detection model based on an improved gated recurrent unit (GRU) and random forest (RF) fusion algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can accurately identify four types of smart contract vulnerabilities, and the accuracy can reach 98.47%. The number of vulnerability types detected has also increased compared to that in previous research.

articleTitle: High Contrast Ratio 4-to-2 Plasmonic Encoder Utilizing Cascaded Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel plasmonic 4-to-2 encoder comprising cascaded ring resonators coated with graphene layers and two metal-insulator-metal (MIM) waveguides. The encoding function operates at 850 nm by modulating the intensity of pump beam focused on the graphene layer to manipulate the state of the plasmonic resonators. The performance of the encoder is analyzed utilizing the finite-difference time-domain method, demonstrating a high contrast ratio of 15.1 dB. Thus, this efficient 4-to-2 optical encoder is well-suited for integration into optical integrated computing devices.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Technology Based on Strong Light Suppression and Infrared Supplementary Lighting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-light image enhancement technology for complex optical environments, which improves imaging quality in low-light conditions through three main designs: strong light suppression, image enhancement processing, and infrared supplementary lighting. These techniques achieve night vision image enhancement and restoration, maximizing the reproduction of the target object, and improving the brightness, contrast, and clarity of night vision images under complex low-light optical environments. This technology emphasizes detail in video images, enhances image recognition, and increases image interpretation accuracy. The proposed method has shown excellent results in night flight tests, significantly improving the accuracy of photogrammetry during night flights.

articleTitle: Real-Time Reachable Set Estimation for Singular Systems with Distributed Time-Varying Delay Based on a New Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, we mainly focus on the real-time RSE for singular systems with distributed time-varying delays under bounded peak disturbance by using a new method. Our primary objective is to wrap the reachable set using a real-time updated ellipsoid. Firstly, we briefly introduce our research motivation. Secondly, under the framework of LMI, we apply integral inequality techniques and other mathematical lemmas, combined with a new method, to find new reachable set estimation conditions for singular systems with bounded peak disturbance and distributed time-varying delays. To validate the effectiveness of our results, we finally provide a numerical examples, and visually demonstrate the effect of real-time RSE through illustrations.

articleTitle: A Novel Accelerated Projection Neurodynamic Model for Convex Optimization Problem Constrained by Set and Linear-Equality
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Accelerated neurodynamic models are important tools for efficiently addressing optimization problems. By making use of projection operators, this paper proposes a novel acceler-ated projection neurodynamic model (APNM) to tackle convex optimization problem constrained by set and linear-equality. The global convergence of APNM is rigorously proved via Lyapunov theoretical framework. When the design parameters satisfy cer-tain conditions, APNM enjoys an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}(1/\zeta(t))$</tex> convergence rate of objective function error. Especially, if objective function satisfies Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality, then APNM has the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{\zeta(t)})$</tex> convergence rates of tracking error and linear equality constraint violation. Furthermore, it is proved that APNM enjoys an exponential convergence rate when the time-varying parameter grows exponentially. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the feasibility and efficiency of APNM.

articleTitle: ISAR Image Super Resolution with Alternating Iterations of Restoration and Degradation Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Recently, deep learning technologies have catapulted the field of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image super resolution (SR). However, most existing methods only focus on the restoration process from low-resolution(LR) to high-resolution(HR) images and neglect the auxiliary role of degradation information, so it is difficult for them to recover weak scattering points and prone to generating spurious scattering points. To tackle these challenges, We introduce the pioneering concept of a degenerate kernel in the ISAR image SR task, utilizing the degradation process from HR images to LR images to construct optimization criteria for the restoration process. Furthermore, we adopt an alternating iterative strategy, which can improve the adaptability to various degradation of ISAR images. A Deep Unfolding Alternating Iterative Network (DUAIN) with channel attention residual dense module is proposed to enhance the quality of ISAR images. By fully integrating the scattering point image features of each convolutional layer, our module can improve the ability to recover weak scattering points. The experimental results show that our proposed network can improve the recovery accuracy of weak scattering points and diminish the occurrence of spurious scattering points in both synthetic and real-world ISAR images, resulting in superior quality ISAR images.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Output-Feedback Containment Control Based Nonlinear Filtering for Multiagent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: A fixed-time containment control problem of non-linear multiagent systems (MASs) respect to directed communication topology and strict-feedback form is studied. Firstly, for purpose of estimating the state of each agent, the observer is designed for each agent by utilizing the measurement output of the agent itself. Moreover, a nonlinear filter, which is used to deal with the problem of complexity explosion existed in backstepping method has been presented. In addition, to conquer the singular-ity problem, an effective fixed-time containment control scheme improving system convergency is proposed, which ensures that all followers can converge to the convex hull formed by the leader in fixed time. Finally, simulation study has confirmed the validity of the approach proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Containment Control of Linear Continuous-time Invariant Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates an approach for distributed containment control to linear continuous-time invariant multi-agent systems. Firstly, a distributed static control protocol aims to guarantee that all followers converge within the convex hull delineated by the leaders. The feasibility of this protocol is theoretically proven. Secondly, the information of neighbor nodes is incorporated, leading to the design of a dynamic control protocol that emphasizes follower cooperation with neighboring nodes during the convergence process. Finally, simulations are conducted for both the static and dynamic protocols, and the simulation results are compared to validate the feasi bility and superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Radar Clutter Simulation and Background Adaptive Clutter Map Detection Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Earth-sea clutter is a significant component of radar signals and can significantly impair radar performance. Radar clutter suppression is an essential aspect of radar signal detection. The realistic modelling and simulation of radar clutter can assist in the identification of more effective radar clutter suppression algorithms. The present paper introduces a more comprehensive radar clutter model and presents the simulation signal of the radar clutter amplitude statistics and spectral characteristics. The aim of this study was to address the issue of a high false alarm rate associated with the traditional constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) detection method when the clutter changes drastically in the airspace. To this end, a background adaptive clutter map constant false alarm detection method based on the clutter environment characteristics of the adaptive change of iteration coefficients was proposed and its efficacy was demonstrated through experimental results. The results demonstrate that the background adaptive clutter map constant false alarm detection method proposed in this paper is capable of effectively suppressing ground and sea clutter, thereby meeting the engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Binary Classification of Diabetic Foot Thermograms Based on HD-EfficientNetV2 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is among the top ten causes of death globally. The disease manifests through various complications, with vascular changes demonstrating a chronic relationship with diabetic ulcer events in the distal limbs. For the binary classification task of diabetic foot thermographs, this paper proposes the HD-EfficientNetV2 network model based on EfficientNetV2. It aims to classify DM subjects from thermal imaging images of diabetic foot. The model introduces dilated mixed convolutions to increase the receptive field and enhance feature extraction capability. It also uses the Hard-Swish non-linear activation function, which is computationally simpler and provides a smoother gradient across the entire input range. Additionally, the CA (Coordinate Attention) mechanism is introduced to enhance the feature extraction of temperature regions in diabetic foot thermal images. HD-EfficientNetV2 achieved an accuracy of 97.8% and an F1 score of 97.2%. The effectiveness of the improved model in the diabetic foot thermal image classification task was validated through comparative experiments and ablation studies.

Author Keywords: Classification of Diabetic Foot Thermal Images

articleTitle: Nested Miller Compensation with Ping-Pong Structure Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Over the past few decades, advances in integrated circuit technology have not only dramatically advanced society and industry, but have also changed the way people live and work. In the face of increased demand for high-voltage and high-temperature environments such as aerospace, automotive and high-temperature environments such as aerospace, automotive electronics, and high-precision measurement equipment, the design of high-voltage operational amplifiers with low noise and low distortion voltage for extreme conditions has become a major challenge in circuit design. In this thesis, the circuit is designed based on the O.25μmBCD process, and pre-simulation of the circuit is completed on Cadence's Virtuoso design platform. The pre-simulation of the circuit is completed. The low-distortion op-amp input distortion voltage is 3.84μ V at 5V supply voltage and 25°C room temperature. The typical value is 3.84μ V at 5V supply voltage, 25°C room temperature, 140dB DC gain, 68.9° phase margin, and unit gain bandwidth of the output is close to rail-to- rail, and the final simulation shows that the specifications basically meet the expected results.

articleTitle: Decentralized Online Multi-Objective Optimization for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: To satisfy the charging demands of electric vehicles (EVs) in cheap and fast way while protecting the privacy of EV charging stations (EVCSs), a decentralized online multi-objective (OMO) optimization framework for EVCSs operations is proposed. The framework aims to optimize the power cost and the utilities of EVCSs and guide their convergence to the targets, which are set before the dispatch.
