A recently reported target-based online dynamic weighted (TBODW) algorithm is used to transfer the multi-objective (MO) problem into single-objective problems. Then, the decentralized optimization method is proposed in this study to solve the single-objective problem decentralized to avoid the leakage of EVCSs. Numerical experiments are designed and their results show the effectiveness and the convergence of this framework.

articleTitle: Predictor-Based Control of Stochastic Systems with Input Delay under Deception Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article explores the mean-square exponential stability of stochastic systems with input delays under deception attacks, utilizing a predictor-based controller. Predictive techniques are introduced to mitigate the impact of the input delay, enhancing system performance and stability. Through a comparison between continuous and sampled-data control systems, the equivalence conditions regarding the stability are investigated. Furthermore, estimates for the upper bound of the acceptable attack probability and the sampling period are derived. Additionally, a qualitative analysis is presented, elucidating various indicators associated with the sampling period and attacks. To validate the findings, computational simulations are executed.

articleTitle: An Improved Indoor Positioning Method by Fusing Ultra-Wideband and Millimeter Wave Radar Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB), the frequently utilized technology for indoor positioning, has been developing at a rapid pace. As a drawback, it requires dense infrastructure to reduce strong errors in complex non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios. To cope with this situation, the study proposed a scheme that fuses UWB and millimeter wave (MMW) technologies. The approach provides position information through MMW radar instead of dense UWB base stations. State variables are provided for solving the target position and Extended Kalman filter (EKF), improving the localization accuracy and reducing the infrastructure deployment density.

articleTitle: An Improved SSD Deep Network-Based Algorithm for Eye State Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor real-time performance in current eye state detection algorithms, a deep learning algorithm-improved single-shot multibox detector (SSD) with both real-time performance and detection accuracy is proposed. Firstly, the lightweight network MobileNetV2 replaces the original feature extraction network VGG16 to improve the detection speed. Then, spatial and channel squeeze-excitation network (scSENet) attention module is introduced to enhance the spatial features and channel features of the eye to improve the detection accuracy. The proposed method is tested on the public data set Closed Eyes in the Wild (CEW), achieving a mAP value of 96.12%, which is higher than current mainstream methods. The experimental results show that the algorithm has high accuracy and efficient detection speed in the task of eye state detection.

articleTitle: Adaptive Nonsingular Terminal SMO for Chattering Suppression in Sensorless SPMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Considering chattering suppression and finite-time convergence of the system states in the sliding mode observer (SMO), an adaptive nonsingular terminal sliding mode observer (ANTSMO) based on the virtual control law is designed for surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) sensorless control. The observer employs a nonsingular terminal sliding mode (NTSM) surface, enabling the system states to converge to the origin in a finite time. The back electromotive force (EMF) of the motor is obtained by integrating the virtual control law, so that the phase delay caused by the filter is eliminated. Meanwhile, the adaptive technique can automatically search for the minimum value of the sliding mode control gain to reduce chattering in accordance with the variations in the motor operating conditions. The feasibility of the proposed algorithm is proven by strict Lyapunov theory, and its effectiveness is confirmed through simulation comparisons.

Author Keywords: adaptive nonsingular terminal sliding mode observer (ANTSMO)

articleTitle: Research on SYN Flood Malicious Traffic Detection Method Based on FPGA-SOC HarmonyOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: SYN Flood malicious traffic attack is a typical representative of distributed denial of service (DDo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>) attacks and one of the primary factors threatening IoT security. In response to the architecture pattern of FPGA-SOC HarmonyOS, a lightweight detection method combining Renyi entropy and CUSUM algorithm suitable for this architecture is proposed. Firstly, the calculated Renyi entropy of the quadruple tuple is used to perform initial inspection on the traffic based on extracted packet features, determining whether it is suspicious traffic. Then, the CUSUM value of SYN packet quantity is utilized for secondary inspection to determine if it constitutes a SYN Flood malicious traffic attack. Finally, through experimental simulations generating both attack and normal traffic, results show that the SYN Flood malicious traffic detection method based on FPGA-SOC HarmonyOS achieves an accuracy rate of 87.7%, which surpasses adaptive threshold algorithms and CUSUM algorithm in terms of accuracy and effectively enhances IoT security protection.

articleTitle: Resnet-A: Multi Standard Classification Prediction of Colon Cancer CT Images Based on an Improved Resnet152 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, we study an automatic screening method for colon cancer CT images using deep learning technology. Recognizing the limitations of traditional medical image analysis methods, we propose a model called ResNet-A based on the ResNet-152 architecture for multi-standard classification prediction of colon cancer CT images. The dataset provided by Southwest Medical University consists of CT image sections from 694 patients with colon cancer, labeled according to four classification criteria (WHO, Nerve, Vessel, MMR). To enhance the generalization ability of the model, we perform various image preprocessing operations such as resampling and random enhancement. Additionally, we introduce two plug-and-play modules named Channel Attention and Spatial Attention to help the model focus on relevant information and improve its performance and accuracy. Finally, we evaluate the model's performance through three-fold cross-validation. The findings of this study hold significant importance in enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of colon cancer diagnosis while promoting advancements in medical image analysis technology.

articleTitle: Feedback Oscillation Circuits for High-Frequency Surface Acoustic Wave Device
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, series-type Colpitts oscillation circuit and parallel-type Clapp oscillation circuit are presented for the rapid initiation of surface acoustic wave device. The stable oscillation signal of SAW device is generated by matching the operating frequency and zero phase point of the feedback oscillation circuit. The experimental results indicate that the oscillation frequency of the designed SAW oscillator circuit is around 434 MHz, the error stability is less than 0.1 MHz, and the oscillation amplitude is 209 mV. This work provides a possible strategy for the stable oscillation circuit design of high-frequency SAW devices.

articleTitle: Time Series Modeling for Heart Rate Prediction: From ARIMA to Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death globally, necessitating precise forecasting models for monitoring vital signs like heart rate, blood pressure, and ECG. Traditional models, such as ARIMA and Prophet, are limited by their need for manual parameter tuning and challenges in handling noisy, sparse, and highly variable medical data. This study investigates advanced deep learning models, including LSTM, and transformer-based architectures, for predicting heart rate time series from the MIT-BIH Database. Results demonstrate that deep learning models, particularly PatchTST, significantly outperform traditional models across multiple metrics, capturing complex patterns and dependencies more effectively. This research underscores the potential of deep learning to enhance patient monitoring and CVD management, suggesting substantial clinical benefits. Future work should extend these findings to larger, more diverse datasets and real-world clinical applications to further validate and optimize model performance.

articleTitle: Energy Functionals and Variational Principle in Electromagnetic Modal Analysis-Part I: Diagonalizing Input Power Operator Method Revisited
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The energy transport theorem (ETT)-based decoupling mode theory (DMT) uses diagonalizing input power operator (IPO) method to calculate the energy-decoupled modes (DMs) of wave-port-fed transmitting antennas. This paper focuses on examining the rationality of the method. To examine the rationality, a set of energy functionals involved in the wave-port-fed energy-transmitting problem are proposed. It is proved that: 1) the physical laws-Maxwell equations and boundary conditions-used to govern classical electrodynamics can be derived from the energy functionals by using variational principle; 2) the energy functionals are equivalent to the input power (or its complex conjugation) in physical essence; 3) the DMs derived from the diagonalizing IPO method can diagonalize both the input power and energy functionals simultaneously. The above conclusions clearly reveal the rationality of using diagonalizing IPO method to calculate DMs.

articleTitle: Energy Functionals and Variational Principle in Electromagnetic Modal Analysis—Part II: Input Power Operators Free of Dependent Variables
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The self energy transport theorem (ETT) used to govern the energy-transmitting process of wave-port-fed antennas is extended to a more general version—coupled ETT— and the coupled ETT is equivalent to Maxwell equations and wave equations. Two energy functionals are formulated, and they can derive the wave equations by using variational principle. The energy functionals have the same physical essence as the input power, which is the energy source term contained in the self ETT. Based on the above results, the fundamental importance of input power is revealed, and then the reason to use the input power operator (IPO) to compute the fundamental modes of antenna is clarified, and, at the same time, the difference between the numerical performances of some different IPOs proposed previously is also exposed. Inspired by the energy functionals and their physical essence, some novel IPOs are proposed, and the novel IPOs have a higher computational efficiency than the traditional IPOs in the aspect of calculating the fundamental modes of antenna.

articleTitle: Energy Functionals and Variational Principle in Electromagnetic Modal Analysis—Part IV: CMs of Magneto-Dielectric Entire/Sub-Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The energy functionals involved in the work-energy transformation processes of magneto-dielectric entire-structures and sub-structures are formulated. The fundamental electrodynamic laws used to govern the entire-structure and partial-structure work-energy transformation processes are derived from the variational stationarity conditions of the energy functionals. It is proved that the entire-structure and sub-structure energy functionals have the same physical essence as the entire-structure driving power (ES-DP) and partial-structure driving power (PS-DP) of magneto-dielectric entire-structures and sub-structures, respectively. The above conclusions give a solid physical and mathematical foundation to the diagonalizing ES-DP and PS-DP methods for calculating the characteristic modes (CMs) of magneto-dielectric entire-structures and sub-structures. In addition, some different operator forms of PS-DP are proposed, and their different numerical performances in the aspect of calculating sub-structure CMs are emphasized. The results and conclusions obtained in this paper are universal for both the lossless and lossy magneto-dielectric entire-structures and sub-structures.

articleTitle: Personal Credit Risk Assessment Based on Swarm Intelligence and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Personal credit risk assessment plays a critical role in the issuance of credit loans by banks and other financial institutions, fundamentally serving as a predictive problem. However, traditional methods often only achieve local optimal solutions. This paper introduces an innovative method for personal credit risk assessment by integrating swarm intelligence and random forest techniques, aiming to find the global optimal solution. The practicality and efficiency of this algorithm have been demonstrated through experimental validation on the German credit database.

articleTitle: High-Order Quantum Genetic Algorithm Based on Quantum Entanglement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Quantum genetic algorithms(QGA) typically construct traditional quantum chromosomes as independent quantum bit systems, which has facilitated the enhancement of search speed and precision in genetic algorithms, demonstrating powerful problem-solving capabilities in optimization issues. Although traditional QGA have enriched population diversity, they still tend to fall into local optima, and the evolutionary update operations require rotation directions to be determined by lookup tables, a process involving multiple conditional judgments that affect algorithm efficiency. To address these issues, an improved method has been proposed to further enhance the performance of QGA. In the initial population selection, a population grouping evolution method based on microhabitat coevolution strategy is used to prevent the algorithm from getting trapped in local optima when solving complex function problems. Additionally, quantum entanglement is introduced on top of quantum super-position by implementing quantum entanglement using quantum registers, and higher-order quantum rotation gates are employed that do not involve multiple conditional judgments of lookup tables, thus improving the efficiency of quantum chromosome measurement and evolutionary updates. Finally, traditional QGA and higher-order quantum genetic algorithms were applied to test functions in multiple experiments. The results indicate that, compared to traditional QGA, the higher-order quantum genetic algorithms have achieved an increase in convergence speed, an approximate 14.3% improvement in convergence precision, and possess enhanced global search capabilities.

articleTitle: Energy Functionals and Variational Principle in Electromagnetic Modal Analysis-Part III: An Expose on the CMs of PEC Entire/Sub-Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The energy functionals and variational principles used to govern the work-energy transformation processes of perfectly electric conducting (PEC) entire-structures and sub-structures are studied. It is revealed that: in physical essence, the energy functional of PEC entire-structures is equivalent to the entire-structure driving power (ES-DP); the energy functional of PEC sub-structures is equivalent to the partial-structure driving power (PS-DP); the energy functional of the PEC entire/sub-structures is equivalent to the input power (IP). Thus, the classical entire/sub-structure characteristic modes (CMs) calculated from diagonalizing ES/PS-DP have also the ability to diagonalize the energy functional and IP of entire/sub-structures. Based on this conclusion, a novel diagonalizing IP method is proposed to calculate the CMs of PEC entire/sub-structures. The novel diagonalizing IP method has a wider applicable range than the conventional methods, because the novel method is suitable for the PEC entire/sub-structures with different internal and external material parameters, but the conventional methods are not. Some numerical experiments are tested for verifying the validity and correctness of the novel diagonalizing IP method in the aspect of calculating the CMs of PEC entire/sub-structures.

articleTitle: PID3D: 3D Object Detection with Object Proposal Instance Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Recent advances in 3D point cloud object detection have made significant progress, but critical challenges still hinder their effectiveness in practical settings. First, existing methods struggle with fine-grained discrimination within object classes, leading to misclassifications and imprecise bounding box placements. Second, detecting objects in complex, real-world environments like crowded urban areas is challenging due to occlusions. Third, an imbalanced distribution of training data across object classes worsens these issues, particularly affecting the detection of less represented classes such as pedestrians and bicycles. To tackle these challenges, this paper introduces a novel LiDAR-based 3D object detection framework that uses instance discrimination to improve fine-grained object differentiation. By developing unique feature representations for each instance, our method enhances the model's ability to distinguish between objects. We also introduce a new view generation technique that mimics occlusions and point drifts typical in autonomous driving scenario, increasing the accuracy and robustness of 3D detectors. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms standard methods, improving pedestrian detection by 6.21% and overall mAP by 1.61%.

articleTitle: CoBiTex-FTM: Multi-Head Attention and Full-Token Masking for Chinese Aircraft Maintenance Manuals NER
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With advancements in technology and the aviation industry, aircraft maintenance has gained attention. The unstructured data, short texts, and mixed Chinese-English content in maintenance manuals pose challenges for Chinese Named Entity Recognition tasks. Current NER models struggle with capturing long-distance dependencies, leading to the loss of contextual information, blurred word boundaries, and handling mixed-language texts. This paper introduces CoBiTex-FTM, an enhanced model combining BERT, BiLSTM, Multi-Head Attention, and Full-Token Masking. We constructed a specialized NER dataset for Chinese aircraft maintenance manuals and found that CoBiTex-FTM effectively leverages contextual information, reduces ambiguity, and improves recognition accuracy. Comparative experiments show CoBiTex-FTM's superior performance over classical models, and additional tests on public datasets confirm its robustness and generalizability.

articleTitle: Improved Real-Time Path Planning Method for Ground Mobile Robots in Unstructured Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In unstructured road environments, real-time autonomous path planning is crucial for collision-free movement of ground mobile robots. However, there are relatively few path planning algorithms currently available for ground mobile robots in unstructured environments. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved path planning algorithm to meet the planning tasks in unstructured scenarios. This paper utilizes independent one-dimensional time-parameterized polynomials for node expansion, combines optimal control theory to construct a heuristic function, and optimizes trajectories using B-spline curves. Additionally, the Receding Horizon Planning framework algorithm is employed to meet the requirements of real-time path planning. Experimental results of robot path planning demonstrate that the proposed algorithm offers faster planning speed and smoother trajectories, with an increase in travel speed.

articleTitle: ARM-Based Distributed Multi-Signal Acquisition System Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In order to meet the real-time and reliable multi-data interaction between avionics equipment, this paper adopts the “top-down” design method to design a distributed multi-signal acquisition system based on ARM, which connects the avionics equipment through cables, and provides working excitation for the avionics equipment through the analog interfaces, RS422 interfaces, ARINC429 interfaces, and collects data such as output status and output parameters in real time. Avionics equipment provides working excitation and real-time acquisition of data such as output status and output parameters of avionics equipment, and summarizes all kinds of signals to the interface master computer through Ethernet. The high degree of modularization and integration of the system allows incremental modification of the module units, which has good flexibility and strong system scalability.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Event- Triggered Reinforcement Learning Control for Discrete-time MASs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper studies the event-triggered output optimal control for discrete-time multi-agent systems (MASs) with unmeasured system states. A state estimator is initially developed to monitor the agent's states, and subsequently, a new event-triggered reinforcement learning control method is devised using the state observer. To avoid the interdependence of agent control inputs, the hierarchy decomposition method is applied to assign priorities for each agent in the control design. A distributed event-triggered condition is designed for the sensor-to-controller channel of each agent, such that the data transmission among the agents can be greatly reduced. Lastly, stability analysis and numerical simulation are presented to demonstrate availability of the scheme.

articleTitle: An Road Scene Semantic Segmentation Algorithm Based on Modified PIDNet
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Though the state-of-the architectures for semantic segmentation, such as DDRNet, demonstrate impressive accuracy, small target information is easy to lose and the details are overwhelmed by the context is one of the primary challenges faced by the road scene. In this paper, we developed an improved PIDNet model for enhancing the accuracy of segmentation. The method used sampling optimization module (SOM) by assigning higher weights to key features, the information loss of the network during continuous downsampling is reduced. The coordinate aggregation attention module was embedded into the parallel aggregation pyramid pooling module (PAPPM), which improved the modeling ability of boundary information captures location information and channel information at different scales. The polarized self-attention (PSA) was also implemented to boost the ability to capture details and achieve accurate segmentation results. To determine the model's efficacy, we assess its performance using the Cityscapes dataset, revealing a mean intersection over union (MIoU) index of 83.52%. It is also effective in promoting visual analysis and other forms of qualitative analysis.

articleTitle: Interlayer Stability Analysis of Two-Layer Networks with Pinning Impulsive by Step Function Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article mainly investigates the unidirectional interlayer stability of the Two-Layer networks with pinning impulsive control. Firstly, by using multi-span step-function method, the interlayer stability of Two-Layer networks with pinning impulsive control can be analyzed. In addition, the novel pinning impulsive controllers are formulated. Secondly, a comparison system is constructed by using auxiliary system method and impulsive control theory, and several new sufficient criteria are given to ensure the stability. Finally, the correctness of theoretical analysis is proved by experimental cases.

articleTitle: A Multiplayer Perceptron Algorithm Based on Global Electrical Heterogeneity and Cardiodynamicsgram for Non-Invasive Detection of Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a key etiology of myocardial ischemia. Currently, early and non- invasive detection of CMD is lack in clinical practice. We proposed a multiplayer perceptron (MLP) model based on global electrical heterogeneity (GEH)- and cardiodynamicsgram (CDG)-based features for non-invasive detection of CMD. 25 GEH parameters and CDG-based features were derived from vectocardiograms (VCGs) of 82 CMD patients and 107 healthy controls to train the support vector machine (SVM) and multiplayer perceptron (MLP) models. Seventeen features (14 GEH parameters, 3 CDG-based features) were finally selected, and the performance of the two models were compared. The proposed MLP model performs better than SVM and provides accuracy: 0.871, sensitivity: 0.925, specificity: 0.775, F1-score: 0.810, and AUC (area under curve): 0.849 in the testing dataset. The proposed MLP model could distinguish CMD from healthy controls, providing possibilities for a noninvasive, low-cost approach for early detection of CMD.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Adaptive Dynamic Event- Triggered Protocol for Multiagent Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed adaptive dynamic event-based consensus problem for a class of linear multiagent systems (MASs) affected by time-varying multiplicative faults. A distributed adaptive dynamic event-triggered control is designed to realize that asymptotic consensus can be achieved in the presence of actuation faults while excluding the Zeno behavior. A novel adaptive dynamic event-triggering mechanism (ADETM) is introduced to regulate the intermittent communication between neighboring agents. The adaptive techniques are introduced to determine the estimated value of the unknown actuator fault and the coupling weight. The new event-triggering function incorporates internal dynamic variables and adaptive parameters to adjust event-triggering conditions, reducing the frequency of triggering events and conserving communication resources. The nature of the proposed protocol is that it is fully distributed, which means the controller operates without requiring global communication graph information. Local state estimation is utilized in the event-triggered protocol, eliminating the need for continuous communication in control law updates and event detection. Finally, a simulation example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Detection, Tracking and Redetection of Moving Target by UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the research of quadrotor UAV in mobile target detection tracking and redetection, and proposes KCF-Y algorithm and KCF-Ys algorithm. KCF- Y algorithm combines Kernelized Correlation Filters (KCF) algorithm and YOLO algorithm, which solves some limitations of KCF algorithm in target tracking, and improves the accuracy and robustness of the algorithm for moving target tracking. The KCF-Ys algorithm uses the YOLOv8 ONNX model to realize the target center control and improve the real-time tracking of the mobile target. Finally, the superiority of the proposed algorithm and the effectiveness of the UAV tracking system.

articleTitle: Task Pre Allocation of Kill Chain based on Tactical Style Templates
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In response to the problem of slow pre allocation speed of existing kill chain tasks without considering typical air combat scenarios and not effectively combining classic tactical style templates, a tactical style template based on classic air combat scenarios is proposed to accelerate the implementation of task pre allocation modules in the kill chain process. This method obtains typical tactical style templates based on classic combat scenarios and embeds them into algorithms to quickly call them in actual combat scenarios. Then, according to the algorithm, the best matching tactical style template is selected for calling, and combat elements are instantiated based on the actual combat background, including the number of enemy targets, target type, our aircraft type, weapon type, force configuration, task time, task area, etc. The output data allocates actual combat tasks, thereby achieving fast task pre allocation of the kill chain and improving its practical performance.

articleTitle: Distributed Forward-Reflected-Douglas-Rachford Algorithms for Generalized Nash Equilibrium
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the challenge of developing a distributed solution for the Generalized Nash Equilibrium (GNE) in a networked environment. In this scenario, a group of players communicate through a connected network and aim to minimize their respective objective functions while considering the impact of other players' decisions and shared resource constraints. To address this, the paper proposes a new approach that involves reformulating the local optimal solution, introducing the network-Lagrangian, and redefining GNE as a zero-finding problem for a specific operator. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through its application in a Nash-Cournot production game scenario.

articleTitle: Advancements in Power Grid Monitoring: UAV-Enhanced Transformer Neural Networks for Knife-Switch Status Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the advancement of the smart grid, efficient and accurate monitoring of the status of electric power knife switches has become particularly important. Traditional monitoring methods for knife switch status are hampered by high costs, susceptibility to environmental influences, and complex data processing. This study introduces an intelligent monitoring method for electric power knife switch status based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and a transformer neural network model. Utilizing UAVs for image acquisition, coupled with advanced image preprocessing techniques, the efficiency of data collection is enhanced while ensuring the quality of image data. The transformer neural network model introduced, particularly the ReViT model, employs residual attention connections and multi-head self-attention mechanisms, effectively improving the accuracy of knife switch status recognition under complex environmental conditions. To comprehensively evaluate the model's performance, this study developed an integrated assessment metric, SSICS, which considers the state matching rate, weighted consistency ratio, and harmonic stability coefficient, providing a thorough evaluation of the model's performance under various conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior performance in safety, efficiency, cost, robustness, and accuracy, significantly outperforming existing technologies. Future research will focus on enhancing the system's generalization capability and real-time processing capacity, further broadening its application in intelligent grids and automated facility maintenance.

articleTitle: Decentralized Byzantine-Resilient Stochastic Optimization Over Multi-Agent Systems with Arbitrary Communication Delays
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Byzantine failures and communication delays impose great challenges to the decision-making process of multiagent systems (MASs). In this paper, we aim to resolve a category of general finite-sum optimization problems with simultaneous presence of Byzantine agents and arbitrary time-varying communication delays over networks. The number of Byzantine agents and their identities are unknown to reliable agents and the communication delays are not necessarily bounded. To alleviate the negative impact incurred by Byzantine agents and communication delays, both a generalized norm-penalized approximation technique and an age tracker are considered in the development of a decentralized Byzantine-resilient stochastic sub-gradient algorithm, dubbed DeSSO-AD. Theoretical analysis characterizes an explicit sub-linear convergence rate for DeSSO-AD based on a diminishing step-size. The effectiveness and resilience of DeSSO-AD are demonstrated via handling a machine-learning problem under cyber attacks and time-varying communication delays.

articleTitle: A Cluster Scheduling Algorithm for Concurrent Tasks Based on Global Optimization and Differential Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of efficiently scheduling concurrent Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) tasks in the era of big data. It introduces Aetsa (Advanced Efficient Task Scheduling Algorithm), an algorithm that combines global optimization with differential privacy. Aetsa is designed to balance the IO load and real-time CPU usage of tasks while employing differential privacy techniques to safeguard data privacy. Additionally, Aetsa harnesses the Quartz framework to facilitate high-performance task scheduling. Experimental results indicate that Aetsa surpasses traditional strategies in terms of response time and task completion time, particularly in environments with high CPU utilization. Aetsa proves its effectiveness and reliability across various scenarios, offering an innovative solution for concurrent ETL task scheduling and ensuring dual optimization of scheduling efficiency and data privacy.

articleTitle: Workflow Net Based on Colored Petri Net: A Modeling Method for MBSE Modeling Activities
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the study of various methodologies of Model- Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), the modeling of MBSE modeling activities is an important topic. At present, there is a lack of a method to formalize model iteration and evolution while modeling MBSE modeling process. In this paper, a method called Colored Modeling Workflow net (CMWF-net) is proposed, in which MBSE modeling process is represented by workflow net, and model iteration and evolution are described by colored petri net. A model example of the modeling activities based on a MBSE methodology is built by the method to illustrate CMWF-net's expression ability of both MBSE modeling process and model iteration and evolution. Moreover, an engine of modeling workflow based on the MBSE methodology is developed according to the model example. The method introduces a fresh idea to describe MBSE modeling activities and provides an effective way for the study of MBSE methodologies.

articleTitle: A Solid State Pulse Power Supply Design Adopting Active Capacitor Converter for Low Voltage and High Power Pulse Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Based on the structure of active capacitor converter, this paper studies the topology and control strategy of a solid state pulse power supply applied to low repetition pulse frequency low voltage high power pulse load. Adopt the active capacitor converter can provide enough energy when the load is working in the pulse state, reduce the influence of the output power change on the input power, and ensure that the input power works in a constant and smooth output state. Usually when the pulse frequency is low, in order to ensure that the input power is constant, in order to achieve the output voltage is stable and smooth, the output current is rapidly increased rated pulse current value, it is necessary to use a very large capacity of the super capacitor to reduce the instantaneous voltage peak drop when the load state changes, and provide enough energy to complete high-power supply. In this paper, an active capacitor converter structure is used to replace a capacitor with a huge capacity, which greatly reduces the volume and cost of the circuit, and improves the integration of the power supply. In order to ensure that the active capacitor converter can quickly follow the change of load current when output, provide pulse current, and maintain a small enough ripple, work stably in the process of charging and discharging the energy storage capacitor, and limit the voltage within a reasonable set value, the average current control method is adopted, and an energy storage capacitor limiting circuit is added. It can lock the voltage in time after charging the energy storage capacitor to the set maximum voltage, and quickly enter the step-down output state when it is necessary to discharge. Finally, a solid-state power circuit with a peak output of 4800W, a pulse duty cycle of 0.01 and a peak power maintenance time of 300us is designed, and the simulation results are in line with expectations.

Author Keywords: low voltage high power pulse load

articleTitle: A Target Assignment Fusion Algorithm for Distributed Multi-Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper researches a challenging problem of distributed multi-target tracking in a network of sensors having different fields of view. To solve this, we propose a novel target assignment fusion algorithm consisting of local probability hypothesis density filtering and a target assignment fusion process. To fuse target information within different limited fields of view, we first introduce the concept of fusion possibility and calculate it in the manner of a similar weighted geometric average method. After that, this paper constructs an assignment cost matrix through a judgment strategy based on fusion possibility. Essentially, the target assignment algorithm is ably executed to allocate targets between two sensors with limited fields of view, which benefits from the correct-designed cost matrix. Finally, we combine the sequential fusion strategy to achieve a fusion process across the sensor network. Simulation experiments with a challenging scene verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed algorithm. In addition, The proposed algorithm only utilizes local filters' single-scan posterior intensities without a feedback mechanism, ensuring the timelessness to some extent.

articleTitle: An Image Super-Resolution Network Using Multiple Attention Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Single image super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) images. Existing SR algorithms often lose information when dealing with complex textures and details, and the model's feature weighting in different regions is unreasonable, leading to poor reconstruction effects. Recently, networks based on attention mechanisms have shown excellent performance. Attention mechanisms can enhance the model's use of critical input information and reduce the emphasis on non-critical information. In this study, we improve the traditional transformer framework by incorporating channel and spatial attention mechanisms in the deep feature extraction stage to capture the channel and spatial relationships of each feature map, enhancing the model's high-dimensional information extraction capability. We also utilize a pixel attention mechanism to improve the up-sampling module, allowing the model to retain more detail during up-sampling. The validation on benchmark datasets demonstrates that our method outperforms other models.

articleTitle: Event-Based Data-Driven Consensus Control for Multiagent Systems with Unknown Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of achieving tracking consensus control for multi-agent systems (MASs) with unknown dynamics. First, an augmented neighborhood error system model is designed, and the optimal consensus protocol of MASs is converted to the optimal regulation for augmented system with a performance function. A control policy based on event-triggered is proposed to address the optimal regulation of the augmented system. Then, a data-driven control approach is proposed to implement the event-triggered policy, including a critic network and an actor. The actor is utilized to generate control inputs and the critic network estimates the performance value. Through the selection of suitable event-triggered thresholds and learning rates, the local neighborhood error is proved to be uniformly ultimately bounded, effectively preventing the occurrence of Zeno behaviors. Finally, two simulation examples are presented and analyzed to validate the efficacy of the proposed control model.

articleTitle: Online Bandit Convex Optimization with Stochastic Constraints and Delays
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of online convex optimization with stochastic constraints under feedback delays in the bandit setup. We propose a Mirror Virtual Queue algorithm based on the Bregman distance, which replacing the traditional Euclidean distance. Subsequently, we analyze that the algorithm achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\tau T})$</tex> static regret and constraint violation when the loss and constraint functions are smooth convex and the feedback delay is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex>, representing the best-known results to date. Finally, we provide numerical simulations of online job scheduling in delay scenarios, analyzing the impact of feedback delays and validating the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Stability of Time-Scale-Type Nonlinear Systems with Time Delays
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper explores the finite-time stability (FTS) for time-scale-type nonlinear systems (TTNSs) with time delays, where TTNSs serve as an extension of continuous and discrete systems, including systems on homogeneous and non-homogeneous time domains. In the existing results on the stability of TTNSs with time delays, the time-delay moments were usually assumed to be on well-defined time scales. In this paper, without this constraint for the time delays, the finite-time stability problem is investigated for TTNSs with time delays by introducing an extended time-scale-type Lyapunov-Razumikhin method and backward-jump-like operator. Additionally, this paper emphasizes the examination of finite-time contraction stability (FTCoS), which requires the state to remain within a specified boundary of the initial state before reaching the terminal time. We shed new light on the effectiveness of the theoretical results with an example of coordination of time scale-type multi-agent systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Environment Control at Medical Equipment Detection Site
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Since all medical electrical equipment and systems are subject to varying degrees of electromagnetic phenomena in their normal operating environments, it has become a universal consensus in the industry to establish specific electromagnetic compatibility standards for medical electrical equipment and systems. This article summarizes the shielding body hybrid simulation production strategy through the dipole simulation of the perforated double-layer rectangular shielding body in the high-frequency band and the magnetic shielding analysis in the low-frequency band, exploring the impact of shielding effectiveness on the electromagnetic compatibility analysis and electromagnetic effect assessment of medical devices, providing feasibility for the extremely low electromagnetic environment test in the medical device detection environment.

articleTitle: Research on Mission Reliability Analysis Methods for Earth-Moon Space Measurement and Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The reliability study of the Earth-Moon space measurement and control system can ensure the successful completion of the Earth-Moon space measurement and control mission, and the reliability technology study promotes the development of the measurement and control system, and the reliability technology of the measurement and control system has been widely used in the field of scientific research and engineering at the present stage. Therefore, the article firstly combed the domestic and foreign theories and applications on the reliability research of the Earth-Moon space measurement and control system; then summarized the reliability technology methods used by the Earth-Moon space measurement and control system in the process of executing the mission, and focused on the analysis of the application of the reliability optimization technology of the measurement and control system in the Earth-Moon space measurement and control mission; and finally put forward a reliability research plan of Earth-Moon space measurement and control mission and a review of the reliability research program of Earth-Moon space measurement and control mission for the current research work of reliability optimization technology. Finally, the reliability research program of Earth-Moon space measurement and control mission is proposed in the light of the current research on reliability optimization technology, and the significance and development direction of the reliability research of Earth-Moon space measurement and control system are discussed and prospected.

articleTitle: Robust Kalman Filtering Based on Multivariate Geometric Skew Normal Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel robust Kalman filter, referred to as the robust Kalman filter based on multivariate geometric skew normal (MGSN) distribution (RKF-MGSN). The RKF -MGSN effectively tackles the challenge of linear state estimation under heavy-tailed or skewed measurement noise. First, the MGSN distribution is transformed into a hierarchical representation to model the measurement noise. Then, Gaussian, inverse-Wishart (IW), and Beta distributions are determined as the prior distributions for the three parameters of the MGSN distribution. Moreover, the analytical update forms of the posterior distributions for the state vector and noise modeling parameters are derived through the utilization of variational Bayesian (VB) method. Finally, simulations on maneuvering target tracking confirm the performance superiorities of the RKF-MGSN.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Multi-Channel Recognition Network Combining Signal Correlation Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Signal modulation recognition (SMR) is crucial in wireless communication systems. In recent years, various modulation recognition algorithms based on deep learning have emerged. However, the problems of low recognition accuracy and a large number of network parameters have not been well solved. To overcome these challenges, this article presents a lightweight spatiotemporal multi-channel network (MCLDNN) called RAGMCL network by combining the signal correlation feature, attention mechanism module, and random Gaussian noise. The proposed approach introduces a four-channel convolutional network by augmenting the input of the original MCLDNN network with an additional channel. This channel extracts correlation features from IQ signals, enhancing the feature set used for network training. The RAGMCL network is evaluated using four publicly available datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the RAGMCL network achieves higher recognition accuracy while reducing the model parameters by 19.85%, combining the advantages of low number of parameters and high recognition accuracy. The RAGMCL network designed in this thesis holds potential for satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Steady-State Visual Evoked Potential Brain-Computer Interface Performance with Pyramid Squeeze Attention a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the field of human-computer interaction, rapid advancements in brain-computer interface (BCI) technology are catalyzing a new era of barrier-free communication. Particularly, Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) has become a focal point in non-invasive electroencephalogram (EEG) research due to their reliable response under visual stimuli. However, existing SSVEP signal processing techniques often struggle with signal instability, environmental noise, and fluctuations in physiological and psychological states of users, significantly hindering accurate information extraction and application. Interactions among channels in multi-channel EEG analysis are crucial for the extraction and recognition of signal features; yet, traditional methods often fail in adequately handling these complex interactions and do not effectively utilize multi-scale information, leading to a loss of critical feature information and diminished recognition performance. Addressing these limitations in capturing subtle and crucial time-varying features, which are essential for distinguishing various SSVEP tasks, this study introduces a novel deep learning framework-EEGNetPSA. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset of 12 targets demonstrated that EEGN etPSAs-2 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{EEGNetPSA}_{2-8}$</tex> achieved recognition accuracies of 95.30% and 92.88% respectively within I-second time window, significantly surpassing the basic models EEGNets-2 at 86.980/0 and EEGNeh-s at 84.34%. These findings highlight the substantial potential of combining deep learning with multi-scale attention mechanisms.

articleTitle: Research and Testing of Clock Synchronization for 5G-TSN Industrial Control Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: With the development of industry 4.0, real-time services in factories have higher deterministic requirements for delay, jitter, bandwidth, etc. How to realize high-precision clock synchronization of industrial control networks and ensure deterministic services is an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, we design a high-precision clock synchronization network scheme based on 5G TSN, which combines 5G, TSN, PTP, GPS and other technologies to achieve end to end high-precision clock synchronization in 5G systems. Finally, we built a real network environment for testing. After using a clock source to transmit accurate clock signals, the 5G-TSN dedicated network can provide high-precision clock synchronization and ensure deterministic transmission.

articleTitle: Novel Approach to Hydraulic Support Pressure Prediction by EMD-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Hydraulic support pillar pressure prediction has been a pivotal basis for decision-making during the mining process. It has been one of the fundamental pieces of information for ensuring the stability of the surrounding rock. However, the pressure of hydraulic support pillars follows specific patterns; it cannot be predicted using simple mathematical models. Additionally, during the mining process, issues such as the support attaching and detaching the roof, roof fragmentation, and sensor detection errors introduce a significant amount of random perturbance, turning the pressure data into a non-stationary time series. Non-stationarity significantly complicates the pressure prediction. Based on the Transformer model, this paper proposes an EMD-Transformer model. Empirical mode decomposition aims to decompose non-linear non-stationary data pressure data into intrinsic mode functions, and the transformer model establishes detailed correlations of all components and projects predicted components. The aggregate sum of predicted components gives pressure prediction. Comparative experiments on a real coal mine support pillar dataset showed that the EMD-Transformer model proposed in this paper achieved notably improved performance on all prediction lengths compared to LSTM and vanilla Transformer model.

articleTitle: $H_{\infty}$ Control for Continuous-time Singular System with Cyber-attacks and Hybrid-triggered Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This study delves into hybrid-triggered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> con-trol for continuous-time singular systems exposed to random cyber-attacks. Hybrid-triggered communication mechanism is employed to mitigate the effects of cyber-attacks. Furthermore, a new model of switching singular systems is developed, considering the random nature of cyber-attacks and the integration of Hybrid-triggered mechanism. A Lyapunov-based functional is utilized to validate the stability of the singular system, ensuring it is impulse-free, regular, and exhibits asymptotic stability. The determination of optimal controller gains is achieved through the resolution of a series of linear matrix inequalities. An illustrative numerical example is presented to showcase the effectiveness of the strategy developed.

articleTitle: H∞ Consensus in Linear Multi-Agent Systems with Event-Driven Approaches on Directed Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Given the asymmetry inherent in system matrices due to directed communication topologies, a novel exponentially decaying event-driven control approach is raised to ensure robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus among linear Multi-Agent Systems (MASs), even in the presence of external disturbances within directed topologies. By leveraging controlled output and generalized algebraic connectivity within directed graphs, we transform the consensus challenge into an event-driven stabilization within the linear closed-loop system, effectively mitigating disturbances. We introduce dynamic variables alongside the relative state of neighboring agents at event intervals to formulate a dynamic event-driven control approach. The approach is complemented by the derivation of Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) sufficient conditions, rigorously establishing the attainment of robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> consensus. Subsequently, we streamline LMIs, significantly reducing computational overhead. The parameters governing the control approach are then fine-tuned through the solution of these decoupled LMIs. To validate our propositions, we conduct simulations, affirming the efficacy of our approach.

articleTitle: Exploring the Application and Effectiveness of Current Large Models in Power Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In recent years, a large number of Large Models (LMs) has emerged, showcasing immense potential and value across various domains. These LMs fall into three primary categories: Large Language Models (LLMs), Large Visual Models (LVMs), and large Vision-Language Models (VLMs). These models represent advanced artificial intelligence systems trained on vast datasets, equipped with a multitude of parameters to comprehend and generate outputs resembling accurate and human-like responses. LLMs are primarily designed for text processing and generation, while LVMs are tailored to handle visual data, such as images and videos. VLMs integrate both visual and textual inputs to comprehend and generate content based on the interaction betwen images and text. Their ability enables their application in various fields, such as image classification, object detection, instance segmentation and more. In spite of their achievements in these areas, the effectiveness of LMs on less common objects within specialized domains like power inspection, such as insulator, respirator, nameplate and nests, remains largely unexplored. This paper seeks to investigate the efficacy of current LMs in the realm of power inspection. Initially, we propose a power inspection dataset comprising 12,104 images spanning 6 distinct object categories. Subsequently, we delve into the application of LMs in power inspection. Finally, we evaluate the performance of existing LMs on image classification, object detection and instance segmentation in the field of power inspection using the proposed dataset.

articleTitle: Research on Resource Optimization of Distributed Photovoltaic Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This article conducts a thorough examination of the resource optimization challenge faced by energy storage and power generation systems in photovoltaic power stations. In the introductory section, it underscores the criticality of energy management systems in photovoltaic plants and examines the pivotal role played by photovoltaic energy storage and generation systems in contemporary energy supply. Following this, the article proposes a comprehensive resource optimization strategy tailored for photovoltaic energy storage and generation systems, constructing a detailed optimization model that encapsulates both objective functions and constraint conditions. Furthermore, it delves into the workings of photovoltaic power generation components and energy storage batteries within distributed power sources. In the subsequent system calculation and analysis section, the article provides an overview of the model's data, parameters, and optimization methods, outlining the frameworks used. It then presents simulation results, coupled with an in-depth analysis. Ultimately, these studies aim to offer both theoretical underpinnings and practical insights, facilitating the efficient management and cost-effective operation of photovoltaic power plants.

Author Keywords: Energy storage and power generation system

articleTitle: Customised Routing Algorithms Based on Network Slicing and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Traditional routing algorithms cannot better meet user demands in a service-centric way, and there is a possibility of bandwidth idling or network congestion because it does not take into account making full use of all link bandwidths of the network, which leads to a waste of network resources. In this paper, a Dijkstra algorithm based on greedy algorithm optimisation is proposed in combination with deep learning methods to classify and optimise the weights of link information through deep learning models to achieve the optimal allocation of global resources. Comparing other routing algorithms through simulation experiments, the experimental results show that the custom routing mechanism algorithm designed in this paper reduces the average delay by 9.22%, reduces the average bandwidth occupancy by 25.02%, and improves the resource utilisation rate, which significantly optimises the network resource allocation compared to the traditional single network architecture.

articleTitle: Design of Anti-Jamming Waveforms for Cognitive Radar Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the face of various complex interferences encountered by radar systems in modern electronic warfare, the performance of radar is greatly affected. Therefore, intelligent and adaptive radar anti-jamming waveform design methods have become crucial. This paper proposes a training algorithm for anti-jamming strategies under multiple types of interference based on deep reinforcement learning. Considering that radar jamming resistance possesses Markovian properties, meaning that the current anti-jamming strategy of the radar is only related to the current momentary state and independent of previous states, a reinforcement learning algorithm is introduced to construct the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework. Due to the complex and continuous nature of the state-action space, neural networks are introduced. By quantifying anti-jamming decisions through the construction of state sets, action sets, and reward functions, and modeling the anti-jamming process as a Markov decision process, we propose a radar anti-multiple interference algorithm based on the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm, called RAMI-SAC, to optimize strategies. Specifically, considering the synchronization between radar signals and interference signals, we utilize the characteristics of radar signals and interference signals from the previous time step to construct the state space. We use the RAMI-SAC algorithm to generate anti-jamming strategies, including the masking pulse width, frequency band, and signal power of the current radar sequence. Through multiple sets of simulations, the convergence of the algorithm is demonstrated, resulting in anti-jamming strategies that can withstand attacks from multiple types of interference, maintaining a certain level of detection capability even in the presence of multiple types of interference.

articleTitle: BIER-MNet: A BIER-Based Multicast Member Management Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: This paper proposes a BIER-based multicast member management mechanism (BIER-MNet) aimed at addressing performance bottlenecks of traditional multicast member management protocols in BIER multicast. By introducing a multicast member mapping management mechanism, it achieves finegrained multicast member management, reduces router signaling overhead, and enhances the scalability of multicast member management. The designed BIER-MNet architecture extends the functions of the original BIER multicast architecture, providing an overall architecture that includes the multicast management layer, BIER multicast layer, and unicast routing layer, optimizing the join and leave processes of multicast members. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional PIM-SM protocol, BIER-MNet demonstrates better stability and efficiency in multicast member join latency under different network link delays, verifying the effectiveness and feasibility of this mechanism.

articleTitle: Time-Optimal Trajectory Planning for Robotic Arm Based on Improved Harris Hawk Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low efficiency and poor stability of the robotic arm, a time-optimal trajectory planning algorithm for the robotic arm based on the improved Harris Hawk optimization algorithm (HHO) is proposed. The algorithm optimizes the balance between the ability of global development and local exploration of the algorithm and accelerates the convergence speed by changing the form of the escape energy factor of the Harris Hawk optimization algorithm and introducing the positive cosine algorithm to the exploration stage. Taking the UR5 robotic arm as a simulation model, the 3-5-3 segmented polynomial interpolates the joint space trajectory and optimizes the running time of the robotic arm using the improved HHO algorithm. Through simulation analysis, the improved HHO algorithm has a significant improvement in both convergence time and global exploration capability. The running time of the robotic arm is reduced by 64.43% compared to the fixed-time press.

articleTitle: Surgical Action Triplet Recognition by Using A Multi-Task Prior-Reinforced and Cross-Sample Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Surgical action recognition is an important branch of computer-assisted surgery, which aims to provide real-time monitoring and decision support for clinical surgery. However, most of the existing algorithms only focus on a single aspect of the surgical process and cannot fully describe the surgical process. Following previous work, we modeled surgical action as a triplet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$<$</tex> instrument, verb, target <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> to represent fine-grained information in surgical scenes. In this paper, we propose a Multi-task Prior-reinforced and Cross-sample Network (MPCNet) to model triplet recognition. We use a multi-task learning paradigm to allow component and triplet recognition to benefit from each other. Moreover, we design a Prior Reinforcement Module (PRM) that enhances the raw triplet features with the component features and learns the associations between components. Finally, we propose an external attention-based Transformer that learns cross-sample semantic relationships through shared keys and values. Our extensive experiments on the CholecT50 dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art results.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Event-Triggered Resilient Control for Vehicular Platooning Systems Under False Data Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The article explores the event-triggered resilient model-free adaptive platooning security control (MFAPC) problem for vehicular platooning systems (VPSs) with asymmetric constraints and false data injection attacks (FDI). Firstly, via the system transformation, an unconstrained function expression of the controlled system is developed to overcome the challenge caused by asymmetric constraints of position and velocity. Secondly, based on transformed functions, an equivalent linear model can be acquired from the nonlinear VPSs by virtue of the dynamic linearization approach. Thirdly, taking the excellent performance of the function approximation into account, the radial basis neural network is introduced to approximate the false data, which significantly reduces the negative effects of attacks. Moreover, an event-triggered mechanism is introduced to save network resources effectively. For the VPSs subjected to FDI attacks, a new resilient ET-MFAPSC scheme is proposed for safe vehicle driving. In conclusion, the effectiveness of the designed algorithm can be demonstrated through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis and Optimal Control of SIWCR Rumor Propagation Model with Rumor Countering and Whistleblowing Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: The spread of rumours on social networks hinders economic development and disrupts the normal order of society. This paper proposes a whistleblowing mechanism, which is a user monitoring mechanism that allows netizens to report communicators in order to promote a healthy order in cyberspace, and constructs a novel susceptible-infective-whistleblowing-countering-recovered (SIWCR) rumor propagation model in combination with a countering mechanism. The dynamical equation of rumor propagation under a homogeneous network structure is initially described by the mean field theory. Then, the existence of equilibrium points is analysed, and the basic reproduction number of the model calculated by the next generation matrix method. The Routh-Hurwitz criterion is employed to analyze the local asymptotic stability of equilibrium points, and the global asymptotic stability of equilibrium points is examined using LaSalle's invariance principle. An optimal control strategy is proposed by selecting the intensity of the gag measure as the control variable. Simulation results show that rumor countering, whistleblowing mechanism and gag strategy have important effects on rumor outbreak scale. The model parameters are fine-tuned using the least squares method, leveraging on a real data set obtained from Twitter. The resulting R-squared value of the model is 0.9917.

articleTitle: Schematic Comparison Method Based on Tree Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: In the process of multiple revisions and iterations of integrated circuit designs, different versions of schematics are inevitably generated. The designers will need to compare the differences between different versions to analyze the reasons for different simulation results, so that they can improve the design later. Comparing the differences between schematic versions is particularly important. The time cost of existing tools is high or the comparison results are not accurate enough. We propose a schematic version comparison method based on a tree structure. By comparing the tree structures of two top-level units, the reference unit differences are obtained, and then the corresponding units in the tree structure are compared in turn. First, the device differences are obtained, and a multi-branch tree encoding data structure of the wire net and its connected devices is established. The binary codes of the node devices are XOR to obtain the wire net differences, thereby obtaining the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{final}$</tex> difference results and giving the schematic difference comparison results on the test circuit.

articleTitle: SR-Mamba: Data-Driven EV Charging Load-Altering Attack Detection and Localization Using Selective State based Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Driven by the imperative to reduce emissions from transportation, Electric Vehicles (EVs) are proliferating rapidly. However, the widespread adoption of EV charging facilities poses a potential threat to the stability of the grid. Manipulating the demand for charging facilities can disrupt the supply/demand balance of the grid, potentially leading to blackouts. Moreover, current load alternation attack detection relies on static linearized grid modeling, which struggles to accurately represent the dynamic nature of the grid, thus making it difficult to detect such attacks effectively. In this paper, we propose a data-driven model using a State Space Model (Mamba-based structure) to capture temporal correlation among buses. We introduce spectral domain representation to enhance detection and utilize hidden grid representations for identifying load alternative attacks and their location.

articleTitle: SERGCN: Graph Convolutional Neural Networks with Skip-Edge Residual Connection for Node Classification Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have been widely used for node categorization, graph embedding, and link prediction, etc. Two main challenges regarding developing deep GCNs for node classifying are overfitting and oversmoothing. The main causes of oversmoothing are overfitting and training barriers, which is directly caused by gradient disappearance. To resolve this issue, we propose the Skip-Edge Residual Graph Con-volution Network (SERGCN), which extracts a certain proportion of edge information at each layer in the novel way and integrates the initial information and the information of the previous layer in the convolution process, so as to prevent and slow down the gradient disappearance and further oversmoothing. Based on extensive experiments and real-world data sets used in several benchmarks, our proposed solution incorporates the benefits of a deep architecture while equaling or even exceeding the accuracy of existing approaches.

articleTitle: Passenger Waiting Time Prediction Based on Density Spatiotemporal Clustering and Time Series Feature Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: Accurate passenger waiting time prediction addresses the taxi supply-demand imbalance in Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). To capture the dependencies of passenger waiting time on urban taxi distribution, we propose a Density Spatiotemporal Clustering and Time Series Feature Processing (DSC-TSFP) method that discovers potential feature relationships of taxi GPS trajectory data. Specifically, a Multilevel Spatiotemporal Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (MST-DBSCAN) is proposed to cluster taxi GPS trajectory data to obtain waiting time series with spatiotemporal correlations. Furthermore, a time series processing module based on the Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise Normalization (CEEMDANN) is designed to enhance prediction accuracy by handling non-stationarity and numerical discrepancy, which solves the residual white noise problem in Intrinsic Modal Functions (IMFs) of EEMD and CEEMD. Next, a waiting time prediction module oriented to a Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory Network (ConvLSTM) is incorporated to compensate for the defects of spatially localized dependencies that LSTM cannot capture. Finally, a CEEMDANN-ConvLSTM model is constructed to predict the passenger waiting time by combining the time series processing and waiting time prediction module. Based on real-world taxi GPS trajectory data, experimental results demonstrate that DSC-TSFP outperforms comparable methods regarding prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles with Barrier Adaptive Tracking Control and Unwinding-Free Guarantees
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: For autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), this research proposes a barrier adaptive unwinding-free tracking control method that can handle model uncertainty, external disturbances and unwinding problem. Initially, the AUV's kinematic model is specified using unit quaternions, allowing for a thorough definition of both its translational and rotational movements. To ensure that the quaternion-based attitude is represented uniquely, an anti-unwinding control system is designed that employs a hyperbolic tangent function-based switching surface and a dynamic parameter matrix. In addition, in order to ensure that system states converge inside a preset range of zero, we provide an adaptive control method based on barrier functions. Finally, extensive theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate the advantages of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Research on an Attack Detection Technology Based on Provenance Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Electronic Engineering and Informatics (EEI)
abstract: As a critical production factor, power data needs to flow, reorganize and be utilized across various aspects of the electric power business. Power data security has become a core capability requirement for the security system of power grid enterprises. Aiming at the problem of insufficient accuracy and efficiency in power grid data security threat detection, this paper proposes a data security attack detection method based on deep learning. Firstly, the system log data is effectively collected and the log information is effectively parsed through pre-processing; then the parsed log data is used to construct the provenance graph; graph embedding based on the hierarchical attention mechanism is introduced to represent the characteristics of the provenance graph; and finally the attack detection model is used to effectively perform Data security attack detection. Experimental results show that the performance of this attack detection method is significantly better than other mainstream methods.
